text: The Professor expressed admiration for Craig's resourcefulness and ability to handle natural difficulties during expeditions. Quest noted that Craig appears to be a coward but exhibits remarkable cunning in criminal activities. Lord Ashleigh introduced his head-keeper, Middleton, who was present during the chase. Middleton apologized for firing his gun, which he did out of frustration with poachers affecting his pheasants. The Professor informed Middleton that the escaped man is a serious criminal. Middleton expressed confidence that the escaped man would not get far due to the wild nature of the country. Middleton mentioned he has a personal plan to catch the escaped man without revealing details.

von Knigenstein has been at a location alone for more than an hour. The Prince expressed concern about Mr. Sabin's activities. Felix reported that von Knigenstein left town half an hour ago. Mr. Sabin is believed to have gone to Norfolk to play golf. Felix confirmed that Labanoff saw Mr. Sabin leave King's Cross station. The Prince planned to invite von Knigenstein to dinner next week. Felix delivered the invitation to von Knigenstein at the German Embassy.

Major Jones expressed that there was a mistake regarding a warrant. Peter Ruff stated that Sir Richard's patience had been exhausted by Major Jones's demands. Major Jones claimed he believed Sir Richard was willing to help him. Peter Ruff indicated that Sir Richard had sought his advice on different measures. Major Jones offered Peter Ruff a large sum of money in exchange for his freedom. Peter Ruff refused Major Jones's offer, stating that money would not buy his liberty. Peter Ruff implied that Major Jones was involved in a serious crime related to a murder.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald disappeared through the window of Mr. Barnes' dining room. A police inspector arrived at Mr. Barnes' home shortly after Fitzgerald's disappearance. Mrs. Barnes and Maud reacted with screams upon the inspector's arrival. Mr. Barnes was shocked and speechless due to the situation. Fitzgerald visited a girl named Miss Emerson at a block of flats after leaving Mr. Barnes' home. Miss Emerson expressed delight upon Fitzgerald's arrival and invited him inside. Fitzgerald informed Miss Emerson that his engagement with Messrs. Howell & Wilson was over.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The young American left Von Hern on his doorstep, where he was only half conscious. Von Hern confronted the young American and demanded the return of his property. A struggle ensued between Paul Jermyn and Von Hern, resulting in gunfire. Peter Ruff intervened and prevented a woman from accessing stolen property. Peter Ruff escaped from the scene while being pursued by Von Hern. Peter Ruff arrived at the Duchess of Montford's ball, appearing injured. Lady Mary expressed concern for Peter Ruff's injury, which he downplayed as a graze.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest offered his cup of bouillon to Mrs. Foston Rowe. Mrs. Foston Rowe became ill after sipping the bouillon. The Doctor determined that Mrs. Foston Rowe was dead. Quest requested to examine the cup of bouillon for any poison. The bouillon was served from the same cauldron to all diners. Laura expressed anxiety about the recent death and its connection to a criminal. The Professor left to retrieve a notebook after having an idea.

Mr. Sabin expressed a change in his feelings towards Russia due to its alliance with the French Republic. Mr. Sabin stated that he has no personal gain in Russia's development and prefers to aid England. Felix questioned Mr. Sabin about the implications of his success at Teheran on covenants with France. Mr. Sabin indicated that he is no longer young and lacks the heart for new adventures. Felix accepted defeat in his mission to persuade Mr. Sabin. Mr. Sabin agreed to deliver a letter addressed to Mrs. J. B. Peterson in Lenox, Massachusetts. Mr. Sabin was traveling on the _Calipha_, a small boat sailing to Boston with only seven passengers.

Peter Ruff observed a man named John Dory at a nearby table. Two men and Peter Ruff witnessed an unusual flying object descending from a shed in the valley. The flying object resembled a combination of a torpedo with wings and a prehistoric insect. The flying object traveled towards them at high speed and performed aerial maneuvers. The distance to Barnham Church was confirmed to be sixteen miles from their location. The flying object completed a round trip of thirty-two miles in less than half an hour. The youth expressed a desire to sell his invention for fifty thousand pounds.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Professor has a garden that is described as a jungle. The Professor has a man-servant named Craig. The Professor received a phone call from the curator of the museum. The Professor's anthropoid ape skeleton has been reported stolen. The Professor instructed Craig to contact Mr. Sanford Quest. The Professor arrived at the museum and met with the curator. The curator showed the Professor an empty wooden box that contained the skeleton.

The Professor is not looking for visitors. Quest and Lenora are in a wilderness area with overgrown paths and dense vegetation. They hear a strange sound that seems to be a human-like cry. Quest and Lenora find a small hut made of sticks and bamboos. The hut is locked, and they hear scuffling sounds from inside. Quest sees a creature with human features and a menacing expression inside the hut. Quest uses a device to unlock the door and confronts the creature, which resembles both a man and a monkey.

The Honorable Maurice found an envelope in his breast pocket that was lighter than expected. Inside the envelope, there was only half a newspaper. Peter Ruff inquired about the envelope and confirmed it was the same type used by Maurice. Maurice stated that his servant was off duty when the packet was changed. The contents of the packet were an official reply to a secret communication from Russia regarding a matter in the Balkans. Peter Ruff suspected Count von Hern, whom he identified as an Austrian spy. Lady Mary and Peter Ruff entered the ballroom to locate Count von Hern.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Jean Lemaitre is currently hiding in the back room of a cafe in Soho. The district around the cafe is monitored by spies. Peter Ruff plans to help Jean Lemaitre escape to Putney. A motor car is ready at a garage in Putney for Jean's escape. There is a small steamer waiting near Southampton for Jean after he reaches the coast. The cafe where Jean is hiding is called the Hotel de Flandres. Peter Ruff will present himself as a doctor to gain access to Jean Lemaitre.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Inspector French is from headquarters. A man under a tarpaulin was wearing Craig's clothes but had a different face. The _Durham_ was no longer anchored and was moving seawards. Lenora expressed a lack of sympathy for Red Gallagher, describing him as brutish. Quest received a cablegram from Scotland Yard about a stowaway matching Craig's description. Lenora has an aunt in London who would like her to visit. Quest planned to sail on the _Lusitania_ and instructed Lenora to send a cable to Scotland Yard.

Densham finds a girl beautiful and expresses a desire to find out where she lives. Harcutt suggests that it is too obvious for both of them to follow the girl. Densham agrees to inform Harcutt about his findings the next day. Wolfenden is surprised to find Miss Merton asleep in his study. Miss Merton has tear stains on her face and reveals that she has been turned away from Deringham. Miss Merton claims that Lady Deringham's actions are an excuse to get rid of her because of Wolfenden. Miss Merton expresses a desire to leave after her conversation with Wolfenden.

Peter is introduced as the Baron de Grost. Peter has a letter of introduction from Mr. Edwardes. Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge is a financier. Peter seeks a loan of one to one and a half million pounds. Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge has just committed to a large financial transaction. Peter's wife is named Violet Brown. Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge's wife is referred to as Mrs. Heseltine-Wrigge.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The character Masters appears to be intoxicated and has a thick, raspy voice. Masters expresses a desire to leave the gathering but is restrained by his host, Sir Richard. Sir Richard, who is described as a tall, well-dressed man around fifty years old, is a baronet with financial troubles. Sir Richard reveals that he owes twenty-six thousand pounds and cannot raise the funds. Lord Merries, an Earl, is described as financially unsound and has a debt of eleven thousand two hundred pounds to Masters. Colonel Dickinson is present at the gathering and echoes the sentiment of financial hardship. The group is attempting to discuss business matters with Masters before he leaves.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Richard mixed a drink for Peter Ruff and acknowledged his cleverness and the five hundred guineas he earned. Peter Ruff requested a letter to Richard's tailors. Peter Ruff's secretary, Miss Brown, expressed concern about having too little work. Peter Ruff stated he did not want to engage in certain types of cases. Miss Brown suggested that Peter Ruff was waiting for a case involving a personal enemy. Peter Ruff mentioned their new neighbor, Vincent Cawdor, who is a commission agent. Miss Brown described Vincent Cawdor as a vulgar, offensive person.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Ashleigh and the Professor were informed by the butler that Middleton, the head-keeper, was downstairs. Middleton, the gamekeeper, captured Craig, who appeared in a state of misery with torn and muddy clothes. Middleton used a poachers' pit to trap Craig, who had attempted to escape through the woods. The police were telephoned by the servants at Mr. Ashleigh's request. Quest wanted to confront Craig with the result of his crime, believing it would elicit a response. Craig reacted violently upon seeing the dead man, exclaiming that it was his work before collapsing. The Professor led Quest and Middleton to a subterranean hiding place to secure Craig until the police arrived.

A plain-clothes man and a group arrived at their destination as a storm broke. The Professor met the group in the hall and invited them to the library. The Professor believed that Craig was in the house and would keep his appointment. French reported that Craig had been living quietly with his niece without attempting to conceal himself. A girl was heard calling from outside, prompting the group to leave the library. The plain-clothes man was holding Craig and the girl, who was sobbing, when the group arrived. A sudden blaze of blue light filled the room, resulting in the destruction of the oak table and chairs.

Felix does not know the young lady beyond the fact that she is with Lord Wolfenden for the time being. Wolfenden expresses disinterest in Felix's warnings about the young lady. Wolfenden's servant, Selby, informs him that a young lady visited and is waiting in his study. Wolfenden is surprised and angry to learn about the young lady's presence in his study. Selby believes the young lady is a lady and suggests there may be a mistake. Wolfenden instructs Selby to wait until he rings for him. A brougham carrying Mr. Sabin and a companion is followed by Harcutt's cab and Densham's hansom.

A programme has been arranged for the Metropolitan Opera House this year. Ella is advised to sail on Saturday by Mauretania. Lord Ashleigh is the Chairman of the County Magistrates and President of the local Unionist Association. Ella has decided to leave for New York on Saturday. Lord Ashleigh will send Macdougal with Ella as a courier and general attendant. Ella will take her own maid, Lenora, with her to New York. Lady Ashleigh and Lord Ashleigh will not be able to accompany Ella during the first few months of her stay.

The _Calipha_ was almost at a standstill, awaiting the doctor's brig. Mrs. Watson was sitting heavily veiled apart and alone on deck. A revolver shot was heard, followed by two splashes in the water. A small, recently-discharged revolver and a man's white linen cap belonging to Mr. Sabin were found on the deck. Mr. Watson was seen swimming away from the steamer, alone. Mrs. Watson fainted upon hearing murmurs about the situation. Mr. J. B. Watson, of New York, was reported to have sunk and did not resurface.

The Countess of Deringham was sitting alone in her smaller drawing-room. She watched a pile of grey ashes that remained from a sealed packet she had placed in the fire. Lady Deringham felt a sense of freedom as the ashes disintegrated. Mr. Sabin arrived at Lady Deringham's residence at precisely four o'clock. Mr. Sabin appeared old and tired when he greeted Lady Deringham. Lady Deringham mentioned burning her letters and reminisced about the past. Mr. Sabin expressed his belief that it is the man who suffers as they age.

Mr. Watson recognized that his companion, Mr. Sabin, was in earnest. Mr. Watson followed Mr. Sabin into his cabin after witnessing a revolver being thrown into the water. Mr. Sabin indicated that Mr. Watson's refusal to accept his proposals was evident. Mr. Watson expressed that he was under surveillance from a German man-of-war. Mr. Sabin offered Mr. Watson a chance to live in America without returning to Europe. Mr. Watson revealed that he was one of the Doomschen. Mr. Sabin acknowledged that Mr. Watson's affiliation with the Doomschen complicated matters.

Wolfenden expressed dissatisfaction with a young lady's response regarding an alliance. Mr. Sabin's appearance influenced the discussion about the young lady's response. Wolfenden stated that Mr. Sabin's refusal was due to his niece being already betrothed. Harcutt believed that Mr. Sabin was involved in important negotiations rather than playing golf. Wolfenden and Harcutt discussed the significance of Mr. Sabin and the young lady's social status. Wolfenden noted that Mr. Sabin showed no interest in the locality or its residents during their conversation. Wolfenden mentioned that Mr. Sabin was particularly interested in an incident that occurred at Deringham Hall.

John Dory expressed feelings of undeserving bad luck and carelessness. Peter Ruff visited John Dory to offer assistance in reinstating his reputation. Peter Ruff informed John Dory that he would recover the Clenarvon diamonds and receive a reward of a thousand pounds. A motor-car left Clenarvon Court with the valet of the Marquis de Sogrange as the sole passenger. Peter Ruff and John Dory flagged down the motor-car and requested a lift to the station. Peter Ruff and John Dory restrained the valet and ordered the chauffeur to return to Clenarvon Court. Upon arrival at Clenarvon Court, Peter Ruff instructed Lord Clenarvon to open a hatbox containing the Clenarvon diamonds.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The novel 'At the Foot of the Rainbow' is set in Central Indiana and focuses on themes of friendship and self-sacrificing love. 'Lavender and Old Lace' is a story about love among young people on a newspaper staff in a quaint corner of New England. 'A Spinner in the Sun' features a veiled lady living in solitude and includes elements of mystery and romance. 'The Master's Violin' tells the story of a young man learning about life and love through his relationship with a girl and his music teacher. 'Within the Law' by Bayard Veiller & Marvin Dana is a novelization of a successful play about a woman's revenge against her employer. 'What Happened to Mary' by Robert Carlton Brown narrates the story of a country girl facing temptations in New York. 'The Return of Peter Grimm' by David Belasco is a novelization of a popular play featuring the character Old Peter Grimm.

Bernadine observed a man and a woman with unusual appearances at the Savoy Restaurant in London. The man was tall, thin, and wore fashionable clothes, but appeared unaccustomed to them. The woman was described as fair, thick-set, and adorned with a large amount of jewelry. Lady Maxwell expressed interest in the couple, particularly the woman's jewelry. Bernadine reflected on the man's identity, noting that he was once a prominent figure in Europe. Bernadine felt a mix of fear and curiosity regarding the man's secrets. Lady Maxwell speculated that the couple might be from an Eastern country.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Two bodies were found in a room, one being a valet and the other a Salvation Army girl. Inspector French and Quest arrived at the scene at five minutes past twelve. Quest observed that the valet was obviously dead and covered the head with a handkerchief. French noted that the valet was killed by a blow from behind with a heavy paper-weight. Quest noticed two blue marks on the girl's throat, suggesting she had been strangled. Quest's clothing was disheveled, with a torn tie and trousers, and he was covered in dust. Inspector French questioned Quest about his whereabouts at eleven-fifteen, to which Quest replied he was on tower Number 10 of the New York Central.

Peter Ruff produced a lady's ring with a single opal from his waistcoat pocket. Major Jones handed around a magnificent stone ring for examination. Miss Levey remarked that it is bad luck to give the ring to anyone not born in October. Peter Ruff stated he had a warrant for Major Jones's arrest. Peter Ruff identified himself as a detective. The charge against Major Jones is blackmail, with information lodged by Sir Richard Dyson. Major Jones displayed signs of fear and relief during the conversation.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest suggested going to a café for supper and music to forget recent events. Lenora and Laura agreed to Quest's suggestion, and the Professor also supported it. Quest received a dispatch from French at the Samaritan Hospital in Allguez regarding an incident. The dispatch indicated that Craig was injured in a wreck but had recovered consciousness. Laura expressed excitement about the news and felt guilty for not knowing about Craig's condition. They decided to take the southern route to New York to visit French in the hospital. French recalled being unconscious during the wreck and remembered seeing someone who resembled Craig.

The wedding featured a significant police presence due to the bride's previous engagement to a burglar. The bridegroom, Dory, was a young officer well regarded at Scotland Yard. The bride, Maud, entered the church on her father's arm. During the wedding ceremony, a witness named Spencer Fitzgerald had already signed the register. A diamond cross was given to the bride by a little old gentleman, which caused a negative reaction from the bridegroom. A separate luncheon took place in Curzon Street, characterized by excessive drinking and a lack of food. The main guest at the luncheon was described as short, thick-set, and red-faced.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Admiral and Wolfenden entered a dark room after hearing a sudden cessation of sounds. Wolfenden observed a dark figure near a lamp before it went out. The Admiral fired his revolver but there was no indication that the figure was hit. The room was silent except for a faint breeze causing rustling of papers and curtains. Wolfenden sensed a woman's presence and heard her hurried breathing. Wolfenden touched a woman's arm without her crying out, despite her rapid breathing. Wolfenden planned to strike a light while the Admiral believed the figure was still hiding.

Lady Deringham's husband is a great invalid and has not been the same since an incident in the Solent. Lady Deringham expresses concern about her husband's mental state and the value of his work. Mr. Sabin is seeking information about structural defects in new battleships. There have been attempts by strangers to access Lady Deringham's husband's research papers. A stranger recently gained access to the Admiral's library with a forged letter of introduction. Lady Deringham's son has shown interest in her husband's work and has been studying it without her knowledge. Lady Deringham's husband keeps a revolver by his side while working and is guarded by a keeper.

Guillot is a feared criminal in Europe who has never been caught. John Dory seeks assistance from Peter to remove Guillot from the country. Guillot is currently staying in a second-floor flat at Crayshaw Mansions, Shaftesbury Avenue, under the name Monsieur Guillot. Peter agrees to look into the matter regarding Guillot. Peter visits Guillot at his flat the same afternoon. Guillot expresses anger at Peter's request for him to leave the city. Guillot refuses to comply with Peter's demand to leave within twenty-four hours.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The character referred to as 'M' declined to reveal her identity but made an appointment to visit Mr. Ruff at his office. Peter Ruff wore a new suit and was nervous on the morning of the appointment. Miss Brown arrived late and ignored Mr. Ruff's greeting while sitting with her back turned. Maud, the expected visitor, entered the room with studied embarrassment and extended her hand to Peter Ruff. Maud and Peter Ruff discussed her engagement to Mr. Fitzgerald, who was a friend of Peter Ruff. Peter Ruff expressed that he could not disclose Mr. Fitzgerald's whereabouts without his permission. Maud displayed signs of confusion when questioned about her marital status.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Lord Ashleigh accuses Lenora of being implicated in the crime. Sanford Quest decides that Lenora is not implicated in the crime. Ian Macdougal is given a life sentence for the murder of Lord Ashleigh's daughter. Sanford Quest and Lenora wait for an automobile outside the Courthouse. Lenora expresses relief that Macdougal will not cross her path again. Lord Ashleigh expresses disconcertion at the sight of Lenora. Professor Ashleigh has just returned from South America.

Helène felt that she was not making the best of her opportunities. Helène was once promised marriage by Lord Wolfenden while she was his father's secretary. Miss Merton expressed her anger and disappointment during the conversation with Helène. Helène stated that she has no desire to take Lord Wolfenden from Miss Merton or anyone else. Helène revealed that she is the Princess Helène of Bourbon and is betrothed to Prince Henri of Ortrens. Miss Merton left the room speechless after Helène's revelation. Helène instructed her servant to deny Miss Merton access if she attempted to see her again.

The narrator's father has been in poor health since the great Solent disaster. The father's condition has led to delusions, including a belief that he has been commissioned by the Government to prepare a plan for coast defenses and the navy. The father works ten hours a day with a secretary and typist, but the results are described as unintelligible chaos. Dr. Wilmot, a mind specialist, visited the narrator and expressed interest in the father's case. Dr. Wilmot brought a letter from Dr. Whitlett, which was later revealed to be a forgery. Dr. Wilmot escaped through a window after being confronted by Dr. Whitlett. Mr. Sabin is interested in the contents of the father's study, which has brought him to Deringham.

Miss Brown expressed enthusiasm about going to Prince's. Peter Ruff returned from lunch in a subdued mood and did not smoke. Peter Ruff mentioned that his relationship with John Dory had not been beneficial. Peter Ruff observed that John Dory had not taken his wife to many places. Miss Brown questioned Peter Ruff about the intentions of Maud. Peter Ruff planned to continue offering admiration to Mrs. John Dory. Peter Ruff and Mrs. John Dory attended dinner and a theatre visit together.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Captain Ackinson was on the deck of the _Calipha_ when approached by a German Navy officer. The German officer was Captain Von Dronestein, in command of the _Kaiser Wilhelm_. Captain Ackinson expressed frustration over being stopped by the German Navy. Mr. Sabin, who can speak German, remained with Captain Ackinson during the encounter. Captain Von Dronestein requested to speak with Captain Ackinson in private. The German officer claimed that the stopping of the mail steamer was not by force. Captain Von Dronestein had a warrant for the arrest of one of the passengers on the _Calipha_.

A birthday celebration is taking place. The Professor is expected to attend the celebration despite disliking receptions. Mrs. Rheinholdt expresses her desire to be civil to everyone, as circumstances can change. Professor Ashleigh, brother of Lord Ashleigh, has recently returned from South America. The Professor shows interest in Mrs. Rheinholdt's diamond necklace. A servant named Craig brings the Professor a mackintosh due to a rainstorm. The Professor prefers to walk home after evening events.

Peter Ruff stood before the door of a house after a motor car had turned around and disappeared. The door was unlatched with a footstool placed against it inside. Peter Ruff entered the house and listened intently, noting a woman's voice humming a song upstairs. The song was identified as the opening bars of the Servian national anthem. Peter Ruff found an empty room with an easy-chair and coffee on the hob. The little lady changed her gown and prepared to listen while seated in the easy-chair. Paul Jermyn arrived, disheveled, and handed the little lady an envelope after a struggle with Von Hern.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Germany has accepted an offer and will act accordingly. A few documents are the only obstacles to achieving success. The speaker feels a sense of obligation towards Knigenstein. Helène expresses a strong desire for a strategic victory. The speaker questions Helène's courage regarding the potential for violence. Helène asserts her independence regarding her personal affairs. The speaker believes Helène's marriage to Henri is politically motivated.

Mr. Sabin was anxiously watching the platform as he waited for the train. The train departed the station two minutes after Mr. Sabin arrived. Mr. Sabin took out an atlas and expressed dissatisfaction with America. A young man named Felix approached Mr. Sabin and explained how he found his way to him. Felix posed as Mr. Sabin's servant to secure a suitable carriage for their journey. Felix deduced that Mr. Sabin would be traveling to America based on his circumstances. Felix noted that America was the only country strong enough to provide Mr. Sabin with asylum.

Peter Ruff sent a telegram himself. Peter Ruff admitted to making a fool of John Dory. Peter Ruff stated that the firm does not profit from the affair. Peter Ruff claimed to have a fourth share in the Franklin Flying Machine. Letty Shaw entered a restaurant with Austen Abbott shortly before midnight. Letty Shaw was known for her engagement to Captain the Honourable Brian Sotherst. Letty Shaw was seen supping alone with Austen Abbott, a man of bad reputation.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Sirdeller returns to America. The Count von Hern and Prince Marsine come to America. The Duchesse della Nermino comes to America. The Duchesse, Sirdeller, and Marsine are on the same steamer. The Count von Hern travels by the Lusitania due to Sirdeller's last-minute change of plans. The Duchesse was living in Cuba during the Maine disaster and was married to a rich Cuban. The Duchesse is traveling against the wishes of Von Hern.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The alliance between Helène and Henri is compulsory for uniting the two branches of the royal family. Henri is described as having excellent qualities but is also characterized as weak and dissipated. Mr. Sabin urges Helène to consider her duty to her country and royal lineage over personal desires. Helène expresses a preference for the convent over marriage with any man. Mr. Sabin believes that Helène's marriage to Henri is necessary for his acceptance by the people of France. Helène agrees to consider marriage if it is assured that it is necessary for Henri's acceptance. Mr. Sabin states that Helène and Henri represent two great Houses that could claim the throne.

John Dory and Lady Mary discuss the nature of their professions. Peter Ruff believes that the morning papers are undervalued by the British public. Peter Ruff prefers reading police news and advertisements over novels. Peter Ruff reads an advertisement in the Daily Mail seeking Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald. Peter Ruff suspects that the person seeking him, referred to as 'M', is Maud Barnes, now Mrs. John Dory. Peter Ruff instructs Miss Brown to reply to the advertisement with a request for proof of good faith. Miss Brown expresses disapproval of Peter Ruff's response to the advertisement.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Ella is described as being one of the most beautiful debutantes of the season. Lord Ashleigh is going out for an hour or two with Fitzgerald to shoot partridges. Ella expresses her excitement about her musical training and her desire to know more about it. Lord Ashleigh received a letter from Delarey regarding Ella's musical training. Delarey advises that Ella's musical training should take place in New York. Lord Ashleigh has a cablegram from Delarey that he intends to read. The setting includes a breakfast table arranged on a terrace with flowers, fruit, and silver.

The Double-Four has succeeded in discovering the source of foul literature. The government initially appealed for assistance several months ago. The navy, army, post-office employees, telegraph and telephone operators, and railway men have been the main recipients of the literature. Two million dollars have been spent to corrupt a crucial class in France. Bernadine, Count von Hern, is identified as the leader of the organization responsible for disseminating the literature. Sogrange asserts that Bernadine must die due to his actions against the Republic of France. Bernadine is guilty of treason and has fled to another country, where he cannot be extradited.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Sabin entered the room and invited Lord Wolfenden to join them for coffee. Helène welcomed Lord Wolfenden with a smile and offered him coffee. Mr. Sabin observed a change in Helène's demeanor and beauty. Helène expressed her intention to stay in the dining-room instead of moving to the drawing-room. Wolfenden declined the offer of liqueurs from Helène. Wolfenden questioned whether he should have come that evening. Wolfenden expressed his strong feelings for Helène and his determination not to give up on her.

Mary was taken to a room by the girls after a distressing event. French and Quest were left alone to discuss the situation. Quest expressed concern about the whereabouts of the Professor. Quest and French decided to search for a black box. They arrived at the Professor's house and entered without ringing. Quest discovered a hollow brick in the fireplace containing a black box. Inside the black box was a message referencing the January 1905 issue of the American Medical Journal.

Peter noted the interest of evening papers in his financial activities related to New York. The Duchesse revealed that she was born in Cuba and still owns estates there. Peter asked the Duchesse about the reported salvage of the Maine, which caused her distress. The Duchesse exhibited signs of faintness and terror in response to Peter's question. The Duchesse explained that the topic of the Maine is sensitive among her countrymen. Peter expressed regret for bringing up the distressing subject. Sogrange was found by Peter in his stateroom, relaxed and reading a French novel.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Craig finished a job that allowed the narrator to move their limbs. The narrator does not remember anything else until waking up in bed. Professor Lord Ashleigh remarked on the psychological circumstance involving Craig. Quest expressed a desire to confirm whether it was Craig who was involved. A small package addressed to French was brought by a nurse. The package contained a black box and a note signed 'THE HANDS'. Sanford Quest and his assistants arrived in Allguez to search for John Craig.

A murder and robbery occurred in suite number forty-three of the Leeland Hotel. Ella was found dead and had been strangled shortly before the police arrived. Lenora, a witness, reported that Ella thought she saw the door handle move before she was found. The maid discovered Ella's body and reported it to the manager, Mr. Marsham. The Ashleigh diamonds, which Ella was wearing, were reported stolen. Macdougal, a servant of Lord Ashleigh, was absent from the hotel at the time of the crime. The police inspector called for an expert, Mr. Sanford Quest, to assist with the investigation.

A district messenger in ordinary clothes was sent to find someone. Mr. Greening had previously rung up the person three times. De Grost was summoned to go to a location in London. Violet expressed concern about the disturbance of their evening. De Grost took a taxicab to London Bridge. He ordered a liqueur brandy and reread a note he received. De Grost observed a warehouse with lights on and two individuals working inside.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Sabin expressed interest in a story about Lord Deringham related to Wolfenden's father. Wolfenden stated that his father's work on English coast defenses and naval strength is worthless. Wolfenden's chief authority on his father's work is his secretary, who is resigning due to the work's hopelessness. A man named Franklin Wilmot, claiming to be a physician, visited Wolfenden's family with a forged letter. The visit from Wilmot was to discuss a new method of treating mental complaints and to view Wolfenden's father's work. Wilmot escaped through a window before Dr. Whitlett arrived, and Wolfenden did not secure him. Wilmot appeared well-dressed and of good manners, misleading both Wolfenden and his mother.

The conversation involves a character named Wolfenden expressing his love for Helène. Helène indicates that she is involved in an entanglement with another man but does not care for him. Wolfenden believes he can make Helène happy and urges her not to marry the other man. Helène acknowledges that something has changed her life and asks for time apart. Helène reveals that Mr. Sabin is her uncle and is involved in a significant enterprise. Helène states that her marriage to someone else is necessary for the success of Mr. Sabin's plans. Wolfenden expresses concern about Mr. Sabin's intentions and refuses to leave Helène with him.

Sanford Quest identified Macdougal as the elderly family retainer involved in a crime. Macdougal had lost both his wife and the jewels. Quest observed a white face pressed against the window before leaving the room. A man entered the apartment and attacked Macdougal with a weapon. Quest and two detectives apprehended Macdougal after revealing the truth about the situation. Quest informed the Inspector that the diamonds had been recovered and the murderer was arrested. Lenora, Macdougal's wife, was not required to give evidence against him.

Sir Richard asked Lord Merries if he had a sum of money at his disposal. Lord Merries declared that he did not have any money. Sir Richard mentioned Colonel Dickinson's small but regular income and his expectations. Mr. Masters refused to accept bills for indebtedness and insisted on cash. Mr. Masters attempted to leave the room but found the door locked. Sir Richard revealed that they could not afford to let Mr. Masters go unless he agreed to their terms. Sir Richard struck Mr. Masters with a life preserver, rendering him unconscious.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Wolfenden was informed that the price of returning the Admiral's papers was his help. Lady Deringham expressed uncertainty about the purpose of the man's proposal to steal the Admiral's papers. Lady Deringham recalled a quarrel between her husband and the Admiral that prevented direct communication. Lady Deringham desired a letter written after her marriage, which she regretted writing. Wolfenden insisted on knowing the name of the man who held the letter for blackmail. Wolfenden planned to involve the police and Scotland Yard to find the man. Lady Deringham revealed that the man was Mr. Sabin.

Spencer Fitzgerald is a subject of discussion between Maud and Peter Ruff. Maud enjoys her evening with Peter Ruff despite her marriage to John Dory. Peter Ruff believes he could have made Maud forget Spencer Fitzgerald if she were not married. Maud frequently brings up her former lover during her meetings with Peter Ruff. Peter Ruff suggests that he could arrange for Spencer Fitzgerald to come to London. Maud expresses a desire to see Spencer Fitzgerald only once to ask a question. John Dory feels uneasy about Maud's return home after her evening out.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Fitzgerald has four hundred pounds saved and a few pieces of furniture. Mrs. Barnes offered Mr. Fitzgerald more beef, which he declined. Mrs. Barnes explained that their maid, Maud, is allowed to go out on Sundays. Mrs. Barnes praised Maud's skills in keeping house and emphasized the importance of economy. Mr. Barnes suggested getting port wine to toast Mr. Fitzgerald's health during his first visit. Mr. Fitzgerald felt content with his future and his prospective in-laws. The front-door bell rang, indicating the arrival of visitors, prompting curiosity from the family.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Wolfenden commented on the appearance of a girl dressed elegantly, suggesting she is not English. Harcutt mentioned that they could find out the name of a man when they leave, as the table was reserved. Densham informed Wolfenden that their friend Felix had left due to an engagement with his chief. Wolfenden described Felix as a junior attaché at the Russian Embassy, recently appointed. Harcutt is a young man of fortune who works in journalism and is well-connected in smart society. Densham is a rising young portrait painter. The atmosphere in the room was lively, with conversation and music creating a sense of abandon.

The Clenarvon diamonds were missing from the room. John Dory was excited and prepared to leave in a motor-car. A doctor among the guests examined a man named Saunders, who had been shot in the back of the head. The bullet that struck Saunders was described as long and needle-like. A man who was outside the room reported hearing an explosion before entering. Peter Ruff chose to remain behind instead of joining John Dory in the pursuit. Peter Ruff examined the table and took an item from a book before asking a policeman to speak with the butler.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest jumped onto the last car of a freight train while it was moving. Quest struggled to maintain his balance on the train car and caught a chain with his hands. Red Gallagher and his mate were at the scene of a dead signalman, expressing horror over the situation. Red Gallagher admitted to having killed the signalman out of anger towards Quest. Gallagher and his mate fixed a tire on their car before fleeing the scene. Mrs. Rheinholdt welcomed Inspector French and asked him to drive to Mr. Quest's house. Mrs. Rheinholdt expressed excitement about retrieving her stolen jewels and praised Mr. Quest.

Victor is mentioned as someone who may need assistance from the speaker. Lord Deringham is referenced as a person who may not recognize Victor after many years. Mr. Sabin and his niece had dinner and enjoyed a dessert of muscatel grapes and peaches. Lord Wolfenden is described as an ardent suitor and a gentleman. Mr. Sabin traveled from Cromer to Peterborough and then to his current location by train. Mr. Sabin invited Lord Wolfenden to dinner, but he declined the meal and agreed to visit afterwards. Mr. Sabin finds Lord Wolfenden interesting and believes he has valuable information.

Attendance is not required early in the morning. Lenora is asked to accompany Mr. Quest in his car for a conversation about her mistress. Lenora's face is described as ghastly pale and she shows signs of fear. Mr. Quest and Lenora drive through the city streets after she is handed into his car. Lenora is seated in an easy-chair in Quest's sitting-room in front of a fire. Quest encourages Lenora to telephone someone and provides her with instructions. Lenora makes a phone call to James to inquire about his safety and the status of the jewels.

Lord Wolfenden's father is still alive but in delicate health. Wolfenden invites Mr. Sabin and his niece, Helène, for tea at the 'Geranium Club' on Ladies' Day. Mr. Sabin declines the invitation due to an overdue appointment. Wolfenden assures Helène that no harm will come to Mr. Sabin that night at the 'Milan.' Wolfenden is invited to join Mr. Sabin and Helène for supper at a quarter past eleven. Wolfenden finds a blue ribbon that fell from Helène's gown as she entered the cab. Wolfenden encounters Felix, Mr. Sabin's assailant, while crossing the street.

The Baron informed the Prince that he is currently in disgrace with his family. The Baron suggested that the Prince has signed an undertaking to influence a treaty with a certain Power in the event of succeeding to the throne. The Baron revealed that the Prince's cousins, Prince Cyril and Prince Henry, are suffering from diphtheria and are not expected to live. The Baron stated that Prince John has resigned his heirship and will enter a monastery. The Baron warned the Prince that Count von Hern is watching him and that Nisch is a confederate of Count von Hern. The Baron offered to lend the Prince money to pay his debts on the condition that he does not sign any documents from Count von Hern. The Prince acknowledged that he owes sixteen hundred pounds and the Baron provided him with two thousand pounds.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff remained silent while speaking to a woman who appeared terrified. Peter Ruff asked the woman two questions that required truthful answers. The woman denied shooting Abbott and claimed she left the room before he was shot. The woman stated that Brian Sotherst had a key to enter the premises. The revolver used in the incident belonged to the woman and was a gift from Brian Sotherst. Peter Ruff questioned the woman about why she had supper alone with Austen Abbott. The woman acknowledged that she had a habit of not dining alone with men.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: John Dory expresses triumph upon encountering Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald. Miss Brown urges Peter not to shoot and claims he should have listened to her. Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald denies being called Peter and states he has never seen the others except for Miss Brown. John Dory mentions an old warrant for Mr. Fitzgerald and suggests further inquiries. Mr. Fitzgerald claims his name is James Fitzgerald and that he is an actor at the Shaftesbury Theatre. John Dory connects Mr. Fitzgerald to a previous incident involving a clerk named Spencer Fitzgerald. Peter Ruff enters the scene, dressed in evening clothes, and expresses surprise at the situation.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Watson is the largest American holder of Cunard stock and a director of the American Board. Mr. Sabin joined a group of passengers watching a rowing boat approaching their vessel. The occupants of the rowing boat included a man with a thin sallow face and a woman wearing a thick veil. The woman in the rowing boat is Mrs. James B. Watson, who expressed gratitude to Captain Ackinson for their rescue. Mr. Watson's yacht is reported to have a broken shaft, but he relied on his engineer's assessment. Mrs. Watson is described as a nervous woman who prefers not to travel on small boats. Mr. Watson stated that his wife has lived for many years on the Continent and does not consider herself an American.

Blanche has never possessed a thousand shillings in her life. Wolfenden believes there is a scheme involving Blanche and her employer, Mr. Sabin. Wolfenden offers Blanche a hundred pounds a year for life in exchange for information. Blanche requests time to think over Wolfenden's offer until the next morning. Wolfenden writes down the terms of his offer for Blanche. Blanche expresses a desire to return quickly after their conversation. Wolfenden offers Blanche a ride in his carriage, which she accepts.

Baron de Grost and Mr. Courtledge are discussing Prince Albert's financial situation. Prince Albert has not settled his debts for a fortnight and owes over seven hundred pounds. The committee has instructed Mr. Courtledge to ask Prince Albert not to return to the club until he has paid his debts. Baron de Grost acknowledges that Prince Albert has a small income and no expectations. Prince Albert is a member of a royal house, although he is far from the succession. Baron de Grost plans to speak with Prince Albert after Mr. Courtledge addresses him. Prince Albert appears pale and has been losing money while gambling at the club.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Miss Violet Brown was upset because it was past the time Peter Ruff usually left the office. Violet Brown expressed frustration at Peter Ruff for being infatuated with another woman. Peter Ruff indicated that he believes in everyone until proven otherwise. Violet Brown warned Peter Ruff that John Dory would arrive shortly after Mrs. Dory. At eight o'clock, Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald entered Peter Ruff's office. Violet Brown pleaded with Mr. Fitzgerald to leave before it was too late. Mrs. Dory entered the office and was surprised to see Mr. Fitzgerald.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The character is described as young, impetuous, and ambitious. The existence of this character is expected to lead to factions among the nobles. Dissensions during the first generation of the re-established monarchy are considered a significant threat. The marriage between the girl and Henri would ally the Houses of Bourbon and Ortrens. The girl reflects on her feelings towards Wolfenden and her duty to her country. Mr. Sabin expresses confidence in the girl and her role in the destinies of her country. The Duchess of Montegarde arrived in London yesterday, and the girl plans to visit her.

Mademoiselle Celaire hosted a gathering in a large drawing-room with a dozen or two assembled guests. The drawing-room was decorated with pale green satin and Chippendale furniture. A grand piano was present in a smaller room adjacent to the drawing-room. The room was lit entirely with shaded candles, creating a mysterious atmosphere. Andrea Korust greeted his guests while wearing a velvet dinner jacket and a drooping black bow tie. Korust expressed a dislike for solitude and a desire for social interaction. Korust's brother prefers solitude and avoids social gatherings.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Lady Ashleigh mentioned that her daughter now cures the hams. All daily produce at the residence comes from the home farm. Lord Ashleigh often rides in the park before breakfast. The valet entered the room in a distressed state, indicating something had happened to Lord Ashleigh. The Professor confirmed that Lord Ashleigh was dead. Lord Ashleigh's body had two black marks on his throat. Quest ordered a doctor and the local police to be contacted.

Sir Richard Dyson is consulting Peter Ruff regarding a troubling situation. Sir Richard admits he could not have paid Job Masters at the time of a heavy settlement. Sir Richard and others have drawn considerable amounts from bookies after a successful double. Peter Ruff charges a fee of five hundred guineas for his consultation services. Ruff assures Sir Richard that he will be protected from any consequences related to the recent affair. Colonel Dickinson expresses skepticism about the value of Ruff's services to Sir Richard. Detective John Dory arrives to inform Sir Richard of a warrant for his arrest related to the disappearance of Job Masters.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Laura entered the tent and sat on her bed. Laura screamed after feeling something soft in her bed. A snake was discovered under the bedclothes. The Professor shot the snake multiple times after it was revealed. The Professor identified the snake as a rare and fatally poisonous species. Inspector French accused a Chinaman of placing the snake in Laura's bed. French and the cowboys pursued the Chinaman after he fled on horseback.

Peter Ruff and Sir Richard discuss a man named Teddy Jones, who is described as an adventurer. Sir Richard expresses a willingness to pay five thousand pounds for information about Teddy Jones's death. Peter Ruff agrees to investigate Teddy Jones's past to determine if he is unmanageable. Peter Ruff discovers that Teddy Jones, also known as Major Edward Jones, has a questionable history of obtaining a living. Peter Ruff observes Teddy Jones in a cafe conversing with a man known to have a criminal background. Teddy Jones appears well-dressed and has gained weight, suggesting a change in his circumstances. The conversation between Teddy Jones and his companion in the cafe indicates they are not on good terms.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest announced his intention to go to Southampton to board a steamer. Lenora was advised to stay behind and rest in a room provided for her. The group caught a train to Southampton and was joined by a man from Scotland Yard. Quest offered a ten-pound note to anyone who could get them to the _Barton_ before it sailed. They reached the steamer just as it began to move away from the dock. Quest explained to the Captain that they were searching for a criminal believed to be on board. The Captain agreed to let them on board under the condition that they would find the criminal quickly.

Peter Ruff expresses a desire for a simple life in the country, where he can hunt and shoot. Marquis de Sogrange has a different perspective on life and expresses a gambler's instinct. Peter Ruff requests that Sogrange not involve him in any plans regarding the Clenarvon jewels. Sogrange makes a remark about Peter Ruff's character, suggesting he should have been a mayor. A large dinner-party is held at Clenarvon Court with around one hundred guests. During the dinner, a loud rumbling sound is heard, prompting concern among the guests. Peter Ruff, Sogrange, and Lord Sotherst investigate the source of the noise and find an explosion has occurred.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Professor was playing the violin softly before relapsing into what seemed to be sleep. Craig followed the Professor, pleading and expostulating as they moved through a small passage. A woman with a diamond necklace approached the Professor, who then pushed Craig away. Lenora cried out about Mrs. Rheinholdt's jewels as they observed the scene in the mirror. The Professor was seen in Quest's study with a Salvation Army girl before he left her with an evil glance. The Professor was observed descending the stairs of Ashleigh House before closing a door with a strange look. After the Professor awoke, he inquired if he had slept and noted the presence of a metal band.

The thirteenth name on the list of dead was Bernadine, Count von Hern. Bernadine was killed by the strikers. Sogrange and Peter were discussing Bernadine's death when a motor car arrived at Peter's house. The Baroness von Ratten, a friend of Bernadine, came to see Peter. Peter and Sogrange had recently lunched at the Ritz with Violet. The Baroness expressed that she had struggled before deciding to visit Peter. The Baroness revealed that she had a shock due to Bernadine's death in a railway accident.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: A character in a borrowed overcoat and cap is studying a book on seagulls. Laura and Lenora are dozing while Mr. Harris is reading detective stories. Quest comments on the success of the excursion as a pleasure cruise. Laura insists that she saw a man named Craig board the steamer. Mr. Harris states that they have searched the ship thoroughly and found no one matching Craig's description. The Professor expresses a change of outlook and is content with the current situation. The group is traveling to India, and the Professor is pleased to hear this.

Mr. Vincent Cawdor and Rounceby are discussing a late sitting away from the other three men. Cawdor mentions that he brought a young lady, who is a particular friend of his. Captain Lowther is identified as the private secretary to Colonel Dean, the chief of the aeronaut department at Aldershot. Cawdor states that Captain Lowther has a draft for twenty thousand pounds, contingent on his satisfaction with the plans. Rounceby produces a roll of oilskin and insists that there must be no copying or making notes. Two plainclothes policemen enter the room and identify themselves as holding warrants for Rounceby and Marnstam's arrest. John Dory approaches Rounceby and Marnstam, stating he holds warrants for their arrest.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Blatherwick has observed a change for the worse in his lordship's state of mind over the last week. Mr. Blatherwick expressed concern about his lordship's unfounded suspicions of Miss Merton. Mr. Blatherwick described an extraordinary occurrence as a development of what he considers insanity. Mr. Blatherwick wishes to leave his position immediately due to concerns for his physical safety. Mr. Blatherwick mentioned that his lordship committed an unprovoked assault on a keeper. Wolfenden is interested in finding out the sender of a letter addressed to Mr. Blatherwick. Wolfenden proposed that Mr. Blatherwick meet a mysterious person at the Grand Hotel for lunch.

The Prince has a favorable view of the Count von Hern and acknowledges his support. Peter expresses concern that the Prince's reward to the Count von Hern is against his country's interests. The Prince is committed to rewarding the Count von Hern within a year. The Prince believes that Spain is facing a revolution and desires to be elected President of a new Spanish Republic. The Prince intends to keep his conversation with Sogrange confidential from the Count von Hern. The Count von Hern is described by the Prince as jealous and overly cautious. The Prince receives a marconigram that causes him to react with excitement.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Bill Taylor used to keep a house that was difficult to find before he was shot. The protagonist used a small, hard pellet to create an explosion that damaged the house. Sanford Quest emerged from the house after the explosion and requested to be taken to headquarters. Quest informed the police that there was no one else in the house at the time. Inspector French recognized Quest when he arrived at the central police station. Quest promised Inspector French that he would deliver the Ashleigh diamonds at nine o'clock and the murderer by midnight. Lenora visited Quest and delivered the Ashleigh diamonds to him.

Quest returned to New York after his arrest. Quest believes that arresting certain men will clear his name. The Professor expresses support for Quest's plan to arrest the men. Quest has communicated with Lenora through a pocket wireless. Lenora described her location as a room at the top of a house with a roof window. Quest plans to personally punish the man responsible for Lenora's abduction. Quest arrived in Bethel and was greeted by the Sheriff.

The passage outside was in darkness. De Grost and Monsieur de Lamborne discussed the state of a safe. De Lamborne expressed a sense of uneasiness regarding the contents of the safe. De Grost indicated that the packet in the safe was not the same as before. De Lamborne insisted that no human could have opened the safe. De Grost suggested that the safe was accessed from the room belonging to Madame de Lamborne. A woman entered a private room at the Hotel de Lorraine.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter intends to drink whiskey and soda after his encounter with the Duchesse. The Duchesse is in the music-room with several Marconi missives when Peter approaches her. Peter questions the Duchesse about her trust in the Count von Hern compared to himself. The Duchesse expresses skepticism about Peter's honesty and his right to discuss her affairs. Peter asserts that the Duchesse's affairs are of national concern. The Duchesse indicates she may require a service from Peter but needs time to think. Peter reads several copies of the New York Herald after the Duchesse leaves.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff's wife has transformed and is now a beautiful woman. Peter Ruff received a letter from RUE DE ST. QUINTAINE, PARIS, inviting him to join a circle on Thursday evening. Violet, Peter Ruff's wife, expressed concern about the invitation and reminded him of his retirement from London offices. Peter Ruff stated that he would not attend the event mentioned in the letter. Two days later, Peter Ruff received another invitation from Madame de Maupassim for Saturday evening. Peter Ruff discovered that his wife, Violet, had left for the village and was missing during lunch. Peter Ruff traveled to Paris the next morning after realizing Violet was absent.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter expressed a belief in superstition and acknowledged his fear of Bernadine. Peter mentioned that he has had twelve encounters with Bernadine, with the next being the thirteenth. The Marquis de Sogrange arrived in Berkeley Square after traveling from Paris without stopping. Sogrange informed Peter that a train from Paris was delayed due to an incident involving the engine-driver being shot. Sogrange stated that France is at risk of a second revolution due to the influence of Socialists. Sogrange criticized the newspapers for downplaying the seriousness of the situation in France. Sogrange revealed that the French government has been unable to identify the source of socialist literature affecting the working classes.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Sanford Quest approached the house after realizing he needed to find a girl. The front door of the house was open, and Quest went directly to the library. The Professor was sitting at his desk and asked Quest where he had been. Quest identified himself to the Professor, who was surprised to see him. Quest informed the Professor that his assistants believed Craig was guilty of a murder and robbery. Quest and the Professor searched the house and garage but found no one. Quest planned to use a wireless to communicate with his assistant Lenora.

Long Jim offered to get someone into the camp quietly for safety. Lenora greeted a returning party and indicated the location of Laura and the Inspector. Laura and the Inspector had been away for over an hour, and Laura expressed frustration about being kept outside. Quest asked Long Jim about a person inside the cook wagon, who was identified as a new Chinese cook. Craig had gone to New York and was not expected to return. Quest planned to leave for the Eastern Limited at seven o'clock the next morning. Quest found a small black box with a note next to his watch upon waking up.

Dory charged Marnstam and Rounceby with the wilful murder of Victor Franklin. Victor Franklin's body was recovered from Longthorp Tarn. Franklin was in Westmoreland with Marnstam and Rounceby a few days prior. Franklin stated he was not robbed and had his plans in his pocket. Dory withdrew the charges after realizing he had been deceived. Vincent Cawdor left the room shortly before Dory withdrew the charges. Rounceby and Marnstam suspected they had been misled and sought the truth from Cawdor.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Duke de Souspennier is suggested as a possible uncle of a character in the text. The Duke de Souspennier was banished from France for intriguing for the restoration of the Monarchy. Felix was involved in an accident with a hansom cab, resulting in a wound on his forehead. Felix instructed the cab driver to seek him at the Russian Embassy for payment of damages. Felix was following Foo Cha, Mr. Sabin's Chinese servant, who had just arrived in England. Lord Wolfenden has a grievance against Mr. Sabin related to the theft of valuable papers from his father's house. Felix claims to have set in motion a plan to counter Mr. Sabin's scheme.

Mr. Sabin had an appointment with Lord Wolfenden. A young lady had been waiting for Mr. Sabin in the study for about two hours. The young lady, named Blanche, had been turned away from her position. Blanche was suspected by Lord Deringham of wrongdoing but he did not know the details. Lady Deringham believed that Lord Deringham was mad and thought Blanche was unjustly dismissed. Blanche had previously amused herself with Lord Wolfenden. Mr. Sabin expressed amusement at Blanche's situation and acknowledged her contributions.

The brougham arrived at a porticoed house in Belgrave Square, London. Harcutt observed a man and a girl enter the house, with the girl displaying graceful self-possession. Densham joined Harcutt on the pavement after they both followed the man and girl. Densham possessed a card from the Princess Lobenski inviting him to her house that evening. Harcutt expressed frustration at being left behind by Densham, who intended to enter the house. Harcutt considered waiting for the man and girl to exit to learn their address. Harcutt ultimately decided to enter the house after observing a servant's gesture.

Wolfenden sent his phaeton to the station with Harcutt. Wolfenden encountered Mr. Blatherwick, who was leaving after a luncheon party. Mr. Blatherwick believed that a letter related to the luncheon was a hoax. Wolfenden warned Mr. Blatherwick not to trust Miss Merton, suggesting she is unscrupulous. Mr. Blatherwick expressed anger at Wolfenden's comments about Miss Merton. Miss Merton was found by Wolfenden in a lounge, amused by the earlier confrontation. Miss Merton stated that she is not interested in marriage.

Wolfenden intervened to prevent an attack on a man in the street. The attacker was able to escape into the gardens after being released from Wolfenden's grasp. The incident lasted approximately thirty seconds. Mr. Sabin thanked Wolfenden for his intervention and offered his card. Wolfenden's friends, Harcutt and Densham, reacted negatively after witnessing the incident. Harcutt and Densham both left abruptly, expressing discontent. Wolfenden noted a change in the behavior of his friends after the incident.

Sanford Quest is abandoning his profession of criminology. Quest is writing a letter to Inspector French to inform him of his decision. Lenora is Quest's secretary and delivers the letter to Inspector French. Inspector French is in the laboratory with a woman named Laura. Laura reacts emotionally when Inspector French expresses his feelings. Quest observes the interaction between Inspector French and Laura. Quest intends to leave with Lenora after discussing his decision.

A woman was standing with an expression of intense dejection. The woman, identified as Lady Deringham, was described as very handsome for her age. Lady Deringham's figure was slim and elegant, with few streaks of grey in her hair. She experienced a moment of abstraction before noticing a dark object approaching her. The approaching figure was a man with a club foot, identified as Mr. Sabin. Mr. Sabin had a pallid appearance and wore black flannel clothes. Lady Deringham initially trembled in fear upon seeing Mr. Sabin, but began to recover.

Mr. Sabin is planning a significant political maneuver involving Germany and England. Helène expresses her frustration and desire to return to Vienna. Mr. Sabin received a dispatch from London indicating that Baron Knigenstein has left for Berlin. The agreement between Mr. Sabin and Germany is nearly finalized. Mr. Sabin acknowledges a misunderstanding regarding the political relationship between Germany and England. Helène questions the possibility of war between France and Germany. Mr. Sabin claims he can offer Germany what it desires most: the key to England.

The Professor explained that they encountered a caravan of peaceful merchants on their way to Jaffa. The caravan halted to arrange for water, food, and horses for the two women. An Arab leading Lenora's horse suddenly stopped and pointed towards a group of horsemen approaching from the desert. The approaching horsemen were identified as the Mongars, who were attacking the caravan. The temporary escort of Quest and his companions fled the scene as the Mongars began their attack. Craig and the Chief arrived on horseback, with the Chief questioning Quest and his companions. The Chief initially ordered an attack but later apologized for the misunderstanding and invited them to his encampment.

The conversation involves two characters, Victor and Constance. Constance expresses a belief that Victor has grown kinder with age. Victor acknowledges a change in his demeanor when Constance uses his Christian name. Constance recalls past memories that evoke strong emotions for both characters. Victor initially reacts negatively to Constance's mention of his suffering. Victor decides to give Constance a bundle of letters that he has kept. Constance expresses gratitude for the letters and acknowledges a new bond between them.

Mrs. Watson expressed regret about the time and indicated she must leave the deck. Mr. Watson approached Mr. Sabin to apologize for his conduct the previous night. Mr. Sabin reassured Mr. Watson that no apology was necessary and suggested it was his wife who deserved one. Mr. Sabin mentioned having an interesting conversation with Mrs. Watson the night before. Mr. Watson acknowledged that Mrs. Watson had lived most of her life abroad and knew little about America. Mr. Sabin expressed his anticipation for his visit to America based on his conversation with Mrs. Watson. Mr. Watson became cautious upon realizing Mr. Sabin's capabilities.

The Baron expressed a tone of regret while acknowledging Madame's many conquests. The Ambassador's wife is described as a beautiful and elegant Parisienne. The Baron de Grost is established as a man of gallantry. The Baron felt a charm from the Ambassador's wife and perceived her preference for him. The Baron de Grost has no career beyond his wealth as a financier. The Ambassador's wife suggested that she and the Baron could form a great alliance. The Baron observed the greed for money in the eyes of the Ambassador's wife.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Caligula is mentioned as one of the mighty figures in the text. Grosset & Dunlap is located at 526 West 26th St., New York. B. M. Bower's novels include various thrilling Western romances. Chip and Delia Whitman are characters in the story 'Chip, of the Flying U'. The story 'The Happy Family' features eighteen Montana cowboys, including Ananias Green. The narrative 'The Lonesome Trail' follows 'Weary' Davidson as he returns to the ranch from Portland. Louis Tracy's romances, including titles like 'Cynthia's Chauffeur' and 'The Stowaway Girl', are available wherever books are sold.

Wolfenden expresses suspicion about a woman's unconsciousness and her potential connection to Mr. Sabin. Wolfenden declines to play golf and requests five minutes to speak with Mr. Sabin. The woman appears offended and leaves the room after Wolfenden's response. Wolfenden confronts Mr. Sabin about entering Deringham Hall and demands the return of a letter. Mr. Sabin admits to being in the house at Lady Deringham's invitation and explains his actions. Mr. Sabin denies the accusation of blackmailing Lady Deringham and claims to have destroyed her letters. Wolfenden asserts that his father would not have shared information with a stranger.

The Ambassador left Mr. Sabin's house and took a hired hansom towards Arlington Street. A young man named Felix observed the Ambassador and entered a private brougham, instructing the driver to go to the Embassy. Felix arrived at the house where Densham and Harcutt had followed Mr. Sabin previously. Felix inquired if the Ambassador was within and learned that he was dining late with a small party, including Madame la Princesse. Felix wrote a note for the Ambassador and instructed a servant to deliver it privately. Felix exhibited signs of great excitement while waiting in a luxuriously furnished room. Felix informed the Ambassador that a report from Cartienne confirmed the value of the documents related to Mr. Sabin.

Peter remarked that the other had business with them. The other replied that his business was to ensure they did not leave the premises alive. Mr. Philip Burr stated he had orders to carry out that had never been disobeyed since the formation of their Society. Mr. Burr offered the guests a choice in the method of their release. Sogrange identified himself as the Marquis de Sogrange and his companion as the Baron de Grost. Mr. Burr revealed that their introduction was facilitated by the Count von Hern. Mr. Burr lost his self-control upon learning Sogrange's identity.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter found Sogrange in the saloon watching a game of 'Up Jenkins.' Peter informed Sogrange that Bernadine has been busy and expressed concern about the next day. A tall man with a black beard entered the saloon and was identified as Mr. James Fanshawe. Mr. Fanshawe claimed to seek the aid of Sogrange and Peter to overthrow the House of Brangaza in Spain. Sogrange stated that the Society of the Double-Four does not interfere in the domestic policy of other nations. Mr. Fanshawe expressed suspicion about the coincidence of their presence on the same steamer. Sogrange acknowledged the necessity of an alliance but reminded Mr. Fanshawe of the English interests represented by the Baron de Grost.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff is instructed to wait for three days before returning to England. Violet expresses concern that Peter Ruff is withholding information. Peter Ruff reassures Violet that he has no cause for concern regarding his friends. Peter Ruff travels to a house at Number 16, Rue de St. Quintaine. Peter Ruff meets Madame la Marquise, who is eighty-six years old. Peter Ruff is entertained with refreshments and small talk at Madame's gathering. A tall, gray-bearded man indicates that they will discuss a matter with Peter Ruff.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: De Grost expressed a final tone and left the restaurant after exchanging greetings. Bernadine observed a couple in the lounge, particularly the woman, while waiting. The man from the couple left the lounge with quick, nervous strides, appearing afraid. The woman began to look around with curiosity after the man left. Bernadine approached the woman and initiated a conversation about their previous meetings. The woman denied knowing Bernadine and expressed her frustration with her husband's wanderlust. The woman indicated that her husband was jealous and disliked acquaintances.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest pushed through a crowd to where Craig was speaking to Inspector French. Craig informed Inspector French that Sanford Quest had escaped from the Tombs prison. Quest disguised himself by turning his coat inside out and wearing a lost hat. Inspector French announced a reward for the arrest of Sanford Quest. Quest felt a sense of helplessness after losing his pocket wireless. Quest had previously saved Craig's life at the Servants' Club before the building burned down. Quest received a telegram from the Sheriff of a small town in Connecticut regarding two men he was inquiring about.

Mr. Sabin displayed enthusiasm and passion during a conversation with the Ambassador. The Ambassador expressed fascination with Mr. Sabin and requested to know his true identity. Mr. Sabin insisted on maintaining his incognito and preferred to be addressed as Mr. Sabin. The Ambassador indicated he would apply for leave of absence to present Mr. Sabin's scheme to his master. Mr. Sabin stated that the payment for his scheme would be conditional upon its success. Mr. Sabin set a limit of fourteen days for the Ambassador's decision regarding the scheme. After their meeting, Mr. Sabin began selecting golf clubs from a pile in the room.

Peter Ruff is feeling depressed and uncertain about his clothing choices for traveling. Violet suggests that Peter should wear brown clothes for the trip. Peter Ruff plans to close his office and leave a notice stating he will be back on Friday. Peter Ruff expresses a sense of apprehension about an upcoming meeting related to a letter he received. During the journey, Peter Ruff is aware that he is being shadowed by two men. Peter Ruff feels a mix of comfort and regret about bringing Violet with him on the trip. As the train approaches Paris, Peter Ruff begins to collect their belongings.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Inspector and Mr. Quest discuss a series of murders and the theft of jewels. Mr. Quest examines the safe and finds no fingerprints, suggesting the thief wore gloves. Inside the safe, Mr. Quest discovers a small black box containing a note signed by the Hands. The note instructs Mr. Quest to look in the right-hand drawer of his desk. Mr. Quest retrieves Mrs. Rheinholdt's necklace from the right-hand drawer of his desk. A conference is taking place in Quest's study with the Professor, Laura, and Lenora present. Lenora describes her experience of being confined and only seeing a pair of hands delivering food.

John Dory is a detective officer from Scotland Yard. John Dory received information that led him to examine the sleeping apartments in a hotel. Monsieur Antoine is the hotel manager who initially refuses to allow the examination of the rooms. Peter Ruff is mentioned in a note addressed to John Dory, indicating that Jean Lemaitre can be found in the upper rooms of the Hotel de Flandres. Dory threatens to arrest Antoine if he does not cooperate with the search. Dory and Antoine find Peter Ruff unconscious in a small back bedroom, with a strong smell of chloroform present. Peter Ruff reveals that he was tracking down Jean Lemaitre, who was hiding as a sick waiter.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Sabin wishes to preserve his incognito while in England. Lady Deringham has not spoken of Mr. Sabin to her son. Mr. Sabin prefers to remain Mr. Sabin to Lady Deringham's son. Mr. Sabin is writing a critical paper on the armaments of the world for a European review. Mr. Sabin received valuable information from Mr. C. regarding his paper. Lady Deringham's demeanor changes when Mr. Sabin mentions her husband's name. Lady Deringham experiences fear and mistrust towards Mr. Sabin.

Wolfenden wore a deep blue gown trimmed with silvery fur. Mr. Sabin has an infirmity that makes walking on stone pavements painful. Mr. Sabin's niece expressed her enjoyment of shopping. Wolfenden assisted Mr. Sabin the previous night and received gratitude for it. Mr. Sabin recognized the man who attempted to assault him. Wolfenden confirmed that the assailant was a guest of his but considered him a stranger. Wolfenden is the son of Admiral Lord Deringham.

Middleton is advised to rise out of the police. The group observes the marshland in silence. The Professor expresses unease about the atmosphere. Lord Ashleigh attempts to alleviate the group's discomfort. Lady Ashleigh is away opening a bazaar. Dinner is served in the great banqueting hall. The Professor reminisces about familiar surroundings and family history.

Peter and Violet entered a crowded music-hall in London to watch a ballet. Mademoiselle Louise received applause as she began her performance. Monsieur Guillot was present in a box, displaying confidence that troubled Peter. Peter recognized a solitary man in the adjoining box who had applauded Louise. Peter instructed Violet to watch Guillot and alert him if Guillot left his box. Guillot briefly left his chair but returned within ten seconds. A young lady exited the stage-door and entered a large motor car waiting outside.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Sanford Quest is described as the greatest master in criminology. Sanford Quest operates as a detective and is referred to as the master detective of the world. He has a great house in a backwater square of New York for his office. Sanford Quest possesses wireless telegraphy, private chemists, spies, and agents in every city of the world. He has the ability to break up criminal gangs and takes only the cases he chooses. Sanford Quest has a notable presence that affects those around him, though he appears unassuming. He was seen descending before a large house in Georgia Square, a unique neighborhood.

Madame was nervous and terrified when she arrived at Bernadine's room. Bernadine offered Madame tea and suggested she unfasten her jacket due to the warmth of the room.
