Madame revealed that her husband, Paul, was highly strung and had a past connected to Russia. Madame's father was killed in riots and two of her brothers were sent to Siberia. Bernadine learned that Paul was sympathetic to the revolutionaries and may have secretly worked with them. Madame expressed disdain for Father Paul, claiming he betrayed the cause for personal gain. At the end of the meeting, Madame declined Bernadine's invitation to return, citing difficulty due to her husband.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Wolfenden feels cold and anxious after a conversation with Felix. Wolfenden states that he acted instinctively to help a stranger. Felix warns Wolfenden to pray not to see the man again, describing him as harmful. Felix refuses to provide details about the man or the lady accompanying him. Felix claims to have multiple reasons for wanting to take the man's life. Felix mentions that the man possesses a stick with a peculiar stone that is said to protect him. Wolfenden considers Felix's warnings to be extravagant and believes he has nothing to fear.

Sir Richard admitted that he has not always adhered to the paths of righteousness. Sir Richard borrowed money and was in financial distress before coming into the baronetcy. In Paris, Sir Richard used an assumed name to gain entry to an exclusive club. Sir Richard lost eighteen thousand francs while playing cards and later returned to win sixty thousand francs through cheating. Sir Richard's actions led to a scandal, and he escaped from France with money. Teddy Jones, who was in Paris at the time of the scandal, knows about Sir Richard's past and has since become a financial burden to him. Sir Richard provided Teddy Jones's address, which is at Mrs. Bognor's boarding-house in Russell Street, Bloomsbury.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff was brought to the bedside of a dying woman without time to change his traveling clothes. The woman informed Peter Ruff that he was four days late in responding to her summons. Peter Ruff had previously notified the council of his retirement from public life four years ago. The woman stated that Peter Ruff had been chosen as her successor despite his retirement. Peter Ruff expressed disbelief at being chosen, citing his absence from the world for four years. The woman insisted that Peter Ruff could only escape the charge laid upon him by death. After the death of the woman, Peter Ruff expressed his desire to see his wife to the Marquis de Sogrange.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Sabin brought a book titled 'The Golf Courses of the World' on his way to Liverpool. Felix was the bearer of a message to Mr. Sabin. Felix's message was an offer from the Czar of Russia for Mr. Sabin to return to Teheran as an accredited ambassador. Mr. Sabin stated that he never bears personal grudges and has no ill-will towards Felix. Mr. Sabin declined the offer to return to Teheran, citing his age as a reason. Felix expressed disappointment at Mr. Sabin's decision to decline the offer. Mr. Sabin mentioned that the new Shah has a passion for intrigue.

Peter sat on the edge of the bunk and expressed concern about his lack of information regarding a situation. Peter mentioned that he had spoken to the Duchesse of the Maine disaster. Sogrange and Peter discussed the ongoing salvage efforts of the Maine and its implications for international relations. The Lusitania was expected to arrive within half an hour, as indicated by the deck steward. Sogrange and Peter acknowledged the influence of Sirdeller on global financial markets and politics. Sirdeller had been visited by Don Pedro, Prince of Marsine, leading to a series of cablegrams to American engineering firms. The outcome of the salvage works on the Maine was anticipated to clarify whether it was blown up from outside or inside.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Lenora suspects a man of being guilty of a crime for which Sanford Quest is in prison. Lenora intends to have the man questioned about his innocence or guilt. The man expresses fear and claims he is innocent. Lenora uses a pocket wireless to send a message about the man being locked up. Laura informs Quest that Lenora believes Craig is involved in the crimes. Laura mentions that Lenora found fragments of embroidered material in the Professor's study. Quest considers a plan to work with the guard to gain access to the situation.

Bernadine and Peter are in a study together. Bernadine possesses a small revolver. Peter is instructed by Bernadine to reassure his wife, Violet, during a phone call. Peter lies to Violet about his safety and the presence of police. Bernadine warns Peter that any mention of danger will result in his death. Peter expresses disbelief in Bernadine's threats and challenges him with a bet. Bernadine shows signs of frustration during the conversation.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The male character expresses his love for Helène and desires her to live in England as his wife. Helène responds that it is impossible for her to marry him. Helène indicates that she will probably marry someone else. The male character believes Helène is being coerced into her decision. Helène asserts that no one would dare to coerce her. The male character feels a mix of anger and longing towards Helène. Helène wishes she could share more about her situation with the male character.

Quest is concerned about the disappearance of his assistant, Miss Lenora Macdougal. Lenora Macdougal stayed at Clifford's Hotel in Payne Street the night before her disappearance. Lenora left the hotel at approximately two o'clock after an early lunch. Lenora was expected to visit her aunt after staying at the hotel, but she never arrived. Quest visited Scotland Yard to report Lenora's disappearance to Mr. Hardaway. Lenora's luggage is still at the hotel, waiting for her to send for it. Quest learned that Lenora had previously been at her aunt's old address in Hampstead.

Peter Ruff claims he has never seen Maud before. James Fitzgerald states he has not missed a day at the Shaftesbury Theatre for three years. Maud indicates that Peter Ruff did not bring the correct Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald. John Dory confronts James Fitzgerald before leaving the room with Maud. Violet Brown expresses anger towards Peter Ruff for causing her distress. Peter Ruff admits to practicing on James Fitzgerald for a deception. Peter Ruff offers Violet Brown dinner as a gesture of apology.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Harcutt and Densham sat down beside Wolfenden while he was having coffee. Wolfenden met Mr. Sabin by chance in Bond Street and spent the evening with him and a girl. Wolfenden stated that he failed to gain any definite information about Mr. Sabin and the girl. Densham expressed a desire to drop the matter, suggesting that the girl and Mr. Sabin were not part of their lives. Harcutt disagreed with Densham, stating that Mr. Sabin was too interesting to ignore. Wolfenden indicated that he had developed feelings for the girl and was not willing to give her up. Wolfenden received a letter from Deringham Hall, Norfolk, which indicated he needed to leave London.

Peter is expected at the stage door in forty minutes. Mademoiselle Celaire is a famous Frenchwoman who appears at the stage door. The Brothers Korust have a week's engagement at the Alhambra with a salary of six hundred pounds. The Brothers Korust have taken a furnished house in Hamilton Place at a high rent and have issued invitations for seven supper parties. Mademoiselle Celaire believes the Brothers Korust are connected to a great European court and have ulterior motives for their visit. Peter and Mademoiselle Celaire plan to watch the events unfold and compare notes later. The car arrives at a handsome house in Hamilton Place where a footman receives Peter.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff wore a grey suit and chose a plain mauve tie. Peter Ruff had coffee, letters, and newspapers set out on a small round table. Peter Ruff typically glanced through newspapers before attending to letters or breakfast. The Daily Telegraph reported a tragedy involving Austen Abbott, who was shot dead. Captain the Honourable Brian Sotherst was arrested in connection with Austen Abbott's death. Miss Letty Shaw was mentioned as being present with Austen Abbott before the incident. Miss Brown expressed shock over the incident and mentioned her acquaintance with Letty Shaw.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Sogrange and Peter discussed their plans to leave New York and go incognito. Sogrange suggested they change their appearance to avoid recognition. Peter expressed doubt about the feasibility of avoiding the press in New York. Sogrange and Peter were staying on the twelfth story of a building in New York. They decided to leave for a hotel on Broadway after altering their appearances. Peter disguised himself as an English maker of electrical instruments. Sogrange transformed into a Canadian connected with the theatrical business.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The body of a boy was thrown into the water, and he disappeared with a splash. Two men, an older man and a younger man, decided to leave the scene after a moment of indecision. Mr. James P. Rounceby and Mr. Richard Marnstam were alone in the small smoking room of the Milan Hotel. Rounceby and Marnstam were in evening dress and appeared to be waiting for someone. Rounceby expressed concern about Vincent Cawdor's reliability, while Marnstam reassured him that Cawdor was trustworthy. Miss Violet Brown entered the room with Mr. Vincent Cawdor, who was seated at a writing table. Cawdor was wearing an opera hat and had a light overcoat on the floor beside him.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Colonel Mayson is referred to as the only military aeronaut in England. Peter and Mademoiselle Korust attend a supper where Colonel Mayson and General Noseworthy are present. Peter enjoys the supper and engages with Mademoiselle Celaire and his hostess. Andrea Korust plays music during the event and expresses distaste towards Peter. Mademoiselle Korust leads Peter to a secluded corner of the music room. Peter mentions an acquaintance with Count von Hern to Mademoiselle Korust. Peter warns Colonel Mayson that General Noseworthy may be inquisitive.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Lady Deringham admitted to aiding a man in robbing Wolfenden's father. The theft involved a handful of notes related to a magazine article. Wolfenden expressed doubts about the severity of his father's condition and the value of his work. Wolfenden mentioned that Admiral Blatherwick had not trusted anyone with important papers for weeks. Wolfenden found detailed sheets related to the Suffolk coast that appeared to be accurate. Lady Deringham revealed that the man involved in the theft was once her lover. Lady Deringham expressed a desire to retrieve letters she had written to the man.

Peter Ruff intends to speak to Lady Mary's brother. Lady Mary expresses concern about the situation and asks if there is any chance of success. Peter Ruff believes there is a chance but warns that the odds are against them and time is short. Lady Mary confirms that the driver of her electric brougham can be trusted and agrees to lend him to Peter Ruff. Peter Ruff instructs Lady Mary to keep her brother occupied in the ballroom until a quarter to two. Peter Ruff waits in Lady Mary's brougham before following a large, closed motor car to a house. Peter Ruff instructs the driver to watch the house and be ready to leave quickly if he reappears.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Bernadine arrives at a gathering wearing a long traveling ulster. The Baroness remains silent after a previous outburst. Bernadine claims to have survived a railway accident and expresses an appetite for food and drink. Sogrange comments on the reliability of the press regarding Bernadine's supposed death. Bernadine explains that he traveled by motor car from Chantilly after losing his servant, who was mistaken for him. Sogrange remarks on the dire conditions in France and the railway strike. Bernadine expresses a pessimistic view of France's future, stating it is plagued by sedition and decay.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The protagonist is waiting for a response from her friend and expresses fear about her situation. A boy outside shouts about a lost baseball, which has crashed into the protagonist's room. The protagonist writes a message for help and attaches it to the baseball. She successfully throws the baseball out of the skylight after an initial failed attempt. Inspector French arrives at the protagonist's location with a policeman. The protagonist is in a state of emotional distress and is assisted by Inspector French. Sanford Quest arrives at the scene with law enforcement personnel.

Wolfenden encounters Harcutt in the hotel stables. Wolfenden is visiting his family near Deringham Hall. Densham has left for India after giving up on a certain matter. Densham sent a message to Wolfenden regarding a girl. Harcutt is in the area for professional reasons. Mr. Sabin is present at the hotel. Harcutt believes Mr. Sabin has an identity beyond his own.

A lariat was thrown around two men, pinning their hands to their sides. Two cowboys disarmed the men and secured them against a wagon. Long Jim threatened the men while preparing to trim their hair. Inspector French intervened, insisting that the law must be respected. Long Jim shot near Inspector French's feet, causing him to jump. The deputies decided to accept Long Jim's offer of a drink. Lenora and Quest were nearby, with freedom just a short distance away.

Mr. Sabin identified himself as the Duc de Souspennier while traveling incognito. Mr. Sabin was popular among the seven passengers and engaged in the routine of steamer life. Mr. Sabin played shuffleboard daily and was skilled at the game. A yacht named _Mayflower_, owned by Mr. James Watson of New York, signaled for assistance. The captain of the steamer considered the yacht's distress signal and discussed it with Mr. Sabin. Mr. Sabin advised the captain not to pick up the yacht's owner and his wife, suggesting they wait for the next scheduled ship. The captain ultimately decided to respond to the yacht's signal despite Mr. Sabin's advice.

The man wore a sombre black cloak and a broad-brimmed black hat. The man requested not to be recognized and expressed that he was being watched. Louise mentioned that the man had changed and commented on his appearance. Louise led the man to a flat she had borrowed on the second floor. The flat contained a round table laid for supper and was dimly lit. Louise left the man alone in the room to turn on the lights. Guillot arrived and inquired about the man's presence.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: John Dory had neglected to shave and was drinking beer. John Dory expressed dissatisfaction with his wife's social activities. Maud mentioned that Peter Ruff had made an appointment with Spencer Fitzgerald. John Dory was eager to capture Spencer Fitzgerald. Maud felt guilty about the situation and worried about Peter Ruff's opinion of her. Maud confirmed that the meeting with Fitzgerald was scheduled for the following night at eight o'clock. John Dory believed that his opportunity for revenge was approaching.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The narrator observed that a group had not started to climb a hill. The narrator made an important call before driving home. Upon returning home, the narrator found that a gentleman had left a note after visiting. The gentleman had been shown into the study and stayed for about ten minutes. The writing materials in the study had been used, and a sheet of notepaper was missing. Wolfenden expressed confusion about the attempted robbery and the value of his father's research. The Countess reported missing papers and models, and Lord Deringham accused Blatherwick of theft.

De Grost and a policeman discussed a Continental wine business that is often late. De Grost crossed the road and returned to the building they had been discussing. Inside the building, a boy turned the key of the outer door after De Grost knocked on the window-pane. Men emerged from hidden places, including a clerk who removed a false mustache and wig. De Grost was surrounded by a group of hard-featured men, with Bernadine standing on the outskirts. De Grost and Bernadine proceeded to a tasting office where De Grost sampled a wine. Bernadine suggested that one of them must go, implying a conflict between him and De Grost.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Dr. Gilette is a physician who interacts with a character named Antoine. Antoine leads Dr. Gilette through narrow passages and steep stairs. A man referred to as 'Double-Four' is found in a room and is instructed by Dr. Gilette to strip. Dr. Gilette descends the stairs carrying his bag after attending to 'Double-Four'. Antoine explains to a customer that a waiter has been ill and is currently in an empty bedroom. Dr. Gilette assures Antoine that there is no infection related to the waiter's illness. A character named John Dory interacts with Antoine and discusses the nature of the clientele.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Constance Manver Deringham reports that her husband is very unwell and has been experiencing hallucinations regarding the value of his papers. He has developed a belief that there is a plot to steal his manuscripts and recently dismissed Miss Merton, a typewriter, without notice. He has installed cast-iron shutters on the study windows and has two keepers on duty outside with loaded revolvers. Constance expresses concern about the gossip surrounding his behavior and notes that he refuses to see anyone. Wolfenden feels guilty for not visiting Deringham sooner after receiving Constance's letter and is conflicted about leaving London. He has been spending time in Piccadilly and Bond Street, hoping to encounter someone he is interested in. Wolfenden decides to visit Deringham to address the situation as soon as possible.

The woman expresses that she cannot dine alone tonight. Bernadine informs the woman that her husband cannot return before morning. The woman describes her husband, Paul, as fierce and rough but generous. Bernadine reveals to the woman that her husband has deceived her. Bernadine claims that the woman's husband is in peril of his life and has a false identity. The woman is shocked to learn that her husband is responsible for her father's death and her brothers' imprisonment. Bernadine instructs the woman to fetch a black despatch box to prove his claims.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Watson closed the door after expressing a lack of malice. Mr. Sabin stepped out onto the deck and observed the sea and sky. Mr. Sabin experienced a sense of depression and reflection on his perceived failures. He recalled his past inspirations and sacrifices related to his love for his country. Mr. Sabin thought of a woman with whom he had a significant emotional connection. Mr. Sabin successfully persuaded the captain to agree to a risky scheme by lunchtime the following day. Mrs. Watson found Mr. Sabin in a secluded corner of the boat and they engaged in conversation.

Wolfenden was smoking in the early hours of the morning. Wolfenden considered the woman he loved to be his first and last love. Wolfenden's father appeared at his door with a revolver in hand. Wolfenden's father expressed feelings of being deceived and betrayed. Wolfenden and his father heard faint sounds coming from the library. Wolfenden's father was described as pale with bloodshot eyes. Wolfenden and his father proceeded cautiously towards the library.

Peter received a cable that he transcribed. Major Kosuth, a leader of the revolution in Turkey, visited Peter with Von Hern. Peter communicated with Paris regarding the situation. Violet expressed that a million pounds is not a large sum of money. Peter indicated that a million pounds is difficult for any individual to handle in cash. Peter is trying to find out who Bernadine and Kosuth are waiting to see. Peter's stockbroker mentioned Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge, a wealthy American financier.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Wolfenden observed a girl who appeared very pale and had an expression of anger and reproach. Wolfenden expressed his willingness to help the girl and planned to visit her the next day. The girl thanked Wolfenden for his kindness and consideration. Wolfenden watched the girl leave in a carriage with Selby and felt relieved after the encounter. The next morning, Wolfenden followed his routine and hoped to see Mr. Sabin and his companion in the Park. Wolfenden returned to his rooms and checked for any messages but found none related to Mr. Sabin. Wolfenden visited Harcutt's rooms where he met Densham and discussed Mr. Sabin's lack of gratitude.

De Grost requested Bernadine to discredit him. Bernadine demanded De Grost's code, keys to his safe, and free entry into his house. De Grost provided a bunch of keys and mentioned the code was in green morocco leather. Bernadine wrote a note on a card to ensure his entry into De Grost's house. De Grost was informed he would be bound and gagged like his manager and clerk. Bernadine planned to telephone after verifying safe conduct and obtaining certain papers. Bernadine arrived at the west end of London and visited his rooms before going to Porchester House.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Lenora expressed concern about a girl caring for Craig. A young woman threatened the group, wishing they had died before arriving. The Professor noted that they were in Craig's power and should avoid mentioning him. The Mongars began preparing to break camp after a warning cry was heard. Craig informed the group that British soldiers were pursuing them. The Chief refused to let the group stay behind, believing they would betray the Mongars. Craig advised the group to follow the Chief's orders due to the Mongars' sensitivity to their words.

Dr. Franklin Wilmot visited Wolfenden to discuss Lord Deringham's health. Wolfenden expressed difficulty in arranging a meeting with his father on short notice. Dr. Wilmot stated that he could assess Lord Deringham's mental condition without seeing him. Dr. Wilmot's method involves analyzing a patient's letters and recent work. Wolfenden mentioned that his father does not share his work with anyone and maintains secrecy. Dr. Wilmot indicated that he needed to act quickly regarding Lord Deringham's case. Lady Deringham expressed her support for seeking Dr. Wilmot's opinion on her husband's health.

Monsieur de Lamborne expressed doubt about the success of a task due to time constraints and difficult conditions. The Baron de Grost received a telegram from headquarters instructing him to assist Monsieur de Lamborne. The Baron de Grost declined to return to the Embassy with Monsieur de Lamborne and suggested he go to his club instead. Madame de Lamborne was the center of attention among a group of admirers at the event. Monsieur de Lamborne returned home at one o'clock and found the Baron de Grost waiting for him in the library. The Baron de Grost examined a sealed envelope and noted its weight before it was placed in a safe. Monsieur de Lamborne and the Baron de Grost prepared to keep watch in the library after securing the document.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest asked the Professor for the time, and the Professor replied it was seven o'clock, five minutes past. French informed Quest that it was three minutes past seven. Quest found a strip of paper in a black box by his bed and showed it to French. A cowboy mentioned to Quest that it was eight o'clock and questioned whether they would make the eight-thirty train to New York. Quest realized that their watches had been set back and exclaimed about 'The Hands.' Lenora found a black box with a scrap of paper that warned of danger to Quest and the others. Lenora attempted to ride after Quest and the others, despite the Chinese cook's refusal to help her.

Bernadine and De Grost are discussing the fate of De Grost's manager and clerk. De Grost expresses concern about the whereabouts of his manager and clerk. Bernadine reveals that De Grost's manager and clerk are bound and gagged in a dark corner of the office. Bernadine indicates that he is waiting for the tide to rise to access the river. De Grost acknowledges the odds against him, noting the presence of eight men. Bernadine suggests two ways to deal with an opponent: a crude method leading to death or discrediting them. De Grost shows composure despite the situation and expresses a desire to continue living.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest asked the Professor how long it would take to reach the Mongar village. The Professor estimated the journey would take two or three days if they could get camels. Laura and Lenora expressed their desire to join the camel ride across the desert. The Professor assured them that the journey would not be unpleasant and that the district was peaceable. The Professor arranged for four camels and a small escort to start the next morning. An Englishman matching Craig's description had recently departed in the same direction. The Mongar village is situated in a cul-de-sac, making it unlikely for Craig to escape.

The inquest on the body of Austen Abbott took place in Letty Shaw's parlor. The attendees included Letty Shaw, her mother, Lady Mary, Sir William Trencham, Peter Ruff, Violet Brown, and Mr. John Dory. Peter Ruff stated that he was present as the agent of Lady Mary Sotherst to prove Captain Sotherst's innocence. Mr. John Dory, who is in charge of the case against Captain Sotherst, expressed impatience and suggested postponing the discussion until after the inquest. Peter Ruff proposed to reconstruct the events of the crime scene as part of the investigation. Letty Shaw reacted with distress during the reconstruction and attempted to prevent access to a closed door.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Harcutt felt tension while listening to a conversation about hidden diplomatic matters. Mr. Sabin expressed that he would not take further action until he spoke with Harcutt again. Harcutt recognized Baron von Knigenstein as the German Ambassador during the conversation. Harcutt experienced a sense of fascination and urgency to uncover more about the discussed matters. Densham was found alone, looking gloomy while observing dancers at the event. Densham attempted to obtain an introduction to a young lady but was informed by Lobenski that she was not allowed to make acquaintances. The young lady was under the care of a guardian or uncle, as clarified by Densham.

Wolfenden observed a carriage approaching rapidly along the private road from Deringham Hall. The carriage was a little brougham that Mr. Sabin had brought down from London. The horses were galloping and the driver made no effort to slow them down as they approached Wolfenden. Mr. Sabin was seen leaning back in the carriage with a forbidding expression. Wolfenden realized that Mr. Sabin was trying to catch the one o'clock express to London. Wolfenden ran towards Deringham Hall filled with anxiety and anger regarding Mr. Sabin. Wolfenden found his father in the billiard-room, appearing relaxed and cheerful.

The diamonds have been recovered. The Marquis congratulated Violet on her husband's cleverness. The Marquis lost a bet of twenty-five thousand francs to Peter Ruff. Peter Ruff stated that he has made friends with Dory and won a thousand pounds. Peter Ruff expressed a desire to look for a little estate in the country. Peter Ruff received a message from Madame requesting his presence on Thursday evening. Peter Ruff is described as a well-preserved English country gentleman.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The horses are described as very fresh and have a tendency to run away downhill. Blanche expresses a dislike for quiet horses and states that she enjoys being run away with. Wolfenden points out Mr. Blatherwick to Blanche while they are driving. Blanche agrees to leave Mr. Blatherwick alone on the condition that she can drive for a mile. Wolfenden observes that Blanche is an accomplished whip when she takes the reins. Wolfenden encounters Helène and Mr. Sabin while driving, which causes him discomfort. Wolfenden reflects on his feelings towards Helène and doubts Blanche's intentions regarding their meeting.

Mr. Sabin is engaged in a conversation with Felix regarding his intentions and actions. Felix has been observing Mr. Sabin's movements for two weeks. Mr. Sabin claims that modern diplomacy has transformed and that secrecy is outdated. Felix accuses Mr. Sabin of cheating at cards, which Mr. Sabin denies. Mr. Sabin asserts that he has obtained a significant power that will soon become a reality. Felix suggests that Mr. Sabin has opened negotiations with his chief, Knigenstein. Mr. Sabin states that he has no price that Prince Lobenski could pay.

Quest expressed skepticism about Craig's character, suggesting he may not be as respectable as he appears. Laura suggested moving on to another job after the Rheinholdt woman received her jewels back. Lenora mentioned Macdougal, who has not been recaptured and has a strong interest in jewels. Quest dismissed the idea of Macdougal being involved due to the return of the jewels. Laura was instructed to take the train to Mountways to speak with the section boss about Macdougal. Quest prepared for his outing by taking explosives and recharging his revolver. Ross, Quest's valet, confirmed that no one else was present at the house that day.

The girl received a bunch of violets from Craig, which she pinned to her frock. Craig informed the girl that he had an appointment at Professor Ashleigh's. The girl observed a man in a blue serge suit talking to the landlady after Craig left. The man in the blue serge suit questioned the girl about her uncle's whereabouts. The girl presented a legal document bequeathing her uncle's possessions to her. The document included a condition that she must not speak to anyone with the name Ashleigh. The man in the blue serge suit claimed to be from the police and insisted on taking the document.

Peter Ruff is a corresponding member of the 'Double-Four' and has the right to appeal for help in France. Peter Ruff has previously felt alienated and treated badly, leading him to consider cheating the law. Peter Ruff claims to have kept his hands clean and does not intend to engage in illegal activities. The Marquis de Sogrange is successful in entertaining his neighbors during dinner. Peter Ruff and the Marquis de Sogrange discuss the income from Sogrange's estate, which amounts to seven million francs. Peter Ruff and his wife are attending the gathering as ordinary guests. The Marquis de Sogrange expresses that he cannot spend his income despite being extravagant.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The price for giving up Peter Ruff is nine hundred million francs. Mademoiselle has expressed that she cares for Peter Ruff. Peter Ruff and Miss Brown are traveling together in a carriage from Dover. Miss Brown has informed Peter Ruff that she has told Monsieur de Founcelles they are engaged. Miss Brown has refused two hundred and fifty thousand francs for Peter Ruff's sake. A woman who was Peter Ruff's first love is described as having fallen upon evil days. Violet claims to be both the secretary and the wife of Peter Ruff.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Sabin was intrigued by a small flag visible from a window. The flag was related to golf, a game favored by Mrs. Peterson. Mr. Sabin expressed a desire to go outside to see the golf course. Mr. Sabin was informed that his room had been prepared for three weeks. Mr. James Green, a Scotsman, was responsible for the golf course. Mr. Sabin indicated he was fond of golf but lacked clubs and shoes. Mr. Green offered Mr. Sabin access to clubs and shoes for playing golf.

De Grost mentioned that his wife brought Lady Brownloe and that the brougham only holds two comfortably. Prince Albert did not respond to De Grost and appeared incapable of speech. The Baron inquired about the amount of Prince Albert's debts. Prince Albert confirmed he would settle his card debts by mid-day the next day or possibly that night. De Grost invited Prince Albert to his house for a discussion before the Prince made another call. During their conversation, De Grost asked Prince Albert where the money to pay his debts was coming from. De Grost revealed that the money was to come from a government with which Prince Albert's family should not have dealings.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff is involved in a situation concerning jewelry and security at a dinner. Mr. Richards has been excused from supervising the dinner service by his lordship. Peter Ruff requests that the remaining jewelry be packed in cases and asks for a plan of the house with guest names. Mr. John Dory returns from a neighboring railway station after experiencing issues with his car's tires. The daily routine at Clenarvon Court continues with breakfast served early for a shooting event. Peter Ruff discusses his intentions with the Marquis de Sogrange regarding aiding Mr. John Dory. The Marquis de Sogrange places a bet of twenty-five thousand francs against Peter Ruff's efforts to assist Mr. John Dory.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Sabin and Felix are traveling alone in a carriage. Felix had previously intended to kill Mr. Sabin during their first meeting. Mr. Sabin expresses a desire for assurance that Felix will not attempt to harm him again. Felix claims that the cause of personal enmity between them is no longer present. Felix received a telegram from Brussels three weeks ago regarding a woman who believed she was dying. Felix recounts a past event involving Mr. Sabin and a failed assassination attempt. Mr. Sabin reacts with visible distress when Felix discusses the details of the past incident.

Craig untied a sash from his waist and tied it to a tree as ordered by Quest. Craig kicked Quest's revolver away and threatened him with a knife. Lenora appeared and ordered Craig to drop his knife, which he did. Craig tied the sash around Feerda, who had been resisting Quest. Quest gagged Feerda with her linen head-dress and took Craig to where others were waiting. Quest instructed Craig to lead them to Port Said while keeping him covered with a revolver. The group rode out of the jungle into the open desert while being pursued by the Mongars.

Peter blew his whistle loudly and persistently. Bernadine mocked Peter and suggested he try again. A bell rang throughout the house, indicating a visitor at the front door. Bernadine instructed a servant to answer the door and inform any visitors that the Baroness was indisposed. Bernadine fired his revolver at Peter, but Sogrange intervened. The police commissioner asked Peter if he had a charge against Bernadine. Sogrange claimed that Bernadine had committed extraditable offenses against France.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest announced that they have found the skeleton. The skeleton was found within a hundred yards of Professor Edgar Ashleigh's house. Quest found the skeleton hidden in a piano box in a hut. A human being named Hartoo was also found in a state of captivity in the hut. Professor Ashleigh received a letter from Sir William Raysmore regarding the discovery of the skeleton and Hartoo. The letter warned Professor Ashleigh to guard his discovery due to potential jealousy from other anthropologists. Craig entered the room to inform them that the hut was on fire.

The book is titled 'PETER RUFF AND THE DOUBLE FOUR' and is written by E. Phillips Oppenheim. The contents of the book include two main sections: Book One and Book Two, each containing multiple chapters. Book One introduces Mr. Peter Ruff and includes chapters about various characters and events related to a supper party at Daisy Villa. Daisy Villa is located on Green Street, Streatham, and is owned by Mr. David Barnes, a coal merchant. Mr. David Barnes is described as a struggling but fairly prosperous individual with Methodist beliefs. The supper party includes Mr. Barnes, his wife Mrs. Barnes, their son, and their daughter Maud, who is introduced to Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald. Mr. Spencer Fitzgerald is depicted as a young man of modest appearance who is courting Maud Barnes.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter Ruff and John Dory attempted to assist a girl who was screaming and clinging to her place. Fluffy Dean was found motionless on the bed, fully dressed, with a phial slipped from her fingers. A piece of paper with a message from Fluffy Dean indicated her intention to not go to Australia. Letty Shaw fainted and was carried to her room after the discovery of Fluffy Dean. Peter Ruff explained that the partition between the sitting room and bedroom was flimsy and had an opening. Fluffy Dean shot Austen Abbott after hearing him with Letty Shaw, then fainted. Captain Sotherst found Austen Abbott dead with Miss Shaw's revolver beside him and was later arrested.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The lieutenant of the _Calipha_ ordered his men to backwater and search for two missing men. After three-quarters of an hour, the search was abandoned and both men were reported drowned. Mr. Sabin and Mr. Watson were last seen emerging from the gangway of the _Calipha_ engaged in conversation. The captain briefly saw both men struggling in the water but could not determine the details of their fight. Mrs. Watson was unable to answer questions about the incident as she was seated on the opposite side of the boat. The captain refused to answer questions from the press and ordered strangers off the ship. Mrs. Watson engaged a hotel room for the night but left Boston without revealing her destination.

Lord Sotherst mentioned that the governor is likely to have plenty of hats. Sogrange expressed concern about the size of his head in relation to the hat. Sogrange decided to send his man to fetch a selection of hats. Lord Sotherst and Sogrange discussed the timing of the first drive and whether places had been drawn. Peter Ruff entered a sitting-room to speak with John Dory. Dory was in a bad mood due to the unsuccessful chase of a car. Peter Ruff explained to Dory that his wife had visited him while she was ill and had since given up the stage.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter has never been called distinguished before. The girl expresses that living with genius can be tiresome due to its whims. Andrea, the host, receives guests in semi-darkness due to his weak eyes. Peter is a guest of Mademoiselle Celaire and has not met anyone else at the gathering. Mademoiselle Trezani is a famous singer at Covent Garden. General Noseworthy is a soldier just back from India. The last guest announced is Colonel Mayson.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Lenora is in hiding and has taken a lodging in the Servants' Club. Quest is anxious about Lenora and is trying to communicate with her through a wireless instrument. Lenora reports that she was seized outside a garage and is now in an attic room with no window except a skylight. Food is pushed through a locked door in the room where Lenora is being held. Quest is waiting for Craig, believing he is the key to reaching Lenora. Quest observes Craig entering the club and hears a conversation about beans from South America. Quest positions himself behind the kitchen door to overhear Craig's conversation.

A great storm is gathering, indicating impending conflict. Germany is arming itself in response to perceived threats from England. Germany feels jealousy towards England due to its colonial successes. There is a belief that a war with England is likely to occur. The first conflict is expected to take place in Africa, specifically the Transvaal. Germany seeks new territories to alleviate overpopulation and strengthen its nation. The Ambassador believes that the price for negotiations will be reasonable if the statements made are fulfilled.

Wolfenden expressed a need to excuse himself from the conversation. Harcutt is a journalist described as a dilettante and hard worker. Densham is identified as a painter known for his talked-about picture in the Academy. Mr. Sabin and his niece are avoiding new acquaintances during their stay in England. Wolfenden felt disturbed by Densham's expression, suspecting he knew more about the situation. The girl appeared innocent and proud, unaware of Wolfenden's scrutiny. Wolfenden offered to introduce the girl to Densham, but Mr. Sabin declined the offer.

Foo Cha was directed to show a visitor in. Mr. Sabin received his visitor standing and appeared pale. The visitor was a thick-set man with dark eyes and a closely-cropped black beard. The visitor informed Mr. Sabin that a report claimed he had developed a scheme for the conquest of the country. The visitor stated that the papers were to be burnt and the appliances destroyed, and that Mr. Sabin was to leave England within two months. Mr. Sabin expressed a desire to appeal the decision, but the visitor stated it was the order of the High Council and there was no appeal. The visitor suggested that Mr. Sabin's life's work should be with them.

Bernadine and Violet discuss instructions from her husband. Violet leads Bernadine to the study, which is initially dark. The Baron de Grost is waiting in the study, dressed in a smoking jacket. Bernadine expresses anger upon realizing he has been outmaneuvered. The Baron de Grost explains how he escaped and arrived before Bernadine. The Baron de Grost reveals that he had men concealed in the warehouse. The Baron de Grost mentions he has an independent entrance to the study.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Wolfenden inquired about Felix's nationality. Felix suggested that it might be better for Wolfenden not to know his nationality. Wolfenden expressed disbelief that intrigue exists in their country. Felix argued that international tensions create an environment for intrigue. Felix mentioned that Mr. Sabin is involved in an intrigue against England. Wolfenden stated that England is not part of any Continental alliances. Felix claimed that Germany detests England.

The Duchesse decided to come to America of her own will. Bernadine and the Prince would have remained in their own country without the Duchesse's arrival. The Prince was observed walking on the deck, absorbed in thought. Sirdeller was seated in a stripped-down royal suite, appearing aged and shrunken. The Duchesse and others were present in the room with Sirdeller. Sirdeller announced that everyone must leave in two minutes if the story took longer to tell. Peter stated that Sirdeller promised to assist the Prince of Marsine in transforming Spain into a republic.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter and Sogrange discussed the necessity of deciding who would carry out a task. Sogrange mentioned that a meeting of the executive council had occurred the previous night. Sogrange expressed concern about the loyalty of their subordinates in Paris, which was in turmoil. Peter revealed that he had never killed a human being before this conversation. Sogrange suggested that they decide who would act by tossing a coin. The coin toss resulted in Peter being chosen to strike the blow against Bernadine. Sogrange informed Peter that Bernadine was on a train that had been stopped outside the Gare du Nord.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Wolfenden expressed discomfort under Dr. Wilmot's gaze. Lady Deringham left the room to try to keep Wolfenden's father away from the library. Wolfenden stated that he only knew the central idea of his father's work regarding the navy and coast defenses. Dr. Wilmot indicated he had not taken an interest in naval matters over the past ten years. Wolfenden noted that his father had changed and avoided discussing his work. The study contained a round table piled with books, papers, maps, charts, nautical instruments, and models of men-of-war. Dr. Wilmot read through the freshly written pages of Wolfenden's father's work with great interest.

Bernadine hosts Peter, Baron de Grost, and Marquis de Sogrange as guests. Bernadine expresses animosity towards Peter and views him as an obstacle to his goals. Bernadine indicates that both men are prisoners and their removal is necessary for his plans. The Baroness, present during the conversation, faints in response to the situation. Bernadine's servants ensure that no one, except him, is armed in the house. Peter realizes that his pocket has been picked and he is unarmed. Peter loses his temper during the conversation.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Marquis de Sogrange expressed surprise upon learning that a servant had a forged recommendation. Peter Ruff informed Sogrange that the servant was a dangerous thief. John Dory and Peter Ruff handed over their captive to two policemen. Peter Ruff demonstrated how the theft was executed by removing a tampered hardwood square. Dory returned with a peculiar weapon and a fishing-rod fitted with an iron hand. Peter Ruff explained that the theft was simple and credited Dory for being on the right track. Sogrange expressed regret for introducing the thief to the house, believing the references were forged.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The letter is from Maud to Peter Ruff, dated March 10th. Maud has left her husband John and is now working in the chorus at the Frivolity Theatre. Peter Ruff feels little pleasure at Maud's invitation to meet after the show. Peter Ruff attends the show and observes Maud in the chorus, noting her lack of ability and transformation. Maud greets Peter Ruff warmly after the show and suggests going to supper. During supper, Maud expresses her dissatisfaction with her previous life and her husband. Peter Ruff feels displeased with himself and Maud's new demeanor during their supper.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: A Frenchman committed suicide in a furnished flat on Shaftesbury Avenue. Two foreigners were deported without trial for being suspected persons. One witness at the inquest stated that the deceased was a famous French criminal. Peter received a signet ring and a telegram from Sogrange congratulating him. Sogrange and Peter were traveling by sea, discussing their comfort and the weather. Peter expressed discomfort about being called away abruptly and mentioned his wife Violet. Peter stated that he is always seasick and dislikes the smell of mutton broth on the ship.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Sirdeller will have received a duplicate message regarding the final report of the works in Havana Harbor. The Maine was sunk by a torpedo discharged at close quarters underneath her magazine. The House of Brangaza is reported to be ruined. Sirdeller came abroad last year for twelve months' travel and took a great house in San Sebastian. Sirdeller was treated poorly by customs officers on the Spanish frontier and was forced to pay a large sum. Sirdeller moved to Nice after expressing his dislike for Spain and its government. Marsine is expected to return to Spain with unlimited credit to establish a republic.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Richardson claimed that no two men had been present and that the master dragged the chest out himself. Richardson reported that he was shot at by the master, with one bullet grazing his temple. The Countess secured the master's revolver and locked it in her drawer. Wolfenden suggested reloading the revolver with blank cartridges. Lady Deringham expressed concern that Blatherwick might leave due to the stressful work environment. Blatherwick's work was described as wasted and purposeless, consisting of tangled figures and calculations. Denvers had previously encouraged Blatherwick and wrote him a friendly letter about his work.

Wolfenden arrived at King's Cross at a quarter to twelve. He purchased a ticket, the _Field_, and a sporting novel at the bookstall. Wolfenden noticed Mr. Sabin's niece seated alone in a first-class carriage. The carriage was marked as engaged, and a maid and guard were present. Wolfenden asked to join her in the carriage just before the train's departure. The maid expressed suspicion about Wolfenden's presence but was dismissed by the girl. Wolfenden brought a collection of magazines and papers to the carriage.

Quest and Craig are in a building that is on fire. Craig initially refuses to provide information about Lenora. Quest retrieves a crude fire escape to help them escape the fire. Craig descends using the fire escape but the rope is burned through by flames. Craig successfully grabs onto telegraph wires after the rope fails. The crowd below assists Craig after he reaches the ground. Quest searches for Craig after the fire engines and police arrive.

Lenora was thrown into the stream when the bridge collapsed beneath her weight. Quest jumped into the stream to rescue Lenora after the bridge collapsed. Craig watched Quest struggle to bring Lenora to safety from the opposite bank. One of the wooden pillars of the bridge had been sawn completely through. Craig was in Mexico and expressed a desire to bring him back. Inside the saloon, there were cowpunchers, dancers, and music being played. A girl named Marta refused to dance with a man named José due to his drunkenness.

The conversation takes place in New York between Mr. Quest and a Professor. Mr. Quest is recognized for his contributions to science. The Professor expresses admiration for Mr. Quest's methods. The Professor discusses an anthropoid ape skeleton he sent to the museum. The Professor claims his skeleton will support Darwin's theory. Mr. Quest is invited to examine the skeleton before it is publicly displayed. The Professor expresses disappointment in Mr. Quest's lack of interest in his work.

The girl wore the dress of the Salvation Army. Her name is Miss Quigg. Miss Quigg asked Quest for a subscription to their funds. Quest agreed to make a donation and asked her to return the next day. The Professor expressed admiration for Miss Quigg's dedication to her work. The Professor donated five hundred dollars under the pseudonym 'Black Box.' Miss Quigg felt happy about the impact of the donation.

Peter Ruff reflects on his feelings of envy towards families and their gatherings. Violet advises Peter Ruff that he needs to prepare for a meeting with Sir Richard Dyson. Sir Richard Dyson arrives dressed with perfect taste and wearing violets in his buttonhole. Sir Richard Dyson expresses that he wants to discuss a man he wishes were dead. Sir Richard Dyson reveals his past involvement with a man named Ted Jones, whom he helped financially. Peter Ruff acknowledges the truth in Sir Richard's statement about giving money to those in need. Sir Richard Dyson describes a confrontation with Ted Jones after refusing to give him more money.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Craig expressed a desire to go to New York to settle his sister Mary's future and make a full disclosure. Jim reassured Craig that he was safe and did not have to leave immediately. Craig decided he must go to New York to meet his sister's child. Marta warned Craig that two men were planning to board a train to New York to find him. Marta urged Craig not to go to New York and offered to hide with him. José attacked Marta with a knife, injuring her before being shot by Long Jim. Long Jim advised Craig to leave the saloon quickly after the shooting incident.

The protagonist was a house-maid suspected of theft and was kept locked up. The protagonist's sister, Muriel, went to America the previous week. The protagonist felt she had nowhere to go after being released. Lady Deringham did not support the protagonist and treated her coldly. The protagonist wrote a letter to Wolfenden, but he did not respond. Wolfenden decided to help the protagonist after realizing her situation. Wolfenden instructed Selby to take the protagonist to his wife's vacant rooms.

Mr. Blatherwick agreed to stay until after Thursday after being offered fifty pounds by Lord Wolfenden. A carriage arrived at the front door while Mr. Blatherwick and Lord Wolfenden were in the smoking room. Lady Deringham entered the room with a card and an open letter, seeking Lord Wolfenden's advice. Lady Deringham mentioned that a gentleman named Mr. Franklin Wilmot had arrived and was a complete stranger to her. Mr. Franklin Wilmot is a famous physician known for his expertise in cases of partial mania. Dr. Whitlett sent a letter with Mr. Wilmot, requesting that he see Lord Deringham. Wolfenden and Lady Deringham found it unusual for Mr. Wilmot to call at that time for a medical consultation.

Peter and Sogrange are in front of a tall, gloomy house on 100th Street. The surroundings are described as squalid with few passers-by. Their guide opens a door with a Yale key, leading them into a dark house. The interior of the house is well-furnished with lamps, a carpeted floor, and signs of feminine occupation. A group of at least a dozen men enters the room through hidden doors. Philip Burr introduces himself as their spokesman and reveals that their guide has been instructed to bring them there. Burr prefers not to know the identities of Peter and Sogrange.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Violet expresses concern about losing Peter. De Grost believes that modern conflicts are more intellectual than physical. Violet fears Bernadine, who has not forgiven De Grost for outsmarting him. De Grost describes Bernadine as a man who has evaded capture despite numerous attempts. A man named Charles, who is De Grost's servant, delivers a note to him. The note was delivered by a messenger in a taxicab about ten minutes prior.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The narrator decided to show appreciation to a long-time associate by purchasing a house for his parents. The house was an ordinary framework structure of moderate size, in poor repair, and showing signs of neglect. The Inspector, French, had half-a-dozen men monitoring the house for the past twenty-four hours. A concealed cupboard with a telephone was discovered in the house. The telephone was used an hour ago from a call office, indicating someone was in the house. Quest decided to search the front room on the first floor before taking further action. Quest fired his revolver into the floor, prompting a man named Craig to emerge from a hidden space.

The Professor expressed appreciation for his own wit regarding a previous attack on Mr. Quest. Quest stated that French, a detective, made an error in believing Quest guilty. The Professor inquired about Craig and noted that the _Durham_ was almost due. Quest provided the Professor with a cablegram related to Craig's situation. The Professor revealed that Craig's family had served the Ashleigh family for hundreds of years. The Professor produced a historical volume belonging to his brother, Lord Ashleigh, detailing the Craig family's history. Quest and the Professor discussed Craig's father, Silas Craig, who was executed for murder in 1867.

Inspector French informed Quest about a curious object found near the Professor's grounds. The object was described as a finger from the Professor's skeleton. The bone was discovered approximately twenty yards from a gate leading into the Professor's grounds. Quest decided that the discovery of the bone near the Professor's house could not be a coincidence. Quest and his assistants planned to search the Professor's grounds after discovering the bone. The gate to the Professor's grounds was locked and unusually high. Quest used a special instrument to unlock the gate.

Rheinholdt, her son, the butler, and the Professor were the only occupants of the conservatory. The quickest way to reach Mayton Avenue from the back part of the house is through the conservatory. Mrs. Rheinholdt stated that the servants might occasionally use the conservatory exit, but not on nights when she is receiving. The butler informed that he suggested to the Professor's servant, Mr. Craig, that he could use the conservatory exit. The butler was unaware if Mr. Craig followed his suggestion, as he left shortly after the butler provided him with refreshment. The Professor described Mr. Craig as the best servant and too devoted to consider leaving his service. The butler reported that Mr. Craig left the kitchen when there was only one person present and closed the door behind him.

The woman raised her veil and asked Mr. Sabin if it made a difference. She informed Mr. Sabin that she received a cablegram from Mr. Watson. The cablegram indicated that Mr. Watson had been pardoned and reinstated. The woman was asked to join Mr. Watson in Germany and marry him. Mr. Sabin advised the woman to accept the marriage proposal. Mr. Sabin expressed regret over his own missed chance at happiness. A servant delivered a cablegram to Mr. Sabin signed by Felix.

The text includes works by various authors, including Annie Hamilton Donnell, Katherine Cecil Thurston, and George Barr McCutcheon. Annie Hamilton Donnell's work focuses on the heart tragedies of a little girl. Katherine Cecil Thurston's story, 'The Fly on the Wheel,' portrays the spirited Hibernian character. George Barr McCutcheon's 'The Man from Brodney's' features an island setting with a hero and a princess. Joel Chandler Harris's 'Told by Uncle Remus' continues the adventures of Uncle Remus and Brer Rabbit. Margaret Deland's 'Dr. Lavendar's People' and 'Old Chester Tales' depict life in a quaint old town. Elizabeth Miller's works, 'The Yoke' and 'Saul of Tarsus,' are set against historical biblical backdrops.

Mr. Sabin believes that a copy of certain figures is necessary. The girl describes the man they are discussing as mad and mentions various security measures he has taken. Mr. Sabin cannot spare the girl for a month as he needs her assistance. The girl expresses her disinterest in returning to her family and describes them as involved in farming. Mr. Sabin offers the girl a cheque for one hundred pounds to rejoin her family in one week. The girl declines Mr. Sabin's invitation to supper, citing his niece as a reason. Mr. Sabin indicates that he has no time for leisure until his work is completed.

Peter addressed a group regarding a financial transaction involving Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge and the Turkish Government. Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge loaned one and a half million pounds to the Turkish Government on questionable security. Peter stated that the security for the loan consisted of two battleships and a cruiser being built by Shepherd & Hargreaves in Belfast. Peter claimed to have paid two hundred thousand pounds for the ships and held the shipbuilder's receipt. The Turkish Government had not paid the second installment for the ships, allowing the shipbuilders to sell them. Bernadine acknowledged that Major Kosuth would return the letters of credit to Peter's friend. Peter and Bernadine discussed the potential future of warfare and enmities between nations.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest informed the Professor that no one else was in the room. The Professor appeared pale and unnerved but regained composure after drinking wine. The Professor expressed a desire to leave his current location and accompany Quest to his rooms. The Professor revealed that Craig had forged a page from the Medical Journal and had blackmailed him for years. Lenora suggested using the Electro-thought transference apparatus to read the Professor's mind, claiming he was lying. Quest acknowledged Lenora's concern and allowed her to retrieve the apparatus.

De Grost represents a secret power that aims to bring closer together Hagon's country and Great Britain. Hagon has decided to refuse De Grost's request for information. Hagon possesses a means of instant death that he does not use due to his love for one person. De Grost is taken aback by Hagon's refusal and acknowledges that he cannot spare him from more powerful forces. Violet, De Grost's wife, is aware of the situation and suggests that Bernadine may try to use Hagon's infatuation with a woman. Bernadine has recognized Hagon and is cautious about approaching him. Madame Hagon is ushered into Bernadine's apartments the following afternoon.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mr. Sabin and Knigenstein engage in a heated conversation regarding loyalty and betrayal. Knigenstein accuses Mr. Sabin of being bribed by Russia and threatens him with violence. Mr. Sabin denies any dealings with Lobenski and claims a greater power has intervened. Knigenstein acknowledges the significance of a red mark that Mr. Sabin points out. Mr. Sabin reveals that he has connections to Russia through his father. Knigenstein expresses despair over the situation and prepares to send a telegram. Mr. Sabin offers Knigenstein a chance for glory and fame if he holds to their agreement.

Admiral, the Earl of Deringham, was seized with a fit while alone in his study. Dr. Bond of Harley Street was summoned for a consultation regarding Lord Deringham's condition. Lord Deringham was a leading authority on fleet and coast defenses and was working on an important project at the time of his seizure. Mr. Sabin claimed that Lord Deringham was mad and had been for years, but he insisted he had nothing to do with the admiral's illness. Helène expressed concern about the treatment of Lord Deringham and accused Mr. Sabin of being reckless. Mr. Sabin stated that he had a personal pledge from the German Emperor and that a compact would be concluded the next day. Helène declared her intention to withdraw from marrying Henri, the direct heir to the throne.

The youth is in financial distress, having only two shillings and owing for petrol. The elder man gives the youth a bundle of notes and mentions future earnings from royalties. The group drinks homemade wine at a tiny inn before the elder man brings out a gold-foiled bottle of champagne. The youth sets fire to a barn to prevent it from being discovered, believing he has been watched. The youth claims to have the plans for building another flying machine in his pocket. The youth becomes senseless in the car after expressing excitement about the future. The elder man and another man prepare to dispose of the youth's body as they hear a car approaching.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Peter is interested in a Turkish loan. Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge is skeptical about the security of the loan. Peter represents a company that is not well-known. Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge plans to conclude the loan transaction in a week. Peter requests Mr. Heseltine-Wrigge not to inform Count von Hern about his visit. Peter invites Mr. and Mrs. Heseltine-Wrigge to dinner at the Carlton. The dinner party is successful and the topic of Peter's visit is avoided.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The cowboys began their meal after the cook served stew. Long Jim criticized the cook's stew and flicked a biscuit at him. Long Jim's horse suddenly started, causing him to injure his arm. The cook helped Jim by resetting his dislocated arm. Jim expressed gratitude to the cook for fixing his arm. Craig observed the cowboys and began to clean up after the meal. Craig played the violin for the cowboys, who appreciated his music.

The Inspector and Mrs. Rheinholdt arrived at Quest's house in a car. The Inspector rang the doorbell multiple times but received no answer. The Inspector found a fragment of white embroidery with stains caught in the door. The Inspector used a pass-key to open the door and entered the house. Inside, the Inspector discovered the bodies of the secretary-valet and Miss Quigg. Mrs. Rheinholdt entered the room and expressed shock upon seeing the scene. Quest arrived at the house with the Professor and Craig, and was visibly disturbed by the situation.

Mr. Sabin hit a golf ball seventy yards further than a professional player. Mr. Sabin is scratch at three clubs and plus four at one. Mr. Sabin was four up and three to play at the fifteenth hole. Mr. Sabin holds the record for fifteen holes at sixty-four strokes. Mrs. Peterson, who is Mr. Sabin's former acquaintance, has lived in America for six years. Mrs. Peterson's husband has been dead for four years. Mr. Sabin expressed feelings of exile and failure upon meeting Mrs. Peterson.

Mr. Watson expressed surprise at Mr. Sabin's perception of nationality based on appearance. Mr. Sabin noted that nationality does not always correlate with complexion or size. Mrs. Watson appeared at dinner in a black and white outfit and was seated next to Captain Ackinson. Mrs. Watson expressed her displeasure with the yacht _Mayflower_ and preferred the current setting. Mr. Watson did not treat his wife with the expected consideration of American husbands. Mrs. Watson invited Mr. Watson to walk on deck, but he declined and chose to smoke instead. Mr. Sabin observed the interactions between Mr. and Mrs. Watson and noted their dynamics.

Quest slept well despite his unusual surroundings. A man-servant brought Quest his clothes and a small china tea set. Quest was informed that breakfast would be served at nine o'clock. Quest found a small black box containing a warning message in his satchel. The message warned Quest that he would fail and that there was danger for him in the country. Quest considered the safety of Lenora and dismissed the idea of her being in danger. The atmosphere in the breakfast-room was cheerful despite Quest's sense of foreboding.

The subject of the conversation is a man who is copying his work by hand. The man expresses concern about Duchesne, a spy and adventurer, potentially discovering his work. Dr. Whitlett believes the man will never recover from his condition and may lose more. Wolfenden observes his father during dinner and notes his outward appearance and demeanor. Wolfenden's father refrains from drinking claret, citing the need for a clear head for writing. Mr. Blatherwick enters the smoking-room and discusses a letter he received, which he believes is a practical joke. Mr. Blatherwick is described as a young man with clerical aspirations who suffers from chronic biliousness.

Quest tore a card and a box to pieces and drew a revolver from his pocket. Quest ordered the girls to leave him to finish things up. Quest observed a dark shape emerge from the thick growth near Craig's tent. A wild scream of horror was heard, and Quest fired his revolver and ran. The Professor believed a lion had visited the camp based on the commotion. Quest claimed that the creature had killed Craig and that he had seen Craig come out of his tent. Feerda urged Craig to listen to her and suggested that he could return with them to the countries he knew nothing of.

Mr. Sabin has been using a room as a dressing-room. Mrs. Watson and Mr. Watson have taken the room that Mr. Sabin uses. Mr. Sabin expressed annoyance about the situation. The captain was walking with Mrs. Watson on deck. Mr. Sabin observed Mrs. Watson glancing at him while walking with the captain. Mr. Sabin suspected that Mrs. Watson and Mr. Watson were secret agents of the German police. Mrs. Watson reproached Mr. Sabin for not rescuing her from the captain.

The Captain was alone in his room with a chart and compasses when Quest and Harris arrived. Quest reported to the Captain that they had searched the ship thoroughly without finding the man they were looking for. Laura claimed to have seen Craig board the steamer in Southampton Harbour. The Captain expressed his intention to speak with Laura about her claims. Laura insisted that Quest and Harris had been fooled in their search for Craig. The Captain's steward confirmed that the search had covered every possible hiding place on the ship. The Captain concluded that the man they were seeking was not on his ship and suggested that Laura keep her suspicions to herself.

Bernadine is deceased. The speaker claims to have been faithful to Bernadine while he was alive. The speaker expresses a sense of freedom now that Bernadine is dead. Sogrange acknowledges the potential value of the documents mentioned by the speaker. The car arrives at a well-lit brownstone house. The Baroness is hungry and requests to take care of her guests until she is ready. Sogrange and Peter suspect the Baroness may have ulterior motives.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Professor snatched an anklet from a girl's ankle and examined it closely. The anklet is a collector's item that the Professor needed to complete his collection of Assyrian gold ornaments. The Professor recognized the anklet as having the double mark of the Pharaohs. The group expressed relief when the Professor began to speak in his natural voice after leaving the street. The camel drivers and guides were sitting together, chattering excitedly after finishing their supper. Laura and Lenora decided to get a drink from the waterbottles. Hassan, the dragoman, collapsed after drinking from a cup offered by Laura.

Quest ordered Craig to turn around and mount the stairs. Quest threatened Craig with an automatic pistol. Craig was previously locked in a garage by a girl named Lenora. Quest stated that he was sending a message to Lenora about Craig's situation. Craig expressed defiance, claiming that Quest could not force him to speak. Quest indicated that he would extract information from Craig despite his resistance. Craig fell into a stupor and was later revived by Quest with water.

Laura is mentioned in a conversation between Lenora and Quest. French reported finding Lenora in an empty house on Gayson Avenue. Quest stated that he was an escaped prisoner. Quest recounted an incident where he was attacked by two thugs who stole his automobile. The Sheriff confirmed Quest's account regarding the stolen automobile. Quest's chauffeur provided a specific time of eleven-ten when a tire blew out. Professor Ashleigh expressed his congratulations to Quest for proving his innocence.

Craig was waiting for the Professor while driving him in his automobile. Lenora questioned Craig about why he was not waiting downstairs. The Professor expressed disappointment over the lack of progress in solving the mystery of the disappearance of a skeleton and Mrs. Rheinholdt's necklace. Quest informed the Professor that there were no clues to report regarding the case. Lenora mentioned that Craig was listening at the door and was in a state of panic. Quest noted that Craig was present at the Rheinholdts' house the night of the robbery. Inspector French had been monitoring Craig since the night of the robbery.

Bernadine has promised to go with a friend to look at some polo ponies. The gallery featuring Japanese prints is closed until Monday. Bernadine and Baron de Grost engage in conversation at a restaurant. De Grost expresses a preference for coffee and cigarettes over lunching with a woman. Bernadine suggests that they should work together regarding a mutual interest in a certain individual. De Grost is cautious about forming an alliance with Bernadine. The two men observe two people of interest sitting in a corner of the restaurant.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: A pillar of marble fell and buried Bernadine beneath masonry. Peter narrowly escaped being struck by the falling debris. The house was collapsing, accompanied by loud noises and flames. The Baroness reported losing her belongings and claimed she had no companion. Peter insisted on returning to help others still in the house. Sogrange informed Peter that Bernadine was beyond hope. Peter declared his retirement from their world following Bernadine's death.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Quest is uncertain about the evidence against him. Laura expresses urgency in locating Craig. Quest instructs Laura to call the guard. Quest convinces the warder to enter the cell. Laura changes her clothes quickly at Quest's command. Quest leaves the prison and arrives at Georgia Square at five minutes to three. Quest finds the garage empty and discovers a handkerchief he recognizes.

Monsieur de Lamborne is a tall, slight man with large features, hollow eyes, thin gray hair, and a pointed gray beard. Monsieur de Lamborne received important papers from his Government that he is to hand over to the Foreign Minister the next morning. Bernadine has undertaken to send a copy of the document's contents to Berlin by the next night's mail. The letter from Bernadine states that a verbatim copy of the document will be sent to Berlin without fail. The English Government has asked how many army corps they should place at France's disposal and where they should be concentrated in case of a simultaneous attack by Germany. Monsieur de Lamborne plans to secure the document in a safe at the Embassy and watch over it until morning. Monsieur de Lamborne expresses concern about Bernadine's attempt to send the letter and invites De Grost to share his vigil.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The Professor gazed at an empty box and remarked that nothing was left except the smell. Quest, a criminologist, and Lenora entered the room where the Professor was present. The Professor introduced Quest to Mr. Francis, the curator of the museum. Quest examined the box with a magnifying glass and asked the curator a few questions. Lenora used a foot-rule to measure footprints in the garden as directed by Quest. Lenora returned with a small object identified by the Professor as the little finger of his ape. A newspaper headline announced the escape of a convicted prisoner named Macdougal.

Peter Ruff dismissed another partner and requested to see two individuals again. Ruff was informed that Count von Hern had not yet been found. A young American and his partner found a secluded seat in the ballroom vestibule. The young woman was engaged in conversation while playing with a string of pearls. Lady Mary identified Count von Hern, who was conversing with Jermyn and another companion. Ruff approached Count von Hern to discuss a mistaken exchange of programmes. Ruff noted that Count von Hern had four dances with the Countess and no dances reserved after the twelfth.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Louise begged Guillot to promise not to hurt a young man. Guillot ordered Louise to return to her rooms for her own safety. Guillot entered a room and closed the door behind him. Peter, Baron de Grost, arrived and revealed he had won a bet against Guillot. Guillot was surprised to see two men in plain clothes waiting in the room. Peter informed Guillot that the young man he was after was on his way back to his country home. Guillot admitted defeat and took his leave while holding a revolver to his temple.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The two men lunched at Sherry's and drove in Central Park. Sogrange expressed that they would have a pleasant week with a unique experience. Sogrange received a collection of cards and notes inviting him and Peter to various social events. Sogrange noted that the invitations required responses and visits to be returned. Peter informed Sogrange that reporters were waiting downstairs for an interview. Sogrange welcomed the reporters and introduced himself and Peter. Sogrange stated that the purpose of their visit was to go to Mexico for business related to mining properties.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: Mademoiselle Celaire approached Peter and took his arm. Peter informed Mr. Andrea Korust that Colonel Mayson was genuine and that their English military aeronaut had shared all his knowledge with Maurice Korust. Mr. Von Tassen commented on the differences between the current location and New York. Sir William Bounderby requested Peter to change his shooting stand for the day. Mr. Portal arrived in a motor-car with Major Kosuth and Count von Hern. Major Kosuth is a high-ranking diplomat from the young Turks and attended as a spectator. Count von Hern and Peter de Grost exchanged greetings during the gathering.

source.author: Edward Phillips Oppenheim
source.title: Peter Ruff and the Double Four

text: The woman is going to a house near Cromer that her uncle has taken. Her uncle is devoted to golf and believes Norfolk is the proper county for it. The woman expresses a lack of interest in games and prefers riding and archery. She identifies as a Frenchwoman and expresses a preference for Paris over England. Mr. Sabin intended to accompany her but was delayed by an important matter. The man and the woman discover that they are both traveling to Cromer. The woman's uncle does not want her to make acquaintances in England.
