Aline described an encounter with a man named Thomas Fletcher who was looking for his runaway wife. Fletcher arrived in a wagon with another man and confronted Aline aggressively. Aline claimed to be the sister of the person Fletcher was looking for, but he did not believe her. Fletcher threatened to harm his wife and Aline felt frightened during the encounter. Jasper later intervened and confronted Fletcher, ultimately physically assaulting him. Aline expressed gratitude to Jasper for his actions against Fletcher. Jasper advised Aline to inform him if Fletcher or anyone else threatened her in the future.

Deringham observes a blue lake and a white peak in the valley. Dark pines surround the lake and diminish in size up the hillside. A sawmill is located beside the river, producing blue smoke. A substantial square log-house is situated some distance from the lake. Sleek cattle are present in a corral, and yellowing oats are fenced off. Deringham and his daughter discuss their unknown relative, who is a rancher. They find the log-house unwelcoming and in disarray upon entering.

The narrator and others worked through a sudden thaw while staying in a shanty filled with steaming garments. The narrator felt gloomy despondency but was motivated by thoughts of Grace and the loyalty of his companions. Spring arrived, bringing warm winds from the Pacific and flowers to the mountain region. A man named Calvert approached the narrator, seeking help to escort two ladies into the Lonsdale valley. Calvert expressed concern about the safety of the trails and the condition of the ponies offered by the Indians. The narrator agreed to assist Calvert, as they had been waiting for materials and needed a change. Upon reaching the station settlement, the narrator recognized Miss Carrington and Grace among the new arrivals.

Appleby aligned himself with the Sin Verguenza to avoid capture by the Spaniards. Appleby earned the rank of Teniente through his daring actions and counsel. Harper joined the Sin Verguenza due to strict coastal surveillance preventing his escape. Appleby had feelings for Violet Wayne, who was his best friend's sweetheart. The Sin Verguenza previously received hospitality in Santa Marta before being attacked by cazadores. Colonel Morales was responsible for the harsh treatment of those who could not escape during the attack on Santa Marta. Appleby and his comrades planned to enter Santa Marta despite the presence of two companies of cazadores.

Alice Deringham entered a room where her father, Deringham, was sitting still before a table. Deringham did not respond when Alice called out to him and appeared huddled together. Forel, who was with Alice, urged her to leave the room after she expressed horror at her father's condition. Forel removed a recent impression from a blotting-pad and disposed of the contents of a wineglass before calling for a doctor. The doctor later confirmed that Deringham died from heart disease. Forel speculated that Deringham may have had a quarrel with Hallam, which could have contributed to his death. Alton visited Forel to inquire about Deringham's sudden death and learned that Hallam had seen Deringham shortly before his passing.

Appleby is waiting for Morales, who is expected to arrive in one to two hours. Appleby experiences growing tension while waiting and listens to Harper's footsteps above. Harper returns after searching for Pancho and expresses frustration at not finding him. Harper mentions that a sergeant has moved his men closer to their location. Morales arrives with several cazadores and proposes a course of action to Appleby. Appleby declines Morales' proposal, leading Morales to place Appleby and Harper in custody. Appleby and Harper are instructed to go down the stairway under the supervision of the sergeant.

The narrator expresses relief at not leaving a companion with wild men in a city. The narrator and companions arrive at a chalet hotel that is not yet completed. The narrator reflects on the contrast between their previous hardships and the comforts of the hotel. Alice, a companion, appears to be unwell and mentions the narrator's uncle usually sleeps in the afternoon. Alice discusses the narrator's sister Aline, who is teaching and appears unhappy. Alice suggests that the narrator could help Aline, who is struggling financially. The narrator feels guilt for not considering Aline's situation while focusing on personal plans.

A man ran down the road and informed Maccario that it was one company only. Maccario expressed that if the company saw nothing, the road would be open from there to Adeje. The men prepared their weapons as they awaited the approaching company. The company was marching carelessly in open fours, accompanied by laughter and voices. Appleby observed the company and felt a desire to warn them of the Sin Verguenza. The Sin Verguenza typically attacked at night and preferred not to engage in open conflict. The soldiers in the company were mostly young men, some still in their original uniforms.

Deringham expresses uncertainty about a man's seriousness regarding a claim. Alice Deringham reacts to her father's comments with embarrassment. Alton approaches Alice Deringham and offers his support. Alice Deringham feels pride and rejects Alton's sympathy. Alton acknowledges their relationship and expresses concern for Alice's troubles. Miss Townshead is in her father's house while he displays irritation towards her. Townshead is depicted as a resigned man, sipping coffee and feeling unsettled.

The narrator reflects on a past relationship with Geoffrey, who is distantly related to him. Geoffrey's father was a trustee for him under a will and managed his property while he was in the army. The narrator's father has expressed a desire for the narrator to marry Geoffrey. Geoffrey has invested heavily in a mine that has not yielded any ore. The narrator struggles with a promise made to Colonel Carrington regarding his relationship with Grace. Colonel Carrington is described as having a drawn and haggard appearance, indicating distress. Grace expresses that she cannot leave Colonel Carrington due to her sense of duty.

Alton is the owner of Somasco and has inherited Carnaby from his father. Deringham is unfamiliar with Alton's type of character and observes his behavior. Carnaby is described as a heavily encumbered property. Deringham expresses concern about the impact of losing Carnaby on his daughter. Alton recalls the hardships faced by women and considers the implications for Miss Deringham. Alton was searching for a silver lead in the mountains prior to the conversation. Alton has plans for Somasco that include roads, mills, and a fruit cannery.

Commander Thorne is perceived as busy by Alton. Mrs. Forel mentions that Thorne and Alton were great friends in the old country. Lieutenant Atkinson informed Mrs. Forel about Thorne's background. Thorne comes from a good family and recently inherited money. Alton feels inadequate compared to Thorne. The conversation in Forel's smoking-room shifts to shooting and fishing. Seaforth shares a story about a quiet man who faced danger while hunting.

Colonel Candotto would send messengers to Morales. Maccario stated that Candotto's men would march circumspectly and lie behind the walls of an aldea at night. Appleby and Maccario planned to assault Santa Marta soon. Tony was sleeping in the same room as Appleby. Tony expressed a desire to join the assault on Santa Marta despite Appleby's objections. Appleby intended to leave a handful of men behind to hold the hacienda. Tony had not participated in a fight before and was eager for the experience.

Seaforth and Okanagan launched a canoe at daylight. The canoe was dragged through ice and slid down a river towards a canyon. Okanagan commented on the usefulness of a man lying in the canoe. Seaforth expressed a grim understanding of their situation. The canoe moved quickly through the canyon, creating a tumult of spray and sound. Seaforth noted the height of the canyon walls above them. Okanagan instructed Seaforth to hold the canoe straight as they faced a rapid.

Alice Deringham and Seaforth are observing a scene involving the genus _bos_ from a hill. The area is characterized by great trees, a stream, and fallen timber. A steer is seen moving quickly through the underbrush, followed by two mounted figures. One of the mounted figures is a girl who is riding without a hat and has a red smear on her companion's face. The steer attempts to escape by charging into a hollow and then climbs an almost vertical slope. Miss Deringham finds the pursuit of the steer exciting and watches the riders closely. Alton, one of the riders, instructs his horse to jump clear of the thicket during the chase.

Harper mounted clumsily on a saddle. Appleby drew bridle and twisted himself round in his saddle. Santa Marta lay against the sky, with church towers rising above it. Anthony Palliser of Northrop is buried beneath a tall black cross outside the walls. Appleby and Harper decided to travel circumspectly due to divided sympathies in the region. They narrowly avoided an encounter with loyalist troops two days later. Appleby decided to buy a fishing barquillo to put to sea after learning about the delays of a small vessel with arms.

The settlers included individuals dressed in furs and deerskin, primarily of British descent. Colonel Carrington was successful in large-scale wheat-growing and had a bold approach to farming. Colonel Carrington aspired to lead a British settlement and brought young Englishmen to break virgin prairie. The settlers had mixed success as farmers and occasionally harbored rumors of revolt against Colonel Carrington. Grace Carrington arrived home with a group of well-born young men who had grown into strong individuals on the prairie. Grace Carrington greeted Mr. Lorimer and invited him and his friend to upcoming festivities at Carrington. Further introductions were made by Grace Carrington in a gracious manner before she moved toward her carriage.

Mr. Harding has a daughter who was the means of sending Tony to England. Tony believes that Appleby has not told Harding the entire story regarding an incident in England. Tony expresses a desire to make amends for his past actions. Harding acknowledges Tony's efforts to make things right and expresses hope for his future. Tony has transferred ownership of Dane Cop to Appleby, stating it is rightfully his. Tony insists that Appleby must return to England to help him make peace with Violet. Appleby is hesitant about returning but understands the importance of the situation to Tony.

Appleby commanded the men to leave, resulting in quietness. Nettie fell asleep and did not hear a man come up the stairway. The man who came up had a lean face and keen blue eyes filled with anxiety. The man asked Appleby about his daughter and offered five hundred dollars for her return. Appleby confirmed that the daughter was present and suggested the man speak to her. Harding entered the room and later emerged with a wallet. Harding recounted his difficulties in escaping a mob and being detained by Morales' officer.

The narrator believes they will not be successful in the mill. The narrator intends to leave enough for a third-class passage to Winnipeg for Reggie and Aline. Martin Lorimer acknowledges the narrator's stubbornness and offers support for their departure. Minnie Lee expresses dismay at the narrator's decision to leave the mill. The narrator arrives in Winnipeg during a dismal spring afternoon. The narrator feels idle and without purpose while observing the busy citizens of Winnipeg. Martin Lorimer gives the narrator a draft for one hundred pounds on the Bank of Montreal.

The inquest on keeper Davidson was held and initially seemed to cause Tony Palliser less anxiety than expected. The Pallisers had lived at Northrop for generations, and their servants had a long history of service. Tony Palliser was known for his kind demeanor and generosity towards his staff and guests. Northrop village had formed opinions about Tony's involvement with Lucy Davidson and largely exculpated him. The coroner's inquiry revealed that the cause of death was exhaustion from immersion, not directly from the bruises. Sergeant Stitt testified to signs suggesting a scuffle but could not confirm it. Miss Wayne appeared at the inquest and answered questions with a clear, cold voice.

Alice Deringham confessed to Alton that she withheld a message from Miss Townshead. Alton expressed disbelief that Alice had kept back the message. Alice admitted that she sent a note to stop Alton from relocating the mine, intending to hurt him. Alton showed visible distress upon hearing Alice's confession. Alice felt a mix of emotions, including humiliation and confusion, regarding Alton's unwavering faith in her. Alton reassured Alice that he believed she could do no wrong. Alice insisted that her actions were driven by hatred and a desire to punish Alton.

Nellie Townshead acknowledges that Jack's decision to go up was influenced by a desire for money. Hallam has a hold on the ranch owned by Nellie Townshead's father. Nellie Townshead states that they are selling the stock due to Hallam's influence. Alton expresses concern about Hallam's intentions regarding the ranch. Nellie Townshead fears they will be sold up and driven out shortly. Alton requests that Nellie Townshead send word to him when she receives notice from Hallam. Alton feels that women complicate his plans and expresses dissatisfaction with his interactions with Miss Deringham.

Godfrey Palliser dined at Northrop Hall. Palliser asked his nephew Tony for his opinion on Bernard's innocence regarding Davidson's death. Violet Wayne expressed her belief in Bernard's innocence. Tony's views on Bernard's innocence changed since he last spoke with Palliser. Palliser noted that Tony had nothing to urge in extenuation for Bernard. Palliser expressed a wish for Tony and Violet not to wait long to be together. Tony felt a sense of degradation for having perjured himself to Palliser.

Sunlight reduced the effect of frost in the brown woods. Tony and his friends experienced a weight lifted off their minds during their time in the woods. A nut on the bush of the dog-cart's wheel slackened during the homeward journey, causing an accident. Tony and three friends had to walk home after the horse was taken to a neighboring farm. As dusk fell, Tony and Appleby reached a footbridge across the river. The men discovered a body in the water, identified as their keeper, Davidson. Appleby assisted in retrieving the body from the water after it was found.

Appleby informed Violet Wayne that Tony had done nothing wrong. Tony was found idling in an empty room instead of participating in shooting. Violet Wayne expressed concern for Tony's quiet demeanor and encouraged him to talk. Tony acknowledged having worries but downplayed their significance. Violet Wayne offered financial assistance to Tony, which he declined. Violet Wayne questioned Tony about Appleby's actions at eleven o'clock. Violet Wayne noted that others perceived Tony as someone who avoids difficulties.

The bullet was ragged and had a strip of lead torn off that was embedded in Okanagan's flesh. Seaforth expressed concern about Okanagan's injury and the effects of the cold on it. Alton was not fully conscious when he awoke due to loss of blood, fatigue, exposure, and hunger. Tom Okanagan was grinding a knife while waiting for Alton to regain consciousness. Snow began to fall during the night, increasing the cold conditions in the tent. Seaforth observed that Alton was finally sleeping restfully after a long day. The next morning, Seaforth noticed that Alton was awake and smiling.

The speaker expresses a lifelong indebtedness to another individual. An unseen person acknowledges the speaker's sentiment and mentions the potential for suspicions regarding Lorimer's benefit from a partner's death. Grace asserts that others, besides Mr. Lorimer, would benefit from Geoffrey Ormond's death. Colonel Carrington congratulates another character on a lucky escape and suggests visiting a sick man. Wilson is identified as a bachelor who deals in mining gear and has made friends with Ormond. The surgeon informs that Ormond has internal injuries with little hope of recovery. Ormond bequeaths his possessions to Ralph Lorimer in gratitude for an attempted rescue.

The narrative describes a scene involving a peon in a plaza and cazadores with rifles. The 'Maine' is mentioned as going under, with bodies surfacing in the water. Appleby reflects on leaving Morales at the cuartel and expresses a desire to meet him again. Maccario states that Morales will wait until dawn to act against the Sin Verguenza. Appleby learns that there are a section or two of troops at the hacienda. Maccario mentions the dangers of spying on the Sin Verguenza and the risks involved. Appleby and Maccario discuss the situation regarding Morales and the mutiny of a handful of men.

Alton entered the room and sat in a creaking chair. Alice Deringham was sitting in a basket chair and appeared pretty and collected. Alton expressed that spending time with Alice would not be a waste. Alice commented on the tawdriness of the surroundings and noted Alton's reaction. Alton indicated that the place had a church-like effect on him. Alice prepared coffee and noted it was different from what they had previously. Alton acknowledged he had to address some issues with the storekeeper regarding supplies.

The scene involves women with powdered faces and ragged men with rifles. Nettie Harding is described as having a white face, torn garments, and sparkling jewels. A man with dusky skin and a machete shouts, prompting laughter and causing Nettie to flee. Nettie encounters two men who speak to her in Castilian and English. Nettie inquires about the safety of the Hotel Cuatro Naciones after losing her companion. One of the men expresses concern for Nettie's safety and leads her away from a crowd. Nettie recognizes one of the men as resembling someone she met on board the 'Aurania.'

Carrington sat at the head of the table in a great oak chair. Raymond Lyle called the meeting to discuss the projected creamery. Lyle advocated for an open-door policy to attract well-educated Englishmen. Carrington questioned Lyle's commitment to the future of Carrington. Several men supported Lyle's proposal for the creamery despite Carrington's skepticism. The men expressed a desire for improved infrastructure and economic growth in Carrington. Colonel Carrington reacted with astonishment to the support for Lyle's ideas.

The landscape features tall reeds, buffalo bones, wild peppermint, and flowers among the grass. A large area of grain, including oat tassels and wheat heads, is described as extensive and impressive. The settlers work hard and often cut down rations to succeed in farming despite challenges. Ralph Lorimer and Harry Lorraine are partners in the firm of Lorimer & Lorraine, which sends wheat by special freight train. Harry is seen protecting their stock with a smudge-fire to shield cattle from mosquitoes. Grace has initiated a project to open new lands for the homeless poor, but not all beneficiaries have been grateful. Ralph Lorimer reflects on his past poverty and the efforts made to support the community and improve the colony.

Grace was the subject of concern for the speaker. Ralph Lorimer identified himself as the assistant cashier in the Orb Mill. Martin Lorimer expressed frustration over Ralph's desire to leave the mill for Canada. Martin Lorimer mentioned that Ralph's father left four hundred pounds, which has increased to five hundred under his stewardship. Martin Lorimer highlighted the educational fees for Ralph's siblings, Reggie and Aline. Ralph acknowledged Martin Lorimer's generosity towards his siblings.

Nellie Townshead and Harry Alton engage in a conversation about marriage. Nellie Townshead expresses that she cannot marry Harry Alton. Harry Alton acknowledges his unfitness and disability but still expresses a desire to make Nellie happy. Nellie Townshead indicates that there are two reasons preventing her from accepting Alton's proposal. Nellie Townshead asks Harry Alton to leave and not speak of the matter again. Harry Alton admires Nellie Townshead's courage and beauty despite her rejection. Nellie Townshead suggests that nothing Alton could say would change her decision.

The narrator did not see Grace or Colonel Carrington during the following weeks. The Day Spring shaft was reported to be a costly venture with no traces of payable milling ore found. Colonel Carrington continued to work on the Day Spring shaft, driving an adit into the range side. An informant suggested that more gold was going into the diggings than would be extracted. The narrator attempted to give Colonel Carrington advice but was met with indifference. The narrator and his partners faced various natural difficulties while working on their project. The arrival of the first train in the mining town was anticipated as a significant event in its history.

Anthony Palliser was killed in action in Santa Marta, Cuba. Hester read the telegram informing about Anthony Palliser's death. Violet expressed a desire to go home after receiving the news. Mr. Earle offered sympathy to Violet and suggested there might still be hope. The vicar agreed with Violet's belief that there was no hope left regarding Anthony Palliser. Violet preferred to be alone and declined offers for company. Bernard Appleby was in New York, finalizing a business agreement.

The conversation involves a railroad builder named Mr. Lorimer. Grace Carrington expresses concern about the financial struggles of the narrator. The narrator recounts a profitless struggle involving poor food supplies. Johnston, a partner of the narrator, is described as never grumbling. Grace Carrington acknowledges the value of loyal partners in business. Colonel Carrington has invested money in a new mine in the Lonsdale district. Grace and her father plan to live at a ranch during the summer to assist with the mine's development.

Alice Deringham observed a stranger with a fleshy face and beady black eyes. The stranger, Willard Hallam, is associated with Hallam and Vose, land and mining agents. Deringham and Hallam engaged in a conversation where Deringham expressed indifference. Alice Deringham felt a growing dislike for Hallam as she perceived similarities between him and her father. Deringham received a Colonial Journal that mentioned a missing heir related to a family quarrel in England. The article in the Colonial Journal discussed Mr. Henry Alton, who is connected to the Deringham family. The article indicated that Mr. Deringham is a distinguished London financier with dealings in the area.

The narrator expresses regret for missing Miss Carrington in the afternoon. Grace expresses pride in Ralph and mentions that better times are coming. Martin invites Ralph to visit and stay for a month. The train departs as Ralph waves goodbye and the passengers cheer. Harry suggests returning to finish the evening with stump speeches and banjo performances. The narrator spends time walking to calm down after a day of varied emotions. The next morning, the narrator finds Johnston asleep among the fragments of his broken banjo.

The Atlantic mail passed by as the characters stepped down on the track. Harry expressed a desire to be buried in the forests if they failed at Fairmead. Johnston indicated he might not return after crossing the Rockies. The camp was located beside a partly completed track in a mountainous area. The region was described as auriferous and home to a wooden town struggling for existence. Lee organized a temperance meeting outside the Magnolia saloon, inviting all to attend. Fanny Marvin was identified as a rising religious reformer who had gained attention in several towns.

Mr. Alton of Somasco is mentioned as a rancher who has taken out timber rights in the valley. Deringham believes that Alton stands between him and the Carnaby property. Deringham describes the Carnaby property as a small estate that is heavily in debt. Hallam expresses a dislike for Alton and states that he does not like anyone who gets in his way. Hallam claims that Alton has taken out a claim ahead of him for timber rights. Deringham acknowledges a past mistake regarding the Peveril property. Hallam offers to show Deringham the Tyee and other resources in the valley.

The narrator and Jasper drove to Clearwater to find an elevator that was already staffed. The manager of a new creamery was looking for a handyman to collect milk and assist with accounts. Jasper mentioned that the creamery manager was from Ontario, near the narrator's family home. The narrator and Jasper brought Thomas Fletcher from Winnipeg to work at the creamery. Fletcher appeared worn and thinner upon arrival, with signs of possible alcohol indulgence. Jasper expressed doubts about Fletcher's character and work ethic during their journey home. The narrator and Harry helped Fletcher and his family by bringing them food during the winter.

The man carrying a flour-bag was noted for his ability to carry the load lightly despite its weight of 140 lbs. Miss Deringham observed the man wearing a blue shirt and ragged overalls, with flour in his hair and a bronzed, dusty face. The stranger offered to take Miss Deringham and her belongings through in his wagon, despite it being full. Miss Deringham considered recompensing the man for his trouble but ultimately did not offer him money. The man was identified as a bush teamster, and Miss Deringham felt uncomfortable offering him a piece of silver. The teamster drove the wagon down a difficult trail while Miss Deringham enjoyed the scent of cedars and the cold wind. Their journey was interrupted when the teamster reined in the horses to allow a line of loaded ponies to pass.

Appleby experienced physical discomfort while observing a chaotic scene. A mounted officer appeared, and commands were issued amidst confusion. The Sin Verguenza engaged in combat with the cazadores, resulting in casualties. Appleby witnessed the Sin Verguenza emerge from hiding and attempted to rally with them. Harper expressed concern about finding food among the fallen mule team. Maccario informed Appleby of a lack of pesetas among the Spanish troops. Morales was reported to be marching with four companies, prompting urgency to move quickly.

Nettie Harding laid her hand on her companion's arm after a concert. Thérèse Clavier returned to obscurity after the concert on the Low Wood lawn. Nettie Harding stood beside an effigy in Northrop church while Hester Earle and Violet Wayne prepared for a harvest thanksgiving. The vicar was waiting on the chancel steps with a handful of crimson gladioli. Nettie Harding reflected on the stone face of the effigy, feeling a connection to the spirit of the chivalrous past. Nettie felt a growing desire to help Bernard Appleby after hearing Miss Clavier's story. Nettie Harding resolved to inform Violet Wayne about Tony Palliser's true character.

Harding desired a fortune to bequeath his daughter. Harding invested money in ventures in Cuba that his friends considered reckless. Harding was known for taking risks throughout his life. Morales, known as El Espada, was an officer of Spain tasked with suppressing an insurrection. Morales indicated that political information is not easily shared due to uncertainty about American sympathies. Morales described a military operation involving Americans and the Sin Verguenza. Nettie Harding showed interest in Morales' account of the military operation.

Alice Deringham is significant to Seaforth. Nellie Townshead expresses concern about Miss Deringham's punishment. Seaforth feels sympathy for Harry, who is being punished. Seaforth shares a story about a disastrous march with storekeeper Horton. Horton identifies Damer as the person who recorded Seaforth's claim. Horton plans to charge Damer with horse-stealing. Seaforth questions the implications of Horton's plan regarding Damer.

Alton observed a rapid river and a cluster of smaller trees across from him. He dropped his burdens and began to cut down a tree with an axe. After an hour, he rolled the tree to the river using skids and levers. While attempting to cross the river on the log, Alton lost a blanket and a flour-bag into the water. He decided against retrieving the flour due to the risk of going down the rapid. Alton arrived at a site marked by an excavation and a mound of rocks, which he identified as 'Jimmy's claim.' He began to work on the excavation, discovering stones of unusual gravity that suggested significant possibilities.

Alton is expected to stay for three weeks, with two weeks without pressing and one week requiring supervision. Deringham experiences impotent fury after Alton leaves and shows signs of physical distress. Deringham was advised to avoid excitement and business anxieties before departing from England. Alton is delayed in Vancouver due to important affairs and the harsh winter conditions. Alice Deringham greets Alton with reserved cordiality and believes she understands his reticence. Deringham hopes to provide a satisfactory account of his stewardship regarding Carnaby. Alice Deringham overhears a conversation about rumors that she is initially unaware of.

Lance Chisholm is introduced to Martin Lorimer, who is from Lancashire. Chisholm invites Lorimer to join him in the saloon. Lorimer is surprised by the number of drinks offered at the bar. Alice, a character in the text, has changed little and appears more delicate. Alice and her father traveled to Canada in search of the narrator. Alice's father had been ill but recovered due to his determination. Alice and her father decided to attend the opening of a new railroad line.

The girl is willing to give everything she has to offer, including her faith in the man. The man lacks the courage to test the girl's faith in him. The girl has a calm and proud demeanor, which the man finds intimidating. The man feels committed to a course of deception after the girl believes him. The girl mentions that there are men who would give up everything for a fancy. The girl expects the most from those nearest and dearest to her. The conversation between the man and the girl ends with her indicating that she could have forgiven him if he had made a confession earlier.

The speaker is Adam Lee of Stoney Clough. Adam Lee is searching for his daughter, Minnie Lee. Minnie Lee left her home to follow Ralph Lorimer. Colonel Carrington and others are present during the conversation. Harry supports the idea of allowing Ralph Lorimer to refute the charge against him. Adam Lee expresses his frustration with the wealthy and their treatment of the poor. Adam Lee identifies himself as a maker of shoes for the poor.

Geoffrey Ormond was laid to rest in Canadian soil. The expedition that led to Ormond's death was not unusual, as many who go out on the gold trail do not return. The narrator expressed a desire to return to Fairmead after Ormond's death. Colonel Carrington listened to the narrator's request with cold patience. A Winnipeg newspaper published a clipping that negatively portrayed Lorimer, the prosecutor from Fairmead. Colonel Carrington indicated that Lorimer's reputation would be a barrier to an alliance with his family. The narrator vowed to marry Miss Carrington despite Colonel Carrington's objections.

Three individuals started from Somasco, and one had already left. Alton instructed Seaforth to measure twenty paces east to a rock. Seaforth measured forty paces north with the gully over the fork of the river. Seaforth experienced a sense of depression during their journey. They encountered difficult terrain, including fern-choked forest and devil's club. After four miles, they reached an area affected by a past fire, with charred trees. A loud crash occurred when a big trunk fell nearby, causing dust to envelop them.

The text features a conversation between two characters, Violet Wayne and a stranger, about a memorial designed by a famous artist. The memorial is dedicated to Walthew Palliser, who was killed in West Africa while attempting to make peace with a rebellious tribe. Violet Wayne expresses admiration for the memorial and suggests that the angel should be placed over the effigy. Nettie Harding is introduced as a character who is enthusiastic about antiquities and is staying with another character. Nettie Harding's companion mentions that Violet Wayne has a natural repose and does not make others feel inferior. The Pallisers are described as an old family, and Violet Wayne is suggested to be proud of her connection to them. It is indicated that Violet Wayne is going to marry a member of the Palliser family.

A horse was on board a birch-bark canoe. The narrator swam away from the horse and attempted to gain the center of the river. The narrator seized a long, dark object and fell into the canoe headfirst. The river was described as frothing white with steep boiling ridges. The narrator's paddle broke while trying to push against a submerged boulder. Grace raised her hand as if in farewell, and their glances met in a moment of connection. The narrator continued to paddle despite the danger, aiming to keep the canoe upright.

Miss Deringham inquired about a ranch, but Alton clarified that Mrs. Jimmy was a bar-keep in Vancouver before marrying Jimmy. Jimmy was a trail-chopper and had little money. Alton described a tough winter spent under a glacier, where they lived on salmon and occasionally deer. Mrs. Jimmy became sick and thin but remained cheerful despite their hardships. Alton went to look for Jimmy after Mrs. Jimmy became anxious, eventually finding him dead under a pine tree. Jimmy had found silver but could not reveal its location before his death. Alton expressed more sympathy for Mrs. Jimmy than for Jimmy himself.

The rain had ceased when Tony drove Violet Wayne home from Northrop. Tony and Violet were alone in a dog-cart on a muddy road. Tony informed Violet that he had allowed Craythorne to let people build a mill on the land. Godfrey Palliser had intended the land for Appleby, which could generate revenue. Tony had not heard from Appleby since he was in Texas. Tony admitted he did not respond to Appleby because the situation was too painful. Violet felt a constraint and hesitation about hastening the wedding with Tony.

The cook shook the teapot and asked if more water was needed. Alton responded harshly to the cook's inquiry. Alice Deringham felt relieved and astonished when Alton told a whimsical story. Seaforth and Alice Deringham engaged in conversation about Alton's character. Seaforth expressed pride in Alton's attitude towards the situation. Alton planned to go to Horton's and instructed Seaforth to prepare a list of items. Seaforth noted that Alice Deringham did not drink the tea.

A reef named Los Dientes is located below the water. Harper expressed concern about the proximity of a gunboat while sailing. The crew of the Ventura was instructed to adjust sails to avoid danger. The Ventura was experiencing difficult sailing conditions with water washing over the deck. The gunboat was within easy range of the Ventura. The topmast and mainsail gaff of the Ventura fell due to strain. Harper planned to prepare a lifeboat as a potential escape option.

The surveyor addressed a group after a meal, acknowledging their work on roads and bridges. A woman expressed the community's commitment to building roads for economic improvement despite working long hours. The surveyor praised the engineering work done by the community and announced plans to take over and finish the road project. He stated that the province would pay for the work done on the road and would honor pay orders for the workers. The member present added that they would provide a better road and grants for improvements. The surveyor confirmed that a steel road would be constructed soon, eliciting a strong positive reaction from the attendees.

Violet Wayne and Tony discuss the need to show respect to someone. Violet expresses a feeling of apprehension without knowing the reason. Tony acknowledges that the recent events at Northrop have affected Violet. Violet enters Northrop church to work on an altar cloth. Violet encounters a girl admiring a marble effigy on a tomb in the church. The effigy depicts a knight kneeling with a sword, and its history is uncertain. The blue-eyed girl expresses a connection to the effigy, mentioning a man who resembled it.

Appleby and Harding discuss a business deal related to the sugar trade. Appleby expresses gratitude to Harding while taking up a document. Harding mentions a warrant out for Appleby and the difficulty of avoiding the police. Appleby plans to sail on the 'Cunarder' on Saturday. Nettie Harding is mentioned as expecting them at Glenwood. Nettie expresses confidence in her father's decision regarding Appleby. Nettie recalls a past encounter with Appleby when he was dressed in rags.

The men expressed a willingness to take chances despite having no work or resources. Contractor Lorimer assured the men that he would act fairly in their dealings. The group prepared to travel through the Rockies with their possessions in cattle-cars. Harry and Lee were traveling together on a freight train through the mountains. The surveyor indicated that the train was moving quickly to reach a side-track ahead of the west-bound mail. The narrator described the scenery as they traveled, including snow-covered peaks and polished rock slopes.

Tony Palliser did not see Violet again that night and went to bed early. Tony was awakened in the early morning by the sound of a door being opened and hurried footsteps. The Darsley doctor informed Tony that Godfrey Palliser passed away ten minutes prior. Tony Palliser stood beside a yew tree at Northrop church during Godfrey Palliser's funeral. Godfrey Palliser had taken Tony into the place of his deceased son and left all his possessions to him. Tony felt a sense of fear during the funeral service as he reflected on his relationship with Godfrey Palliser. The will read by lawyer Craythorne left Tony as the owner of the Northrop property.

Nellie Townshead felt a curious confidence in rancher Alton and his comrade. The auctioneer described the land as having the richest soil in the Dominion. A bidder at the auction was known to be in debt and likely did not have sufficient funds. Nellie Townshead expressed anger that a man she barely knew was trying to help her while her friends did not. Nellie Townshead's father, Townshead, believed the land was standing at a third of its value. Nellie Townshead asked her father where they would go if they were turned out by the purchaser. Townsend expressed concern about the prospect of having a balance after the auction.

Colonel Carrington is not addicted to changing his mind. Grace Carrington will never marry a poor man with Colonel Carrington's consent. The narrator worked and waited while Grace remained Miss Carrington. The river between the mining town and Cedar loses itself in a gloomy cañon. The cañon is difficult to navigate, with few attempts made by white men. Grace Carrington plans to spend a few days at the Lawrences' ranch. A wild shrill cry startled Grace Carrington and the narrator during their conversation.

Harry expressed frustration with Hudson's living situation and suggested he could find a better companion. Hudson expressed his dissatisfaction with his home environment and mentioned plans to leave Canada for Dakota. Harry offered to buy Hudson's property, which Hudson had been willing to sell for two years. Hudson stated that he could not sell the property until legal improvements were completed. Harry and Hudson negotiated the terms of the sale, considering the risks involved. Ralph agreed to the purchase terms proposed by Harry, despite concerns about financing. Hudson accepted a check from Ralph for the property, which included land that was not fully developed.

The narrator drove a canoe toward a fall, experiencing a deep booming sound and a heavy splash as they descended. The fall was described as being more than a fathom in height over a distance of three yards. After the fall, the narrator and Grace struggled in the stream, with the canoe taking on water and capsizing. The narrator managed to find a foothold and crawled out onto the shingle, dragging Grace with him. Grace approached the narrator while he lay on the shingle, confirming that she was unharmed. The narrator expressed gratitude for Grace's safety and acknowledged the danger they had just faced. Grace advised the narrator to sit down as he had not fully recovered from the ordeal.

Sloo is a lake formed by melting snow. Jasper's broncos were less than half-tamed and backed round in rings when re-harnessing was attempted. The scent of wild peppermint was present in the cool air during the evening. Harry and the narrator drank green tea and ate flapjacks after completing their work. The narrator had a vision of golden wheat and Grace Carrington before falling asleep. Each day at Fairmead involved similar tasks until the grain was drilled in with a borrowed seeder. Wild fowl migrated from the south to the tundra mosses beside the Polar Sea during this time.

Alton expressed regret for not having already started his journey. Alice Deringham noted that Alton's visit may be the last time they see each other. Alton mentioned that he had asked Miss Townshead to marry him, but she declined. Alton planned to return to the snow the following day to search for silver. Alton informed Forel that he briefly joined his party and addressed rumors about himself. Alton requested Forel to find Miss Townshead a job and offered to cover her salary if needed. Forel agreed to help Alton with his request regarding Miss Townshead.

The coroner requested Bernard Appleby twice, but there was no response. Sergeant Stitt entered with a telegram stating that Appleby had not resumed his duties and his whereabouts were unknown. Appleby purchased a ticket for Liverpool on the evening Davidson's body was found. The coroner noted that it was unfortunate that Appleby, an important witness, was not present. The jury concluded that the deceased died of exhaustion from a fall during a struggle with one or more persons. The coroner recorded a verdict of manslaughter by unknown persons. Northrop Hall was nearly empty as guests left due to the suspicions surrounding the case.

Deringham and his daughter observed a dripping object crawl out on the opposite side of the river. Alice Deringham commented that there is still a good deal of the beast unsubdued in her tame bear. Alton expressed regret that Alice Deringham was not pleased with him. Alice Deringham found the situation with Alton sufficiently exasperating but questioned if his actions were justifiable. Deringham intervened during Alton's altercation with a workman, which Alton appreciated. The cook brought a tray with a metal teapot, bread, condensed milk, and butter to the verandah. Alice Deringham indicated that they did not want anything else from the cook.

Appleby is faced with a decision between a life of command and the allure of the Sin Verguenza. Maccario acknowledges that it is not important whether a man is a merchant or a soldier. Appleby is preparing to leave and is recognized as a faithful comrade and valiant soldier. The men express their goodwill towards Appleby with a toast. Appleby is informed that Señor Palliser wishes to see him urgently. Appleby meets a wounded man who believes he has only a short time left to live. The wounded man, Tony, recalls an incident involving a cazador and a bayonet.

Appleby received a message from Nettie Harding before she left England. Nettie Harding indicated that there were people in England who knew the truth about Appleby. Appleby felt a sense of faith in Nettie Harding's capabilities. Appleby, along with Harper and four members of the Sin Verguenza, approached a location near Santa Marta. Appleby was concerned about the presence of Morales' cazadores near the road. Appleby had a restless feeling after receiving Nettie's message and sought excitement to distract himself. Appleby realized that Nettie Harding had likely vindicated him in Violet Wayne's eyes.

Miss Deringham expresses frustration about a man ruling at Carnaby where her mother lived. Deringham comments on the potential negative impact of the man's rule on Carnaby. Miss Deringham finds the details of the man's potential actions at Carnaby unnecessary. Miss Deringham sleeps comfortably on a bed of cedar-twigs after a night in the wagon. The wagon driver stops at a meeting point of four trails to discuss their journey. The driver informs Miss Deringham that he cannot take her directly to the settlement due to a prior commitment. Miss Deringham feels exasperated by the driver's refusal to accommodate her wishes.

Several individuals from the party shook hands with the narrator. The names mentioned by the surveyor were well-known in Winnipeg and Montreal. A procession approached the train, led by a man reading from a written paper. The locomotive pulled the first train into the wooden town amid public acclamations. Martin Lorimer appeared thinner and older, with white hair but keen eyes. Alice expressed happiness at the reconciliation between her uncle and the narrator. A railroad magnate invited the narrator to a celebration dinner on behalf of the chief.

Earle and Melton waited in another room while Mr. Appleby spoke with Craythorne. Melton offered to drive Appleby to see Miss Wayne. Appleby expressed gratitude towards Melton for his offer. Appleby visited Mrs. Wayne's drawing-room and felt anxious before Violet and her mother arrived. Violet Wayne asked Appleby to recount his experiences with Tony in Cuba. Appleby shared his memories of Cuba, detailing various scenes and events. Violet expressed gratitude to Appleby for sharing his memories of Tony.

Appleby and Harper had breakfast on the veranda. Appleby appeared weary and had a small amount of bread and coffee. Harper noted the absence of the major-domo, Pancho. Appleby sent Pancho away with a message for Maccario after a visit from Morales. Morales made a demand that Appleby could not entertain. Appleby expressed concern about the potential actions of Harper's countrymen regarding the 'Maine'. Appleby planned to take a risk due to Harding's investments in Cuba.

Horton presented a warrant for Roger Damer. Constable Andersen was instructed to put handcuffs on Roger Damer. Horton indicated that his men had enough authority to enforce the warrant. Damer did not speak to anyone during the day following his arrest. Damer suggested to Seaforth that someone would regret the situation. Seaforth believed he had identified the man they were looking for. Damer escaped during the night, leaving behind defective handcuffs.

Appleby cannot leave his current location and must see the trouble through. Tony decides to stay with Appleby instead of leaving. Tony expresses that he cannot face Violet if he leaves Appleby in peril. Appleby acknowledges that Tony's decision to stay makes sense given the circumstances. Harding agrees to give Appleby a month's leave after they take Santa Marta. Harding is preparing for a journey to Santa Marta and needs to dress in Cuban fashion. Tony insists on staying until after Santa Marta is taken, despite Appleby's objections.

Alice Deringham felt a thrill when Alton held out his hand before leaving. Alton expressed a desire to visit Alice in Vancouver upon his return. Alice agreed to Alton's proposal to visit if it would please him. Deringham commented on the influence of heredity in Alton's character. Alice questioned how long it would be before Alton returned. Ten days later, Alton was awakened by the trampling of the horses at night. Alton demonstrated an understanding of the nature of the beasts he worked with.

Tony was engaged to Violet Wayne. Davidson approached Tony for money regularly after initially receiving twenty pounds from him. Appleby advised Tony to consult a lawyer regarding his situation with Davidson. Tony was required to meet Davidson at midnight to give him thirty pounds. Appleby asked Violet Wayne for ten pounds, promising to return it the next day. Violet Wayne gave Appleby the ten pounds after initially hesitating. Appleby left the house carrying a riding crop and a key.

Hallam has sent someone to locate Alton's silver claim. Alton has not put in his legal improvements for his claim. Alton was unable to record his mineral claim within the required fifteen days. While the claim is unrecorded, anyone can jump it. Alton's inability to return to his claim due to snow has left it vulnerable. A stranger entered the room while Alton and the girl were discussing business. The stranger appeared to know the girl and was surprised by the situation.

The setting involves a smooth wall of rock that is unclimbable. Mountain streams in British Columbia rise and fall several feet daily. Streams are lowest in the early morning due to frost holding back drainage from snow-fields and glaciers. As the sun rises, the volume of the streams increases throughout the day. The characters Grace and the narrator are in a situation where rising waters threaten their safety. The narrator expresses a willingness to sacrifice his life to save Grace. The narrator confesses his love for Grace, stating he has loved her since their first conversation.

Appleby gasped and drew the trigger of his pistol, which exploded. Appleby struggled to breathe and felt his strength leaving him. Two men, whom Appleby recognized as peons from a wine-shop, stood in front of him. A man crawled out of the gutter while another man sped down the street. Civil guards arrived, one carrying a lantern and another a pistol. The peons explained to the civil guards that they had witnessed a struggle involving Appleby. Appleby confirmed the peons' account of the events leading up to the incident.

Hester expressed uncertainty about whether it would be kind to undeceive a person who is happy in deception. Nettie observed Tony as he focused on plucking a daisy from the turf. Tony suggested that it might be better to let someone continue dreaming rather than waking them to unpleasant realities. Hester pointed out that if a man were sincerely sorry for a wrong he committed, he would make reparation. Tony argued that a well-intentioned person who made a mistake might improve if left alone. Violet Wayne indicated that if the man were truly remorseful, the issue would be resolved. Nettie noted the philosophical nature of the discussion regarding whether a man can be pardoned while retaining the offense.

Seaforth and Alton are discussing a man who stands behind another man. Alton expresses determination to find out more about this man. Seaforth warns Alton about the potential danger of his actions. Alton and Seaforth are partners and friends. The text describes a wooden house that once stood on the outskirts of Vancouver City. The owner of the house was an Englishman who was hospitable to Alton. Alton is waiting for dinner with a young naval officer named Commander Thorne.

Appleby instructed Pancho to leave the light and go for Señor Harper. The major-domo, Pancho, chose to stay and asked the man what he wanted. The man mentioned he had a use for silver and referred to being unfortunate at the Casino. Appleby noted that the safe had not been tampered with and questioned the man's intentions. Pancho advised Appleby to let the man go, citing the law's troublesome nature. The man returned Appleby's stolen pistol and provided a warning about keeping valuables. Pancho observed the man entering the veranda and commented on the importance of living quietly in a turbulent country.

The work involves preparing a rail-bed that will extend to Green Lake before winter. Harry and the narrator agreed to sign a contract for grading work and additional compensation due to labor shortages. Ellsworthy Johnston, a former barrister, introduced himself and offered to become a junior partner in the grading contract. Harry and the narrator made a bargain with Johnston that evening. Harry planned to distribute their livestock among neighbors and hire workers affected by frost damage. The railroad building task commenced on a hot autumn morning with teams harnessed to scrapers for soil removal. A group of men waited near flat cars loaded with rails while a locomotive produced black smoke.

The narrator is knee-deep in slush and snow. The narrator expresses a preference for a life outside of farming. The narrator plans to complete a railroad contract before moving on. The narrator boards a first-class train with a special pass. The conductor of the train recognizes the narrator from a previous encounter. The narrator reflects on the advantages of traveling in comfort. Martin Lorimer and Alice greet the narrator at the station.

Nettie Harding expressed concern about whether Appleby could assist her. Morales arrived while Appleby and Nettie were discussing the campaign. Appleby shared details about an incident at the hacienda but withheld information about certain papers. Morales suggested using a pistol in future confrontations, indicating a lack of tolerance. The banker asked Appleby to deliver a letter to a captain for posting in America. The banker advised Appleby to exercise discretion regarding the letter's contents. Appleby noticed footsteps behind him while leaving the banker's house.

Tony intervened in a struggle to protect Appleby. Morales was being carried to his burial by a half-company of the Sin Verguenza. Tony expressed a belief that Violet was not in love with him. Appleby believed he could bring Tony back to Violet. Tony indicated that he would have tried to give Violet up if he had more time. Tony's thoughts began to wander, mentioning a song and memories of Hester and Violet. Tony commented on the heat and mentioned he had not eaten the previous day.

Violet Wayne is described as patrician, while the protagonist, Appleby, is characterized as an outcast adventurer. Appleby encounters an officer named Espada Morales, who is in a tight green uniform. Morales comments on the difficulty of the Castilian language for strangers and expresses no interest in Appleby's background. Appleby is aware of Morales's reputation as a skilled soldier and a potentially dangerous individual. Morales requests assistance for the troops, stating they are short of clothing and necessities. Appleby offers to donate one hundred dollars to the fund for the troops, although Morales suggests two hundred would be more useful. Morales also seeks a loan from Appleby, citing his unfortunate losses at the Casino.

Miss Deringham expressed sympathy towards Alton and appeared anxious about a message. Alton confirmed that the man who brought the message had consumed too much whisky. Miss Deringham felt relieved after Alton reassured her that she was not to blame. Alton and Seaforth walked along the water-front in Vancouver as autumn transitioned to winter. Alton had already spent an hour in a sawmill and was contemplating details of machines. The scene in Vancouver featured mountains, forests, and various forms of transportation. Alton expressed pride in being born in the country and discussed the differences between types of men.

Damer expressed a sense of apprehension and a desire to distance himself from Alton. Hallam insisted that he wanted Damer to stay and not leave the country. Damer had previously lost his claim in Washington to Alton. Hallam mentioned being present when Gordon was found at the bottom of his shaft on the Quatchigan. Hallam indicated that he had information about Gordon's death that Damer could not access without his permission. Damer agreed to work with Hallam and was instructed to start rock-drilling at the Tyee. Alton was seen by Damer as he left the building, and he was making arrangements for an order to be sent with another man.

Harding expressed confidence that he would reclaim his property in Cuba after the Spanish soldiers are driven out. Appleby and Maccario discussed the risks associated with Harding's actions. Morales was in Santa Marta facing a rising opposition against him. The Sin Verguenza group was growing stronger while the insurrection remained sporadic and disorganized. A man arrived at the hacienda from Brena Abajo, having traveled a long distance on foot. The man reported that his wine-shop was destroyed and a comrade was killed by Candotto's soldiers. Maccario noted that Morales had sent for a column of soldiers to support Candotto.

Appleby observed Morales' demeanor and noted the importance of dignity to a Castilian gentleman. The tobacco merchant explained that he entered the area during a guard change. The tobacco merchant brandished a pistol and advised Morales to remain still. Morales acknowledged the presence of a guard nearby and expressed concern about the noise. The tobacco merchant requested the release of a peon named Domingo Pereira. Morales questioned the tobacco merchant's obligation regarding the peon and the situation in the cuartel. Morales ultimately wrote an order for the release of the prisoner, which the tobacco merchant accepted.

A group of men entered a building where peons rolled out barrels and opened boxes for almost an hour. Morales expressed satisfaction after searching through several sheds without finding a rifle. Appleby observed a workman eyeing Morales curiously while they were in the building. Colonel Appleby noted that his informants had been mistaken and advised discretion. Appleby returned to his living room where Harper informed him that Maccario had left. Violet Wayne and Godfrey Palliser were outside, with Palliser feeling chilly despite the warm sun. Palliser expressed a desire to see Violet married to Tony before he passed away.

Harry fed the engine with birch billets and water from the well. The construction of the straw-pile granary involved driving birch poles into the sod and using willow branches for wattle. The granary is designed to be frost and rain proof after being covered with straw. Harry and another individual transported grain to the railroad, which was forty miles away. Jasper offered to share living expenses and suggested chopping lumber for a house in the spring. A young Englishman was selling his homestead and one hundred and sixty acres of land for four hundred pounds sterling. Jasper advised that taking the homestead would be more beneficial than breaking virgin prairie.

Alton has faced two disasters in the ranges. Alice Deringham is the mistress of all the Carnaby property. Alice Deringham has the power to borrow money or sell the Carnaby property under certain conditions. Alice Deringham feels a sense of humiliation and guilt for helping to betray Alton. Horton is practical and confident in his actions regarding the law. Horton summoned ranchers to his store in the name of the law, excluding those suspected of complicity with Hallam. Horton planned to swear in ranchers as special constables to enforce his authority.

The naval officer and two English financiers were present at a gathering where discussions about the future of the country took place. Several attendees had previously worked as wielders of the axe before achieving success in their respective fields. Alton of the Somasco Consolidated was recognized by most attendees, and those unfamiliar with him listened attentively when he spoke. Alice Deringham observed that Alton was accepted as an equal by respected leaders after he spoke, despite his initial lack of assertiveness. Alton adapted well to the formal environment, wearing city garments with ease and displaying a sense of distinction. Alice Deringham had left the Somasco ranch hastily after Alton's recovery, and their relationship remained undefined. Alton felt out of place amidst the elegance of the gathering and compared it to the simplicity of life at Somasco ranch.

Nettie Harding and Appleby engage in a conversation about relationships and character insights. Nettie expresses curiosity about Appleby's reasons for leaving his home country. Appleby shares personal information with Nettie, who listens attentively. Nettie critiques Appleby's involvement in relationships he does not fully understand. Appleby believes that a man he knows will confess his true nature to a woman. Nettie disagrees with Appleby, suggesting that the woman will eventually see the man's true character. The conversation is interrupted when a banker’s wife enters the scene.

Harper followed a man down the street after shaking off his anger. Harper and the man crossed a street that led back to the plaza. They heard music and voices coming from the plaza. Appleby and Harper went to the 'Four Nations' after the plaza incident. Colonel Morales was waiting for Appleby at San Cristoval the next evening. Morales expressed concern about a serious matter involving a Spanish officer. Appleby believed Morales had ulterior motives for his visit.

Appleby stated that it would be at least a week before he could get away. Mrs. Wayne mentioned that Violet told her Miss Harding's story. Violet expressed that she felt a horror of herself and acknowledged being hard to Tony. Violet believed she made an implied promise to marry Tony and was glad she did. Appleby found that negotiations for building sites and water rights would delay him another week. Appleby preferred to be in the vicinity of Northrop for no apparent reason. Appleby met Violet while she was walking home and informed her that he was leaving that night.

Seaforth had never noticed any signs of mental weakness in Okanagan before. Okanagan picked up a spent cartridge and pointed to a mark in the snow. Okanagan indicated that a man had been waiting to shoot Harry as he approached with a deer. Harry was bleeding badly and knew the other man intended to finish him. Okanagan described a struggle between Harry and the assailant. Seaforth expressed a desire to find the man responsible for Harry's injuries. Okanagan found a piece of blackened lead while searching for the bullet.

A new wagon-road will be cut south towards the big river within twelve months. Surveyors will run a line for a new railroad into the Somasco valley within two years. The promise of new infrastructure implies the opening of mines and mills and a market for local produce. Alton believes that the developments will occur, despite not being able to explain why. Alton warns that unless the men take action to protect their interests, they may be left out when opportunities arise. Hallam of the Tyee is identified as a potential threat to the men's claims and ranches. The men have previously experienced being frozen out of their ranches by wealthier individuals.

Colonel Carrington expressed disbelief at the decision made by the group. A man proposed an amendment to appoint a committee to confer with Mr. Lorimer regarding the creamery. The amendment was seconded and the group prepared to vote. The voting process involved collecting folded papers from the participants. The result of the vote indicated that the amendment was carried with only three dissenting votes. Colonel Carrington reacted with surprise and struggled to regain his composure after the vote. The group displayed a mix of emotions, including indignation and determination to assert their rights.

Alton offers two hundred dollars to a man to fix something without informing Miss Townshead. The man refuses to assist Alton because he is not a relation of Miss Townshead. Alton claims he is a friend of Miss Townshead and insists on taking the dollars. Alton and Seaforth plan to visit Miss Townshead's father after completing their tasks. Townshead is found in a small wooden house with signs of a meager meal and no fire in the stove. Townshead expresses disappointment about the lack of opportunities in the city for himself and his daughter. Seaforth mentions pleasant memories of evenings spent at Townshead's ranch and suggests bringing in some supplies.

The young lad in the mining camp was stricken by rheumatic fever due to working in icy water. The girl had done most of the indispensable work on the ranch. Mr. Alton and his partner would be very wet due to the high creek and could not return to Somasco that night. The girl expressed concern about potentially starving the next day without Mr. Alton's help. The hired man left after a stormy interview, followed by his son. The house was damp and cold, leading to a feeling of loneliness for the girl. The girl reflected on her past in England and felt forgotten by her friends.

A maid informed Alice Deringham that Miss Townshead was waiting to see her. Alice Deringham felt her courage fail before meeting Miss Townshead. After the meeting, Seaforth noted that Miss Townshead's eyes were misty. Alice Deringham's father, Deringham, looked ill and haggard but relieved when he approached her. Deringham had spent an hour with Mr. Alton and a lawyer discussing important matters. Mr. Alton was doubtful about his right to Carnaby and did not want to receive it as a favor. Alton has made over all his rights in Carnaby to Alice Deringham.

Nellie Townshead was sitting in a chair when Alton entered the room. Alton stated that he could not find anyone and came in without a response to his knock. Alton expressed a desire to see Nellie and asked her to sit down. Alton directly asked Nellie if she would marry him. Nellie questioned the suddenness of Alton's proposal and whether she had given him any reason to believe she would accept. Alton explained that he felt lonely at the ranch and wanted someone to brighten his life. Nellie acknowledged Alton's genuine tone and recognized his desire for guidance.

The narrator enjoys the company of a companion who smiles when he recounts stories about Lee. Grace passes by the narrator and his companion without greeting them. Alice expresses resentment about Grace not speaking to them. Martin Lorimer joins the narrator and his companion during the afternoon. The local population celebrates an occasion with merriment, including breaking windows. A banquet is held in the city hall, attended by various members of the community. The surveyor delivers a speech emphasizing the importance of the railroad to the Western Dominion.

A red moon is visible in the night sky, indicating cold conditions in the North. Seaforth expresses concern about the fate of wounded men exposed to the frost. Okanagan suggests using the canon as a means of escape. Seaforth acknowledges that no man has successfully navigated the canon before. Alton, who is injured, questions whether Seaforth and Okanagan staked additional claims. Seaforth admits they did not stake the claims due to their urgent situation. Seaforth and Okanagan plan to travel down the canon together to reach Somasco.

Alton proposed a payment plan of one thousand down, one thousand in six months, and the rest any time in two years, with six percent interest. Callender expressed trust in Alton and stated he would not sell the ranch to anyone else. Alton agreed to provide a cheque to Callender the following day. Hallam approached Alton and Seaforth while riding down the trail. Hallam made an ironic greeting and observed Alton with suspicion. Hallam indicated that there was not enough room for both him and Alton in the valley. Alton remained unfazed by Hallam's threats and continued on the trail.

Lyle anticipates trouble with Colonel Carrington regarding the creamery project. Colonel Carrington returned home yesterday and plans to discuss the creamery with Willmot. Harry expresses skepticism about the feasibility of turning the Carrington territory into an industrial settlement. Grace expresses concern that the creamery project may lead to strife and potentially break up the Carrington colony. Colonel Carrington explicitly states that Lorimer will never marry Miss Carrington with his consent. Lorimer asserts that if Colonel Carrington does not grant his consent, he and Miss Carrington will proceed without it.

The group struggled through choked forests and icy rock slopes during their journey. Provisions ran out rapidly after one pack-horse fell over a precipice. The group failed to find the gorge the prospector mentioned, encountering many wrong ones instead. Johnston expressed a belief that luck would eventually turn in their favor. The group decided to spend three more days prospecting despite the harsh winter conditions. The camp was marked by fatigue and hunger, leading to a melancholy atmosphere among the members. Johnston reflected on the nature of seeking fortune and the consequences of past actions.

Seaforth acknowledges that he has nothing to offer but his gratitude for the help he received. The girl expresses that what matters most is still Seaforth's. Seaforth and the girl are observed by a rancher as they sit together. The rancher greets them cheerfully as he drives by in an old wagon. Seaforth reflects on Harry's misfortunes and expresses concern for him. Harry has lost everything he hoped for and is now lame. Nellie Townshead notices Seaforth's troubled expression regarding Harry.

Harry expressed feelings of bitterness regarding his situation and a lack of gratitude when receiving money. It is suggested that Harry may have been robbed of his patrimony. The new land accepts individuals based on their present rather than their past. A bargain was made, and the vendor received initial payments. Harry and the narrator prepared to drive the first furrow on a clear spring morning. The prairie was described as dappled with moving shadows from clouds. Harry and the narrator felt hopeful about their future as they began to work the land.

Horton informed Alton that the man could not last until morning. Horton suggested that Alton speak to Neilson, the surveyor, for witnesses. Alton had survived a fall into a ravine, unlike his assailant, who was severely injured. Damer revealed that Hallam of the Tyee had hired him to murder Alton. Damer initially was hired to watch Alton while working for him. Damer mentioned that he had a partner named Black Nailer. Damer provided a detailed account of events before his condition worsened.

The narrator is cutting into a silver birch tree while observing a thrasher in the prairie. The crops of the man who employed the thrasher were undamaged, while many others were spoiled by frost. The narrator's throat is parched due to a lack of water, as the creek is alkaline. A construction train passes by while the narrator wipes perspiration from his eyes. Harry warns the narrator of an impending danger as a rumbling sound is heard. The road-bed that had been excavated was swept away by a landslide, leaving debris below. The surveyor indicates that the bank looked solid but is at risk of further collapse.

Alton received a letter from Deringham stating that he would not return to Somasco for some time. Alton mentioned he had a bad accident while bringing in a deer and was found after lying out in the frost. Horton noted that many strangers were in the area looking for timber rights and prospecting around the Crown lands. Seaforth arrived at the hotel and inquired about Harry, who had left for the trail. Seaforth mentioned that one of the boys staying at the hotel had also left for the railroad shortly before Harry. Alton experienced difficulty controlling his horse, which was unusually restive during his ride. Alton felt weak and lethargic due to the cold and the physical strain of riding.

Seaforth and Alton are on a journey to find treasure. Seaforth feels despair and fatigue during their expedition. Alton emphasizes the importance of keeping faith with their comrade, Jimmy. The weather is rainy, making their progress difficult. Seaforth experiences physical discomfort from the conditions and labor. They set up camp after a long day of travel. Alton suggests stopping at a cove for the night due to their exhaustion.

Miss Clavier observed Nettie talking to Mr. Tony Palliser at Darsley and during the evening. Nettie stated that American young women are allowed to talk to and marry Englishmen. Miss Clavier warned Nettie that it would be a mistake for an American girl who had not met many Englishmen to marry Tony Palliser. Miss Clavier revealed that she was Lucy Davidson and that Bernard Appleby did not come to meet her at Northrop Lodge. Nettie expressed genuine astonishment at Miss Clavier's revelation about Bernard Appleby. Miss Clavier admitted to having been fond of Tony Palliser and attempted to warn Nettie about him. Miss Clavier disclosed that she was married to Clavier, who left her before he died in Melbourne.

Aline expressed curiosity about the character Harry and her ability to tame him. The narrator felt shame and dismay regarding his previous interactions with Grace. Aline pointed out defects in the domestic utensils and crockery at Fairmead. The narrator's sister prepared an unusually good breakfast while he attended to the animals. The narrator broke a strip of virgin prairie and cultivated part of the land before the Indian summer ended. Aline showed interest in watching wild fowl during their migration. Jasper frequently visited and engaged in verbal encounters with Aline.

The characters are in a cold environment, and one character has almost lost the use of his limbs. Harry encourages the team to continue despite the cold, and they arrive at Fletcher's shanty by Willow Lake. Fletcher opens the door when Harry and another character arrive with Lee, who is weak and needs assistance. Minnie, Fletcher's daughter, is surprised to see her father and learns that Lee has come in search of her. Lee expresses gratitude for Minnie's marriage to Thomas Fletcher and shares news about her mother, who has died. Minnie expresses mixed emotions of joy and resentment towards Lee regarding their past. The characters must leave quickly to prevent their team from freezing, and they depart shortly after the reunion.

Morales is known to be a loyal soldier with insatiable greed. Appleby is aware that Harding has been making overtures to the insurgents. Morales desires sufficient proof to bring Harding within his grasp. Appleby has seen Morales' dark eyes fixed on Nettie. Morales suggested that haste would be advisable regarding his proposal. Harper expressed anger towards Colonel Morales and desired to confront him. Appleby instructed Pancho to find Don Maccario and deliver a message.

The girl expressed concern about the potential disappointment others might feel when they see her true self. Alton and Seaforth had a conversation late into the night. Alton and Seaforth entered a room at Horton's store during supper. The men present at the meeting were primarily silent and serious workers from the forest. Alton addressed the men about the need for fair distribution of earnings in the valley. There was a general agreement among the assembly that speculators often profited at the expense of laborers. Alton suggested that the laborers should take action to protect their interests.

The dying man held a glass to his lips and instructed Horton to read a document. Horton read the document hastily while the dying man traced characters on it before letting it fall. The dying man expressed a sense of vindictiveness after signing the document. He whispered to Alton about another man involved besides Hallam, which left Alton grim and silent. The doctor indicated that the dying man might last an hour or two but likely would not speak again. Alton grappled with suspicions and the implications of Damer's revelation about Hallam. Alton considered the consequences of taking action against Hallam, particularly the impact on his daughter.

Tony has been loyal to the girl for a long time. Godfrey Palliser expressed impatience about a delay caused by Davidson. Davidson had not been seen since the previous night and was last reported going to the fir spinny. Tony and Appleby were concerned that Davidson might have left without collecting money owed to him. Tony Palliser preferred to avoid telling Miss Wayne about his involvement in a troubling affair. Appleby believed that the story regarding Tony's actions would eventually need to be disclosed. During the shooting event, Tony performed well and interacted positively with the beaters and keepers.

A man at a meeting expressed enthusiasm for a cooperative venture with Alton of Somasco. Alton proposed a program that included selling timber, doubling the Somasco mill, and establishing a gristmill. The plan also involved recording more timber rights and participation in a new silver mine. Alton mentioned the establishment of an office in Vancouver and a desiccated fruit store. Horton expressed his support for Alton's plan and indicated his financial commitment. After the first meeting of the Somasco Consolidated, Alton spent time away from the ranch and engaged in extensive correspondence. Miss Deringham observed Alton's unusual behavior and noted her own contentment at Somasco.

The narrative involves characters named Johnston, Lorimer, Ormond, and Colonel Carrington. The group agreed to march south in company while searching for Macdonald's Crossing. Ormond limped due to a foot injury exacerbated by exposure. Lorimer experienced feelings of resentment towards Colonel Carrington due to perceived inequalities in their circumstances. Ormond and Lorimer halted to observe their surroundings, which included a slope of snow and distant figures of their comrades. Ormond stumbled and slipped on a rocky surface, leading to a precarious situation where he risked falling over a precipice. Lorimer attempted to assist Ormond by offering his hand and encouraging him to lift himself up.

Appleby plans to commit to standing with the insurgents. Harper expresses astonishment at Appleby's decision. Appleby believes that his actions will financially harm Sugar Harding in Cuba. Appleby has asked Maccario to occupy the hacienda to control the carretera to Santa Marta. Harper and Appleby encounter a sergeant and cazadores on the road. The sergeant informs them that the road is not very safe. Appleby and Harper decide to return to the hacienda after the encounter with the sergeant.

Harper spoke in Castilian to the landlord. The landlord mentioned a rich American and a lady who are fastidious but pay well. A man in white duck and a girl in a long white dress entered the room. Appleby recognized Nettie Harding and felt uncomfortable about his appearance. Harding invited Appleby to join them for dinner. Harper expressed indifference towards the Sin Verguenza and accepted the dinner invitation. Harding inquired about the Sin Verguenza's situation, and Harper confirmed they had been defeated.

The men celebrated the completion of the railroad with cider and expressed gratitude towards Harry Alton. Seaforth acknowledged the contributions of a comrade and anticipated his arrival. Alice Deringham felt a deep emotional response as she awaited Harry Alton's arrival. Harry Alton expressed his contentment and desire to start anew with Alice Deringham. Alice Deringham initially resisted Harry Alton's advances, citing her perceived shortcomings. Alice Deringham ultimately accepted Harry Alton's affection, recognizing their mutual feelings. Nellie Seaforth congratulated Alice Deringham on her relationship with Harry Alton, believing it would lead to her happiness.
