The speaker mentions historical figures Essex, John of Austria, and Desmond. The guide, Shamus, claims not to hear a cry in the bog. Amyas expresses concern that there may be someone in danger. The ancient fears the presence of pucks and banshees. Raleigh volunteers to investigate the source of the cry.

Pelagia expresses a desire for help and teaching. Philammon discusses the concept of hell and the need for repentance. Miriam suggests that Pelagia can be saved through repentance. Pelagia recalls her baptism at a young age. Philammon reacts with concern about Pelagia's spiritual state. Pelagia questions the possibility of forgiveness and expresses fear of penance. Philammon declares his intention to accompany Pelagia and seek redemption.

Sir Richard inquires about the whereabouts of the Jesuits. Mr. Leigh informs Sir Richard that the Jesuits left his house an hour ago. Mr. Leigh expresses distress over being accused of treason and lying. Mr. Leigh's son Eustace is not home, and there are concerns about his well-being. Sir Richard mentions that Eustace nearly murdered his cousin Frank. Sir Richard and Will Cary discuss the possibility of the Jesuits escaping by boat at Marsland Mouth. Will Cary leaves to pursue the Jesuits while Sir Richard prepares to meet Mr. Leigh.

Amyas is concerned about finding his companion, Dick. Captain Leigh informs Sir John that Dick has gone off with his lordship. Drake encourages Amyas to follow his leader and drink. The captains have promised to send news if they hear about Dick. The great sea-fight begins to determine the future of Europe and America. Drake, Hawkins, and Frobisher engage the Spanish fleet with their ordnance. The Spanish Armada struggles against the nimbleness of the English ships.

The Spaniards and Englishmen are compared in their capabilities to conquer an empire. The cacique proposed a compact regarding the division of booty between the allies. The cacique suggested that the Indians would take prisoners while the English would take gold. Ayacanora expressed her disapproval of the idea of cannibalism. The English decided to proceed without the Indians after considering the cacique's argument. Ayacanora isolated herself in her hut after the decision to leave was made. The group crossed the Cordillera and observed the city of Santa Fe, which was deemed too large for their plans.

The farm was left to the speaker's father by Lorimer Spell because the father saved Spell's life in France. The speaker's father had papers to prove his claim to the farm, but they were stolen. Carson Davenport expressed anger towards the workmen for believing the speaker's story. George Rogers accused Carson Davenport of selling worthless stock in the Yellow Pansy Extension. Davenport has been involved in multiple oil-well propositions and has a history of selling worthless leases. The speaker, George Rogers, lost fifteen hundred dollars due to Davenport's actions. The boys felt it was their duty to inform Jack's father about the incident involving Davenport.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: A number of letters were brought in from the Haven Point post-office the day following a fire. Jack received a drop letter that contained a message from Professor Lemm. The letter expressed Professor Lemm's resentment towards the Rovers for losing a lucrative position. Jack speculated that Professor Lemm would not take any action against them. The heavy snowstorm cleared, allowing the cadets to skate on the lake. Jack and his friends skated to Clearwater Hall to meet the girls. Jack and Ruth discussed the fire and their plans for the Christmas holidays.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The Rover boys expressed satisfaction with their school selection. Clearwater Hall is described positively by the girls who attend it. The homecoming of the Rover boys was a celebratory event. Dick Rover and Sam Rover discussed the similarities between Colby Hall and other schools. The boys admitted to playing tricks on a teacher named Asa Lemm. The Rover family had dinner together, which included all family members. The boys planned to shop for Christmas presents after returning home.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Paul expresses a fondness for both Russell and Si Doring. Jim Haskett confronts Paul and accuses Si Doring of telling stories about him. Haskett physically restrains Paul and demands answers regarding Doring's accusations. Haskett claims he has been unfairly labeled a thief and mentions that others are looking at him suspiciously. Haskett suggests that Russell is the actual thief and claims to have proof against him. Caleb Walton confronts Haskett about his accusations against Russell. Haskett maintains his accusation against Russell despite Walton's challenge.

Songbird was on the couch, propped up by pillows. Songbird was driving from Knoxbury after visiting the bank for Mr. Sanderson. A man in a heavy overcoat and thick fur cap approached Songbird and asked for directions. The man struck Songbird on the head and chin, causing him to lose consciousness. Songbird noticed a man with a peculiar stutter and whistle outside the bank before the incident. Mr. Sanderson had instructed Songbird to withdraw cash instead of using a check. Songbird observed the man who stuttered and whistled peering at him through a side window of the bank.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Longley Academy has a baseball ground with a new grandstand and bleachers. The game was played at Longley Academy's grounds, with half of the stands reserved for Colby Hall cadets and their friends. The crowd at the game included people from Colby Hall, Longley Academy, Hixley, Columbus, Clearwater Hall, and the surrounding town. Jack Rover was the pitcher for Longley Academy during the game. Durrick was the first batter for Longley Academy, reaching first base with a hit. Jack Rover caught a fly ball from Wilks, resulting in an out for Longley Academy. Longley Academy did not score in the first inning.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: The young ladies in the tonneau of the car likely did not recognize Sam as he was inflating a tire. Sam considered going to Hope to see Grace and planned to leave his card if she was not there. A maid at the seminary informed Sam that Miss Laning was out. Grace had gone automobiling with Ada Waltham and her brother, Chester. Chester Waltham had a new foreign car and was eager to give Grace and Ada a ride. The girls at the seminary mentioned that Grace had permission to stay out until ten o'clock. Sam experienced a blowout while driving and returned to Brill to clean up.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Randy expressed that it would be hard for soldiers and sailors to settle down after being away for months. Andy and Randy were playing in their bedroom when they heard the doorbell ring. The twins rushed downstairs to greet their father, Tom Rover, upon his arrival. Tom Rover hugged and kissed his sons and expressed his joy at seeing them. Similar reunions occurred in the adjoining houses with Dick Rover and Sam Rover returning home. The families gathered in the middle house to celebrate the reunions with hugs and conversations. The Rovers discussed their contributions to the war effort and the challenges they faced.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dave Porter is not the person being referred to in the conversation. Phil Lawrence's father is worried about a letter he received. Phil's father stands to lose between twenty and thirty thousand dollars. The land owned by Phil's father and uncle was initially purchased at a low price. The land was leased to a lumber company for several years. The L. A. & H. railroad company wants to buy the land but cannot due to a title issue. The title issue arose within the last five years.

Walter Russell is a member of the crew of the _Brooklyn_. A lieutenant of marines informed Walter that a steam launch was bound for the _Iowa_ and the _Brooklyn_. The steam launch was fifty-five feet long, twelve feet wide, and manned by eight men and six marines. The launch stopped to investigate a flag spotted by the lookout while approaching Baiquiri. The commander of the launch exchanged letters with a group of Cubans, including a letter for General Calixto Garcia. The launch served dinner to the officers, sharpshooters, crew, and Walter during the journey. The _Brooklyn_ was sighted at night, and the officer of the deck expressed surprise at Walter's return.

The wagon was loaded with blankets and served as a soft seat for the soldiers. The soldiers were traveling down a sandy highway leading to the sea. The fort had some of the finest guns in the country capable of reaching a ship ten or twelve miles out in the harbor. The soldiers had strict orders to keep all outsiders at a distance to prevent Spanish spies from obtaining plans of the fort. Caleb Walton stated that four-fifths of Spanish sailors are shanghied and treated unjustly, affecting their ability to perform as sailors. The sergeant in command confirmed that many Spanish troops had not been paid for nearly a year. Caleb Walton noted that before the war, Spain relied on foreign engineers, many of whom would not stay on Spanish warships during the conflict.

A landslide had completely swallowed up a mine that was lost. Dave, Roger, and others searched for the lost mine, as detailed in 'Dave Porter in the Gold Fields.' Link Merwell and Job Haskers were also searching for the lost mine during the same time. The missing mine was relocated, but another landslide nearly cost Dave and his friends their lives. A man from the other party informed Dave and his friends that Link Merwell and Job Haskers had been swept away to their death. The finding of the Landslide Mine benefited the Morr family financially, and they shared a portion with Dave and others. Dave and his friends later went on a tour through Yellowstone Park and planned a trip on a steamer to Portland, Maine.

Uncle Wilbur escaped from the sanitarium and was located near Oak Hall. Wilbur Poole has been returned to the sanitarium without any trouble. Dave received a letter from Nat Poole regarding Wilbur's return to the sanitarium. Dave's friends noticed his absent-mindedness while he dressed two deer. The weather turned cloudy and rainy in the evening, leading to a storm. Mrs. Wadsworth announced that the worst of the storm was over before bedtime. The hired girl reported that many kitchen items were missing, indicating a burglary.

Laura brought news that prompted a group to follow her outside. Link was unbound and placed on a hammock with a pillow. Mr. Wadsworth confronted Link Merwell, who was identified as a prisoner. Link Merwell expressed that he could not talk and acknowledged his situation. Dave and Phil explained how they captured Link after he fell over a cliff. The group discussed how to transport Link to jail, deciding to wait until the next day. Mr. Wadsworth suggested placing Link in the woodshed for the night.

The Rovers had an early breakfast before riding to the seminary. Grace complimented Sam on his performance in a recent game. Mr. Waltham provided ice cream and snacks for the group under the trees. Dora mentioned that Mr. Waltham was considering joining their summer tour. Sam felt less cordial towards Grace after hearing about Mr. Waltham's potential involvement. The seniors at Brill were preparing for final examinations scheduled for the following week. Sam focused on his studies during the examination period, avoiding sports.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The Italian on the road warned the group to stop due to an impending blast. A loud roar and rumble occurred, followed by a burst of flames and smoke. Rocks, small stones, and dirt fell around the group, striking their automobiles. Dick instructed the group to protect themselves with robes during the rockfall. Tom was hit on the shoulder by a stone, while Sam was hit in the head. The second car sustained a dent from a stone, but no one was seriously injured. Chester Waltham and his sister were farther back and only experienced a slight shower of dirt.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Six cadets broke through the ice but were rescued safely. Professor Brice and Mr. Crews conducted a search for any remaining individuals under the ice. Danger signs were placed on the ice to prevent future accidents. Asa Lemm expressed disapproval of skating races, believing they encourage rowdy behavior. Colonel Colby defended the importance of exercise and fresh air for the cadets. Ruth and May had wet feet after skating and were invited to dry them in the living-room. Andy and Randy reported that everyone was safe and only a skating cap was lost.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The crew of the _Merrimac_ included Deignan, G. F. Phillips, F. Kelley, J. Murphy, G. Charette, D. Montague, and R. Clausen. The crew members were experienced sailors aware of the dangers they faced when attempting to run the _Merrimac_ under enemy fire. The attempt to enter the harbor was postponed by the rear-admiral after a late start on Wednesday night. A catamaran was built and attached to the _Merrimac_ for emergency use in case the small boats were disabled. Walter expressed concern about the risks of the mission and his health, suspecting he might have Cuban fever. Walter received medication from a surgeon and was advised to report back if his condition worsened. By nightfall, Walter's condition had deteriorated, but he chose not to go into the sick bay.

William Philander Tubbs is invited by Tom to a spread in Ashton. Tom mentions various food items for the spread, including spaghetti and sauerkraut. William Philander Tubbs expresses discomfort with the suggested food items. Tom and his friends purchase items for the feast in Ashton. Sam notes that Songbird is feeling down due to issues with Minnie. Tom plans to help Songbird forget his troubles during the feast. Grace has become friends with a rich girl named Miss Ada Waltham.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Ruth suffered an eye injury that caused her to feel sick. The group was traveling by boat to the town when the incident occurred. Alice Strobell expressed concern that Ruth might be blinded for life. The boys speculated that the pepper causing the injury was intended for Jack. They sought medical assistance from Doctor Borden after finding the first physician unavailable. Doctor Borden indicated that Ruth would likely feel better by the next day. Ruth refused to return to school until Jack received medical attention.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: The scene of action is Porto Rico, specifically the forts of San Juan. Caleb expresses excitement about the American navy's progress. Walter mentions that if the San Juan forts surrender, the city will be vulnerable. Reports of a fight at Cienfuegos and sightings of strange vessels off Martinique are discussed. The Flying Squadron is preparing to sail, with a signal to weigh anchor and follow the flagship. The warships in the Flying Squadron include the _Brooklyn_, _Massachusetts_, _Texas_, and _Scorpion_, along with the collier _Sterling_. The _Massachusetts_ is a first-class battleship with a displacement of over ten thousand tons and a speed of sixteen knots per hour.

Sam is interested in talking to Grace but is hesitant because she is out with Waltham. Ada Waltham expresses concern about Chester and Grace being out late. Dora suggests that they should retire for the night, but Dick insists they stay until Grace returns. A bellboy announces a telephone call for Sam Rover. Grace informs Sam that the runabout has broken down and requests assistance. Grace is located at a farmhouse on the road between Dennville and Corbytown. Sam and Tom decide to go to help Grace and Chester after learning about the breakdown.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Lorimer Spell believed there was wealth in oil on his land. Mr. Fitch expressed that investing in the Lorimer Spell claim would be a waste of money. Jack questioned the value of the Lorimer Spell claim after hearing Mr. Fitch's opinion. Uncle Dick felt relieved that he had not invested a large sum in the claim. Andy suggested that Uncle Dick pretend to be upset about losing interest in the claim. Jack mentioned Mr. John Franklin, who had a claim worth investigating. Randy reported that the hotel clerk was unaware of the events involving certain men.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Randy, Andy, Jack, and Fred are preparing to go out on a hunt. The boys have concerns about Professor Lemm and Mr. Brown's interest in the island. The boys discuss the limited value of the island and its lumber. The boys pack a lunch and a thermos of hot chocolate for their outing. Uncle Barney Stevenson expresses concern for the boys' safety while they are out. Uncle Barney paces in his cabin and reflects on his nervousness about the boys. Uncle Barney decides to leave his cabin and follow the boys after feeling lonely.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The text describes a group of individuals who have loving families and enjoy comforts in life. They travel from New York to Valley Brook or Cedarville during summer and Christmas. The Rover Boys Series, written by Arthur M. Winfield (Edward Stratemeyer), has sold over three million copies. The series includes various titles featuring the Rover boys in different adventures. The X Bar X Boys series, written by James Cody Ferris, features stories about two boys, Roy and Teddy, and their experiences on a ranch. Both series are published by Grosset & Dunlap, New York. The text encourages readers to keep the book wrapper as a catalog for other stories.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Mrs. Wadsworth expressed agitation regarding a loud yell they heard. Dave suggested that the wild man, Wilbur Poole, might have followed them. The boys and Mr. Wadsworth searched for the wild man in the clearing. Phil described the wild man as waving a sceptre and scaring the girls. Mr. Wadsworth expressed concern about the wild man's potential to cause worry. The group decided to inform the Pooles about the wild man. Ben and his companions reported encountering a wild man on their way back.

Snow hung down off the rough roof of each cabin. Uncle Barney led the boys to the cabin they were to occupy. The cabin door was locked to prevent outside hunters from entering. The cabin contained a living-room and a sleeping apartment with various furnishings. The boys expressed delight at the accommodations in the cabin. Uncle Barney planned to take a turkey cock to Rockville to be shipped to the Rover boys' family. The boys decided to wait until the next day to eat the game.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Dave confronted Link Merwell after he sent a derogatory note. Phil supported Dave's decision to confront Merwell. Dave accused Merwell of being a faker and not reforming. Phil suggested tying Merwell's hands to prevent him from escaping. Merwell was forced to comply and had his hands tied with fishline. The group began to lead Merwell back along the brook. The group encountered other boys fishing and discussing Merwell's situation.

The Rovers were informed about trouble among property owners in the county. Mr. Powell had been visiting the Stevensons with his wife and daughter May. Mr. Powell accompanied Mr. Stevenson on a trip for leisure. The quarrel between Uncle Barney and the Stevensons could have been resolved earlier. The Rovers and Mr. Powell found Slugger and Nappy had gone ashore at a low point of the island. The Rovers discovered a cabin with smoke coming from the chimney. Inside the cabin, Slugger Brown had an injured ankle and Nappy Martell was attempting to open a treasure box.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Gabe Werner is a young man who previously attended a military academy with the Rovers. The Rovers are searching for Gabe Werner after seeing him in the area. Jack believes he saw Gabe Werner crossing the roadway. The Rovers encounter two men sitting outside a shack who deny seeing Gabe Werner. One of the men goes back inside the shack where Gabe Werner is hiding. Jack expresses a desire to confront Gabe Werner for past grievances. Randy notes that the two men were present on the hotel veranda earlier.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Mrs. Wadsworth questioned the servant girl, Mary, about the state of the valuables in the bungalow. Mary confirmed that everything was in its place when she went to bed. The boys and girls searched the kitchen and pantry for missing items. Ben reported that their bungalow had been robbed of nearly all food and kitchen items. An examination revealed that all valuable tableware and two rings belonging to Laura were missing. Footprints were found leading from the pantry window to the edge of the forest. At the Basswood bungalow, Mrs. Basswood reported that some solid silver tableware had also vanished.

Slugger Brown and Nappy Martell were confronted by Bob Nixon, Captain Dale, and Professor Brice. Colonel Colby ordered Slugger and Nappy to march to his office. After their meeting with Colonel Colby, Slugger and Nappy hurried to pack their belongings. Codfish was found sobbing in his room and denied seeing anyone. Nappy threatened Fred and attempted to hit him, but Fred retaliated. Jack fought Slugger, who was knocked down despite hitting Jack on the shoulder. The auto-stage arrived to take Slugger and Nappy away from the school.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Roger announced that there was no use in looking for Phil's uncle around their current location. Phil expressed his desire to send word to his father that his uncle had been found. Lester Lawrence stated that he would be able to walk in a day or two despite his sprained ankle. The boys discussed their situation until after noon and then decided to have dinner. Phil wrote a message to be sent to Carpen Falls to inform his parents about his uncle. Lester Lawrence advised the boys to follow a shorter route back to Bear Camp. Dave and Roger discussed the implications of finding Phil's uncle as they returned to Bear Camp.

Mr. Hoover stated that a stable boy let out a horse while he was away. The stable boy described the man as wearing a heavy gray overcoat and a heavy fur cap. Mr. Hoover had to pay four dollars to get his horse back from old Bray. Songbird planned to have a photograph of Blackie Crowden enlarged and sent to various police stations. Mr. Clinger agreed to re-photograph and enlarge the picture of Crowden, providing copies by the next morning. Tom Rover surprised his brother Sam by visiting Ashton without prior notice. Tom expressed a desire to return to his studies at Brill.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The boys were sent away out of town to avoid being present when Dick Rover was attacked. Dick Rover was attacked by at least three men, possibly Davenport, Tate, and Jackson. Dick Rover's bag and its contents were stolen during the attack. Dick Rover's money, watch, and diamond ring were not stolen. Dick Rover had gone to Wichita Falls to retrieve documents related to the Lorimer Spell claim. Mr. Fitch, an oil expert, stated that there was no oil on the Lorimer Spell claim.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dave's father is at least ten or twelve years older than Dave. Dave's father is uncertain about what to do with the land. The railroad company prefers to buy Dave's father's land rather than lease it. Dave's father has been told by the railroad company that they will look elsewhere if they cannot acquire his property. Phil Lawrence's father is considering advertising to find out about his uncle. The Oak Hall Club's first outing is considered a success by the members. Dave observes smoke on the horizon, which Ben suggests is from an incoming steamer.

Phil's Uncle Lester was involved with a trust company that managed certain funds. Approximately five years ago, some funds from the trust company went missing, leading to suspicion against Uncle Lester. Uncle Lester left home and moved to another state before a warrant for his arrest could be served. A local newspaper article suggested that Uncle Lester was guilty, which contributed to his disappearance. Phil's father has made efforts to locate Uncle Lester, including hiring searchers and placing advertisements, but has not received any information. Uncle Lester held a one-quarter interest in a tract of land, which complicates the sale of the land due to the need for his signature on the deed. Less than four months after Uncle Lester's disappearance, a criminal was arrested who admitted to stealing the funds that Uncle Lester was accused of taking.

The cadets discussed teaching Asa Lemm a lesson. Dan Soppinger was assigned to watch Asa Lemm in the school library. The cadets planned to get two goats into Asa Lemm's room using a fire-escape. Dick and Dora had a son named John and a daughter named Martha. Tom and Nellie had twin boys named Anderson and Randolph. Sam and Grace had a daughter named Mary and a son named Fred. After over an hour of searching, no trace of Link was found. Several days passed without any sightings or news of Link Merwell or Ward Porton.

The book is titled 'The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck' and is authored by Arthur M. Winfield. This book is the fifth volume in 'The Second Rover Boys Series for Young Americans.' The first series introduced characters Dick, Tom, and Sam Rover and their relatives. The Rover boys established themselves in business in New York and became married. The younger Rovers were sent to a boarding school due to their lively disposition. The current volume shifts the setting to the oil fields in the southern part of the United States. The book contains multiple chapters detailing various adventures and events involving the Rover boys.

The group had attached a long rope to the bobsled to assist in hauling it along the ice. As they skated, the snow began to fall steadily and the wind increased, making conditions less pleasant. Uncle Barney expressed that he did not expect such a heavy snowstorm when he set out to find the boys. The old lumberman became disturbed by the worsening weather and the growing snowdrifts. Uncle Barney suggested that they should head directly for the island instead of trying to navigate around the snowdrifts.

Ward Porton disappeared after learning about Dave's visit to Obadiah Jones but returned to his old tricks. Link Merwell was tried and received an equal sentence of imprisonment as Jasniff. Commodore Dewey's victory at Manila was celebrated by the American public. Men from both the North and South served together in the army and navy during the conflict. The United States converted ocean steamers and coast craft into war vessels to support the blockade. Naval Reserves and volunteers were in high demand for the navy during this time. Rumors circulated that Spain would send a fleet to bombard New York or other eastern cities. Acting Rear-Admiral Sampson monitored the blockade along the northern coast of Cuba. Tad Rason informed Dave that Ward Porton would no longer be with the moving-picture company due to a letter he wrote about his parentage. Dave was worried that Ward Porton might try to prove that he was the real Dave Porter, which he found concerning. Jessie reassured Dave that she did not care about his background and believed in him regardless of his past.

Dick Rover returned to the hotel late in the evening. Dick Rover telegraphed for Mr. Fitch to come after inspecting the Franklin claim. One of the men recommended by Nick Ogilvie was willing to invest five thousand dollars in boring a well. Mr. Franklin agreed to give Dick Rover entire charge of the oil matter for a payment of one-eighth of the oil produced. Mr. Fitch began an inspection of the Franklin farm after arriving. The older Rovers were mustered out of the United States service, with Tom and Sam returning first, followed by Dick. Walter Russell works as a clerk for Phil Newell, a newsstand proprietor and Civil War veteran. Phil Newell recalls his experiences aboard the _Carondelet_ during the Civil War. Walter expresses a desire to enlist in the Navy after hearing news of a victory at Manila. Phil Newell mentions that his age and disability prevent him from re-enlisting in the Navy. Walter's brother, Ben, has joined the militia in New York and is waiting to be sworn into service. Walter's youngest brother, Larry, is currently at sea in the Pacific Ocean. Phil Newell believes that the United States needs both soldiers and sailors during the current conflict.

Phil Newell worked at a stand located in the heart of Boston, outside a leading hotel. Walter Russell expressed his desire to enlist in the military due to the war with Spain. Walter had obtained his guardian's consent to enlist, which he had in his pocket. Phil Newell encouraged Walter to enlist, despite not wanting to lose him as a clerk. Walter Russell was one of three brothers, with Ben as the eldest and Larry as the youngest. Larry Russell had previously shipped on a vessel bound for Hong Kong and served under the flagship Olympia. Ben Russell had secured employment in a hardware establishment in New York City before enlisting in the 71st Regiment of New York.

Commodore Schley conducted a bombardment to assess the enemy's strength and the location of shore batteries. Admiral Sampson arrived on June 1 with additional warships, including the _New York_, _Oregon_, and _Mayflower_. The _Oregon_ was a first-class battleship with over ten thousand tons' displacement and a significant armament. Lieutenant Richmond P. source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Ben's father expressed uncertainty about the identity of an individual, suggesting he may not be Wilbur Poole. Ben advised his father to inform Nat's father about the uncertainty regarding Mr. Poole. Mr. Basswood left for Carpen Falls in the middle of the forenoon. A group of young people decided to go bathing at a sandy beach near the bungalows. The young people enjoyed swimming while the older folks watched from a fallen tree. A swimming race was organized with the goal of reaching a rock in the cove. Ben, a good swimmer, initially led the race but later disappeared from view.

Tom and Sam were traveling to Dennville in a touring car. They reached Dennville, a small town surrounded by hills, within half an hour. Sam and Tom found signboards indicating the direction to Corbytown. They encountered a hilly and poor road after leaving Dennville. Grace met them at the farmhouse, appearing hysterical and on the verge of tears. Grace reported an automobile breakdown and mentioned a broken front axle. Mr. and Mrs. Akerson, the farmers, provided shelter to Grace after she knocked on their door.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Phil Franklin expressed gratitude and presented wooden gifts to the Rovers. The gifts included an inkstand, a miniature canoe, a napkin ring, and a tray for pins and collar buttons. John Franklin confirmed that they were returning to Texas the next day. John Franklin planned to confront individuals who had swindled him out of his farm. Randy and Jack gave Phil Franklin two storybooks as a farewell gift. Longley Academy won a game against Columbus Academy with a score of eleven to two. Gif, the captain of Colby Hall, called a team meeting to emphasize the need for practice.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Chester Waltham did not accompany Grace to the farmhouse. Tom and his brother entered the sitting-room of the farmhouse. Grace recounted an incident involving Mr. Waltham while speaking to Sam. Grace expressed that Mr. Waltham was reckless during their ride. Mr. Waltham drove the car many miles until they reached Dennville. Grace pushed Mr. Waltham away when he attempted to kiss her. Sam decided to take Grace back to the hotel in Larkinburg.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The three Rovers were traveling and came to a crossroad with a sign pointing left. Riverview is a fair-sized town located on a stream. The auto-stage was empty when the Rovers arrived at the hotel. The driver of the auto-stage reported that a passenger named Blackie Crowden had disappeared. Blackie Crowden jumped from the auto-stage while it was traveling at twenty miles an hour. The driver indicated that Blackie Crowden had a small handbag when he jumped off. The Rovers decided to search for Blackie Crowden at the location where he jumped off.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: A woman and a little boy were pulled in by the boatswain. Dave and his friends were heading towards a woman and a girl struggling in the water. Dave managed to drag the woman on board, who then collapsed after asking to save the girl named Della. Dave dove into the water to rescue the girl after seeing her hand and arm disappear. Dave successfully caught the girl and brought both of them to the surface. Roger and Phil helped haul the girl and Dave onto the rowboat. The fire on the steam yacht was reported to be out, and other rowboats rescued additional people from the water.

Si Doring is determined to find a gold piece. The cruiser Brooklyn has commodious berthing quarters with two complete decks. The Brooklyn can accommodate a thousand men if required. Walter is assigned a hammock between Si Doring and Paul Harbig. Caleb Walton informs Walter that he will take the place of a man named Silvers. The magazines on the ship are kept locked and can be flooded in case of fire. Ammunition for the guns is supplied by a hoist from the magazines.

Laura expressed alarm about the narrowness of the road. Dave managed to turn the touring-car around by skillful maneuvering. Mr. Basswood requested the use of a towing-rope to assist his car. Dave and his uncle retrieved the towing-rope and prepared it for use. The towing-rope strained as Dave advanced the Wadsworth car to pull the Basswood car out of the mud. The Basswood car was eventually pulled out of the mud to the dry roadway. The two cars continued their journey despite worsening weather conditions.

Fred and Jack discussed the oil industry, noting the high risks and potential rewards involved. Jack received a letter from his sister Martha, which mentioned Ruth Stevenson's eye condition. Ruth Stevenson had been advised to consult a specialist regarding her eye health. The eye specialist informed Mr. Stevenson that Ruth was in danger of losing sight in one eye. Mary forwarded a letter from Gif Garrison to Fred, mentioning Nappy and Slugger's potential work with Carson Davenport. Jack received a telegram from his father stating he would remain in Wichita Falls for a few days. The boys observed Carson Davenport arriving in Columbina from the direction of Wichita Falls.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: The Rover boys made friends at Brill, including Stanley Browne, Bob Grimes, Will Jackson, and Max Spangler. Max Spangler was struggling with the language and had failed to advance in his studies, remaining in the sophomore class. Sam Rover was referred to as the hero of the occasion after an incident involving Mr. Fogg. Songbird Powell was absent due to a special errand for Mr. Sanderson, who had a broken ankle. Sam Rover was hoisted onto the shoulders of seniors while other students cheered. Sam expressed regret that his brothers Dick and Tom were not present to share the victory. The students prepared to receive the freshies and sophs by lining up and singing their old song of victory.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Smoke was observed in the harbor entrance in front of the warships. Commodore Schley and Captain Cook were present during the events described. A report was made that enemy ships were coming out of the harbor. The command to clear the ship for action was given by the executive officer. Admiral Cervera decided to attempt to escape from Santiago Bay. The enemy ships included the _Maria Teresa_, _Vizcaya_, _Oquendo_, and _Colon_, along with the torpedo boats _Pluton_ and _Furor_. The American warships involved in the blockade included the _Brooklyn_, _Texas_, and _Vixen_, with the _Iowa_ and _Oregon_ also present.

The Colby Hall nine received applause when they returned from the field. Jack, the young pitcher, experienced pain in his hand but did not want to admit it. Gif expressed concern for Jack's hand and offered to replace him if necessary. The game saw no scoring for four innings despite both teams making four hits. Jack's pitching hand was swollen, affecting his ability to pitch freely. In the sixth inning, a Longley player reached first base after a dribbled ball. Jack struck out the Longley batter to maintain the score.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: The boys, led by Andy and Randy, were sent to a military academy called Colby Hall. Colby Hall was located about half a mile from the town of Haven Point, on Clearwater Lake. The school consisted of a large stone building, a smaller building for Colonel Colby and his family, a gymnasium, a boathouse, and bathing pavilions. The Rover boys became acquainted with several girls from Clearwater Hall, including Ruth Stevenson and May Powell, during a panic at a fire in a motion picture house. The Rover boys helped capture a hidden German submarine and assisted in rounding up the fathers of Nappy Martell and Slugger Brown. Nappy Martell and Slugger Brown were sent to a detention camp after their fathers were imprisoned for aiding the enemy. Jack was made captain of Company C and Fred was made first lieutenant during the annual encampment at Colby Hall.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: A commotion occurred in Professor Asa Lemm's room, attracting the attention of many cadets and teachers. Professor Lemm slipped on broken sheets of ice in his room and expressed confusion about their origin. Cadets Andy, Jack, Randy, Walt Baxter, Spouter, Ned Lowe, and Slugger Brown were among those reacting to the noise from Lemm's room. The door to Professor Lemm's room was locked by Randy, but the key was still in it. When the door was opened, Professor Lemm encountered Patrick, a goat, which charged at him. Professor Lemm fell multiple times due to the ice and the goat's actions in his room. The incident involved a humorous misunderstanding as the boys had dressed up the goat, leading to chaos.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The army was landed at Baiquiri, Siboney, and other points, with Guantanamo reserved as a coaling station for the warships. A strong detachment of regulars and Rough Riders was deployed after the first landing. The battles of La Guasima, San Juan, and El Caney followed the landing of the troops. The landing was complicated by high surf and the potential for a Spanish counterattack. The _Brooklyn_ returned to her position on the blockade after the debarkation was complete. Admiral Cervera commanded a fleet of six ships, including four warships and two torpedo destroyers. The three sister ships of Cervera's fleet, the _Vizcaya_, the _Almirante Oquendo_, and the _Maria Teresa_, each weighed seven thousand tons.

Walter is set to meet Caleb Walton at the New York and New England railroad depot at eleven o'clock. Walter has enlisted and is expected to join the _Brooklyn_. Phil Newell informs Walter that he does not leave until the following noon. George Gimpwell will take Walter's place at the stand for five dollars weekly. Walter writes a letter to Ben stating he has enlisted. The stand where Walter works is located in a niche of the hotel and is closed at night with large shutters. A burly man approaches Walter at the stand and inquires about the best variety show in town.

The captain and commander dine alone, while other officers use the wardroom mess. There are several messes on board, including the steerage mess for midshipmen, ensigns, and clerks, and the master-at-arms mess for yeomen, machinists, and boiler-makers. Gunners dine with the boatswain, sail-maker, and carpenter. The meal served was bread and butter, coffee, cold corned beef, and apple sauce. Paul Harbig, a timid lad, inquired about sleeping arrangements and learned that hammocks are stored behind gratings. Si mentioned that a hammock is preferable to a dirty bunk and suggested tying oneself in if afraid of falling. Si discovered that a ten-dollar gold piece was missing from his satchel and suspected Jim Haskett of theft.

Roger went into the cabin to retrieve a pair of powerful marine glasses. Phil used the glasses to observe a small steamer and reported that there was a fire on board. Mr. Lawrence, the owner of the steamer, confirmed the presence of a fire after looking through the glasses. Mr. Lawrence instructed Phil to call Captain Bradley and to be quick about it. Captain Bradley confirmed the steamer was on fire and ordered a change of course to assist. The steamer in trouble was named the _Eaglet_. Dave Porter was found as a child near the railroad tracks in Crumville and was later taken to a poorhouse.

Mr. Basswood and his friends traveled to Rayville, where they found a hotel with good accommodations. Mr. Basswood went to visit friends in the area, leaving Ben and his companions at the hotel. The hotel at Rayville catered to automobile parties and provided satisfactory accommodations. After dinner, the group discussed their plans to reach Bear Camp the following night. Mr. Basswood returned to the hotel with news about a strange man who had visited Mr. Dobson. The strange man was believed to be Wilbur Poole, who was thought to be out of his mind. Ben and his friends searched for the strange man in Rayville but were unsuccessful.

Si claimed he lost money and believed he should have the biggest say in the matter. Walter expressed doubt about having stolen the gold piece and accused Haskett of being guilty. George Ellis, chief yeoman of the _Brooklyn_, stepped forward to offer information about the incident. George Ellis described seeing a man bending down under a gun, who he later identified as Jim Haskett. Si attacked Haskett after identifying him as the thief, delivering multiple blows. Haskett threatened to get revenge on Si, Caleb, and the others involved. Haskett expressed doubt that the officers would believe the accusations against him.

Porton resembles Mr. David Porter. Ben expressed concern about Dave's situation regarding his identity. Dave felt bewildered and hopeless about the mystery of his identity. Dave anticipated a calamity regarding his identity but was unsure of the outcome. Mr. Appleby approached Dave in a motor-boat to deliver a letter. The letter was mistakenly sent to Mr. Appleby and was intended for Dave. The letter was from Nat Poole, which disappointed Dave.

Crowden is expected to be arrested if he returns to the area after the local authorities and postmaster are notified. Chester Waltham expressed dissatisfaction about not being included in the trip to Riverview. The Rovers planned to travel from Valley Brook to the west through Ashton. The Walthams were left behind when the Rovers visited the Sandersons after leaving the hotel in Ashton. Minnie Sanderson reported experiencing a series of misfortunes, including financial loss and her father's illness. Songbird sent a check for one hundred dollars to Minnie's father, which was a small contribution towards a larger debt. Minnie indicated that her father remains bitter towards Songbird despite the financial assistance.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Walter Russell's adventures while 'Fighting in Cuban Waters' conclude with a focus on American naval efforts. The Russell boys have a large inheritance coming to them. Job Dowling has come to a better understanding regarding the treatment of the Russell boys. Luke Striker is serving as first gun-captain on board the _Olympia_ in Philippine waters. Frank Bulkley is recovering from fever at home and is out of danger. Ben and Larry consider joining the army and navy despite the end of the conflict with Spain. A future volume titled 'Under Otis in the Philippines' will continue the story of the Russell brothers and their acquaintances.

Jack Rover won the race. Randy Rover finished in second place. Dan Soppinger and Walt Baxter tied for third place. Jack Rover broke the previous record by twelve seconds. Randy Rover broke the previous record by ten seconds. Professor Brice announced the results of the race. The crowd cheered for the Rover boys after the race.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Andy brought down the second rabbit while the others shot several squirrels. Jack remarked on the rough ground they were navigating. Randy suggested they stay close to the stream to avoid getting lost. The young hunters brought down several more rabbits and another squirrel over the next hour. They heard a strange noise from behind some bushes and saw a flock of pheasants. Jack and Fred shot at the pheasants, resulting in three birds being downed. The group heard a man's voice calling for help from under a fallen tree.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Jack expressed a desire to have brought a hatchet for making firewood. A man was pinned down under a fallen tree and called for help. The boys found flat stones and a sapling to help lift the fallen tree. They successfully raised the tree enough to free the injured man, Fred. Jack assessed that the man might have broken legs and an arm. The man, identified as Stevenson, indicated he could not walk and suggested Bill Hobson lived nearby. The boys introduced themselves as the Rover boys, with Jack being the oldest.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Sam confronted Chester Waltham about his treatment of Miss Laning. Chester Waltham expressed disbelief at being warned by Sam. Sam threatened to physically confront Chester Waltham if he did not treat Miss Laning properly. Chester Waltham dismissed Sam's concerns and expressed a desire to leave the group. Sam indicated that he did not want Chester Waltham to spoil the trip for Miss Laning or anyone else. Grace vowed never to go out with Chester Waltham again after returning to the hotel. The Rover party discussed their experiences and expressed a desire to part ways with the Walthams.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Jack and Fred skated to Clearwater Hall with Ruth and May. Ruth suggested that Jack invite his sister Martha to Clearwater Hall. May suggested that Fred invite his sister Mary to Clearwater Hall. May mentioned that she had sent a letter to Mary a year or two ago. Slugger Brown and Nappy Martell had left Clearwater Hall and were angry at the Rovers. Jack and Fred expressed confidence in handling any trouble from Slugger and Nappy if they returned. Jack and Fred wished to persuade their sisters to attend Clearwater Hall.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The first automobile was driven by Dick Rover, accompanied by his wife, Mrs. Stanhope, and Mrs. Laning. Chester Waltham and his sister Ada were in a third automobile that was a brand-new runabout. Chester Waltham initially wanted to lead the group but decided to follow the Rovers to avoid leading them astray. The group was traveling on a road that became winding after several miles of straight driving. Sam suggested stopping for dinner at the next town, but Tom preferred to continue to Fernwood for a better hotel. The group stopped at a spring by the roadside to drink water, which was described as pure and cool. Chester Waltham expressed concern about the safety of drinking from the spring due to potential germs.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Dave had his rifle ready and believed he saw a wildcat. Roger and Phil joined Dave and saw a small tawny-colored wildcat emerge from the bushes. Dave shot the wildcat, which leaped into the air and fell back onto a rock. The wildcat managed to escape into the bushes after being shot. Roger prepared to shoot the wildcat again when it reappeared, wounded. Roger shot the wildcat again, killing it as it leaped toward the boys. The boys discovered footprints and a log cabin nearby, indicating they were approaching a habitation.

The Martells, the Browns, and Mr. Werner contributed thirty thousand dollars towards driving two wells on the Spell claim. Davenport, Tate, and Jackson contributed an additional twenty thousand dollars. Mr. Fitch provided a report to Dick Rover indicating potential oil in several locations on the Franklin farm. Mr. Fitch advised Dick Rover to sink at least two wells based on his report. Mr. Fitch offered to invest five thousand dollars in cash for stock in the new company if it was formed with a hundred thousand dollars. John Franklin was granted an eighth interest in the new company formed to exploit the Franklin farm. The Rover Oil Company was formed to exploit the Franklin farm, and efforts were made to gather workmen for the project.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Andy expressed excitement about the animals resembling goats. Randy suggested going downstairs again for another idea. The boys found flat boxes behind the garage that contained thin sheets of ice. Randy proposed taking sheets of ice upstairs to place in Professor Lemm's bed. The boys placed sheets of ice in the bed and on the floor in front of the door. Dan Soppinger warned the group that Professor Lemm was coming upstairs. Asa Lemm slipped on the sheets of ice upon entering his room.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The Rovers are searching for Chester Waltham, who was swept off a bridge. Ada Waltham expresses concern for her brother's safety. The Rovers consult with Mr. Barlow and his son, James, before proceeding. The river is swollen and muddy due to a recent cloudburst. The Rovers decide to use a rowboat to search for Chester Waltham. During their search, the Rovers spot a man caught in a tree. The man in the tree is identified as Chester Waltham, who is injured.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Fred, Randy, Jack, Nappy, and Slugger Brown are characters in the text. Nappy and Slugger Brown claim they are not responsible for Gabe Werner's actions. Jack accuses Nappy of being in league with men who robbed his father. Nappy asserts that he did not know Jack's father had been robbed. Nappy and Slugger Brown state they own an interest in a claim worth ten thousand dollars each. Jack claims that his father was robbed of important papers on the night they were led to the storehouse. Jack suspects that Davenport and his partners were involved in the robbery.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: The attack took place on a road at least seven miles from Knoxbury. The youth who was attacked had an errand to run for Minnie after visiting the bank. The youth spent about half an hour in town after being at the bank. Mr. Sanderson's cutter was left in front of the bank building with the horse tied to a post. Timothy Bray found an extra horse in the woods near the road. The horse found by Timothy Bray belonged to Hoover, the livery stable man. The youth who was attacked recalled seeing a fellow on horseback pass him shortly before the attack.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Five hundred men on the _Brooklyn_ prepared for battle by lowering battle hatches, closing water-tight compartments, and filling fire tubs. The _Iowa_ and _Texas_ fired warning shots, followed by the _Brooklyn_ firing her forward eight-inch guns. The first enemy fire came from the _Maria Teresa_, which fired an eleven-inch shell at the _Brooklyn_. The _Indiana_ fired a shell at the _Maria Teresa_, causing damage. The _Brooklyn_ was headed for the harbor entrance to cut off the enemy's westward flight. The _Vizcaya_ attempted to ram the _Brooklyn_, prompting cries from the crew for a broadside attack. The _Brooklyn_ began to turn in a twelve-point circle to avoid the _Vizcaya_ as it approached.

Andy expressed discomfort about the cold snow getting into his sweater. The group, led by Uncle Barney, proceeded to the lake to skate while dragging a bobsled. Uncle Barney guided the group toward a cove near the upper end of Snowshoe Island. Jack spotted wild turkeys among some nearby trees and alerted the group. Uncle Barney confirmed the presence of wild turkeys and mentioned their scarcity in the area. The Rovers abandoned the bobsled and moved toward the shore to prepare for hunting. The group planned to shoot the turkeys together while remaining quiet and hidden.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Luke returned from signaling another car. Dunston Porter suggested digging under a rock to aid in moving an automobile. Dave proposed using a towing-rope to secure the car to a tree. Dunston Porter and Mr. Basswood worked to loosen the rock holding the wheel. The towing-rope held while the automobile was repositioned. Ben and his friends encountered a cow and its owner at the foot of the hill. The group found a sign indicating Rayville was four miles away.

Walter expressed gratitude to George Ellis for his kindness. The Flying Squadron changed course and headed straight for the coast of Florida. Commodore Schley maintained vigilance to avoid being caught off guard by the enemy. The squadron passed through the Straits of Florida and turned westward past the Florida Reefs. The squadron anchored in Key West Harbor early in the morning. The _Iowa_ is the largest seagoing battleship with a displacement of over eleven thousand tons. George Ellis is the chief yeoman and went ashore to look after some ship's stores.

Dick's brother protested that it would spoil the trip for Dora. Tom suggested sending a telegram to ask if Dick should come home. A telegram was sent, and a response indicated that Dick's father would send for him if needed. The stay in Topeka was extended due to a heavy rainstorm that lasted two days. Sam received a letter from Songbird about his efforts to earn money to repay Mr. Sanderson. The tourists resumed their journey after the storm, encountering damaged roads and washed-out bridges. Reports from a small town indicated significant damage from the storm, including lost livestock and destroyed buildings.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Philip Lawrence is looking for his uncle, Lester Lawrence. Philip Lawrence claims to have good news for Lester Lawrence. Lester Lawrence initially believes Philip's visit is a trick. Lester Lawrence eventually recognizes Philip and allows him to enter. Philip informs Lester that he is innocent of the charges against him. Lester Lawrence has been in hiding since he disappeared. Philip introduces his friends to Lester Lawrence.

Link Merwell was placed in the woodshed of the Wadsworth bungalow. Mrs. Wadsworth assured Link Merwell that he would receive something to eat. Mr. Wadsworth instructed that Link should only receive plain food. Dave received a letter from Nat Poole regarding a young man named Ward Porton. Ward Porton had previously been in town with Link Merwell and was visiting people acquainted with Dave. Nat Poole expressed concern about Ward Porton's intentions towards Dave. Dave felt perplexed and suspicious about Link Merwell's earlier comments regarding his identity.

Randy left a note under Stowell's door as a warning for giving information to their baseball rivals. Andy arranged for Pud Hicks to remain silent about the mice incident. An investigation into the mice incident did not yield any results. Colonel Colby returned to the school and was greeted enthusiastically by the cadets. Colonel Colby informed the cadets that their fathers were expected to return in about ten days to two weeks. Colonel Colby confirmed that Jack's father won a medal of honor during the war. John Franklin and his son Phil visited the Rovers on the campus.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Walter lit a match to check the time on a watch held by a man. The man claimed the time was only eight-twenty. Walter identified the watch as stolen from his uncle in New York. The man's demeanor changed when Walter made the accusation. The man fled down the street when Walter confronted him. Walter pursued the man while shouting for help. The man entered a dark hallway of a tenement to hide.

Randy speculated that an auto with Tate and Jackson had been at the location shortly before their arrival. Jack expressed concern about the lack of control by authorities in the wild country compared to big cities. The nearest oil wells were over a quarter of a mile from the Spell tract, with several wells in operation producing about four hundred barrels per day. The oil from the wells was valued at approximately two dollars and fifty cents per barrel, resulting in a daily revenue of about one thousand dollars. The boys planned to visit a new well that was to be shot off that afternoon, located half a mile away. The foreman of the new well indicated that drilling had reached twenty-six hundred feet with promising indications for oil. The moment the well was shot off resulted in a significant eruption of oil, confirming that they had struck oil.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Andy met Pud Hicks, the janitor's assistant, who had caught many mice in the barn. Pud Hicks planned to drown the mice in the river. Stowell reported to Captain Dale that someone had put a large number of mice in his room. Stowell claimed to have locked the culprit in his clothes-closet. Captain Dale decided to call the janitor and his assistant to help with the situation. Bob Nixon confirmed that the mice likely came from Pud Hicks. A crowd of cadets gathered to observe the events unfolding.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Walter expressed interest in the army of invasion and learned that it had already left Key West. The Seventy-first New York regiment was part of the troops that left for the invasion. Walter's brother is a member of the Seventy-first New York regiment. The marines were engaged in resisting several attacks from the Spaniards throughout the day. A midnight attack by a Spanish column occurred, prompting a call to arms among the marines. Walter joined a company of marines and participated in his first battle. Reinforcements and a warship's support helped the marines repel the Spanish attack.

A man with a bucket of water stopped in front of a cabin door. Phil identified the man as his missing uncle, Lester Lawrence. Lester Lawrence disappeared after a robbery. The boys observed that the man limped and had his left foot bound up. Phil approached the cabin to speak with Lester Lawrence. The man inside the cabin expressed a desire to be left alone and threatened to use a shotgun. Phil confirmed his identity as Lester Lawrence's nephew.

Nappy expresses concern that the Rovers are watching them. Slugger believes they can trick Colonel Colby into punishing the Rovers. Codfish mentions that he has not seen the Rovers going down to town since a punishment. Nappy suggests using spoiled tomatoes, ashes, and ink to create a prank against Colonel Colby. Codfish warns that the ink and bad tomatoes could spoil things. Slugger and Nappy discuss how to execute the prank carefully. Fred and Randy overhear the conversation and consider the actions of their enemies.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Jack sits alongside the fireplace and expresses that he has something on his mind. Jack mentions a young lady who is worried and seeks his help. The young lady's family is experiencing significant trouble that affects her. The young lady has an uncle with whom her family had a quarrel years ago. The uncle refuses to allow the young lady to visit him despite her desire to explain the situation. Jack identifies the young lady as Ruth Stevenson, who attends a school near Colby Hall. Uncle Barney acknowledges his past friendship with Ruth's family before the quarrel.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Walter is looking for a man named Harris. Walter confronts a man who has a watch that was stolen from his uncle. The man insists that the watch is his own and denies stealing anything. Walter attempts to apprehend the man, who struggles and escapes down the steps. Walter catches part of the man's watch-chain as he flees. The thief, Deck Mumpers, is hindered by intoxication during his escape. Walter climbs a nine-foot high gate to continue pursuing Deck Mumpers.

The parade featured many soldiers and was attended by several family members including Fred, May, Grandfather Rover, Jack, Martha, Mary, and Andy. Jack noted that their boys were in the second regiment after the one currently passing. The New York State troops approached, causing an increase in noise as various companies were recognized. Family members spotted their fathers in the parade, with Grandfather Rover expressing excitement and waving a flag. The parade continued for several hours, with Aunt Martha expressing surprise at the number of soldiers. Mrs. Dick Rover offered to take Aunt Martha back to the house, but she insisted on staying until the end. After the parade concluded, the family planned to return home for food, expressing pride in their relative Dick.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dick instructed Tom to stay near the automobile and blow the horn three times if he saw anything. The farmer and his wife stated that they had not had any visitors for several days. The farmer allowed the Rovers to search for the criminal they were pursuing, Blackie Crowden. Tom found a crumpled piece of newspaper that was identified as part of the Knoxbury Weekly Leader. The Rovers concluded that the man who stuttered was likely Blackie Crowden based on the newspaper. The postmaster of Fernwood confirmed that Blackie Crowden had visited several times and was anxious to send letters. The postmaster did not know where Blackie Crowden was staying.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Della Ford's aunt expresses concern about getting into trouble regarding information about Ward Porton. Dave Porter seeks to find out about Ward Porton's background and upbringing. Ward Porton claims to have come from a poorhouse in Maine. Della Ford states that Ward Porton lived with an uncle after his parents died when he was about ten years old. Della Ford believes Ward Porton is a faker and has a gambling addiction. Della Ford found a letter from a man named Obadiah Jones, who expressed frustration with Ward Porton and cut off support. Dave Porter considers finding Obadiah Jones for more information about Ward Porton.

Dan Soppinger asked his friends for the names of the fifth, tenth, and fifteenth presidents of the United States. Andy made a joke about Dan's question, suggesting it was about the first laundryman in Chicago. Dan Soppinger expressed frustration at his friends' inability to answer his question. The Rover boys discussed their plans for the upcoming winter holidays. Gif invited his friends to visit him during the winter holidays. The Rover boys had experienced some disagreements with Professor Lemm. A snowfall occurred on Thursday, leading to good sleighing conditions by Friday.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: A fellow had two strikes called on him and four balls, and took his base, moving Flanders to second.
