source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Walter was assisted by a negro and a Cuban gentleman named Señor Ramona. Walter was offered a grass hammock to rest in due to his illness. Josefina, a negro woman, prepared a herbal tea for Walter. Walter fell into a deep sleep after drinking the tea. Carlos Dunetta mentioned that he could take Walter to the shore, but there was no boat available. Walter expressed concern about his ability to swim back to his ship, which was several miles away. The hut where Walter rested was unusually clean for a typical negro hut in Cuba.

Jack and Walt were called to Colonel Colby's office for questioning. Asa Lemm expressed a desire to have Jack and Walt arrested. Colonel Colby refused to force Jack and Walt to reveal names involved in the affair. The other Rovers and their friends held a meeting to discuss the situation. Andy decided to investigate what was happening in Colonel Colby's office. A group of cadets, led by Gif, marched to Colonel Colby's office to support Jack and Walt. Professor Lemm insisted that Jack and Walt should face severe punishment for their actions.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Sam and Grace visited a jewelry establishment to look for an engagement ring. Sam expressed his desire for Grace to have a ring as nice as those of his friends, Dora and Nellie. Grace was initially hesitant about entering the store for an engagement ring. The jeweler measured Grace's finger and showed them several rings. Sam chose a blue-white diamond ring and requested it to be engraved by the next morning. Sam and Grace celebrated their engagement with their friends at a country hotel. Sam sent telegrams home to inform family about their engagement.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Fred and Andy believe Gabe Werner should be in school. Gabe Werner thinks he is old enough to make his own decisions. Dick Rover expresses surprise at Gabe Werner's presence in the area. Fred and Andy notice two men watching their Uncle Dick closely at the hotel. The boys observe a crowded street with a mix of well-dressed and poorly dressed individuals. A man expresses frustration about losing money in oil wells and indicates he is done with oil fields. Fred and Randy see the same men from the hotel at a restaurant, where they appear to be discussing something with another man.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Gif and Fred attempted to move a rock while observing a healthy fern. Both cadets slipped and fell when the rock was dislodged. A black snake, at least three feet long, appeared after the rock was moved. The cadets threw stones at the snakes, killing one and injuring the other. The injured snake approached the girls, prompting further panic. Gif successfully retrieved the fern despite concerns about more snakes. The group resumed their fern hunting after the snake incident.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: The parade was held in New York City to celebrate the return of soldiers after the war. The Rovers attended the parade along with Grandfather Rover, Aunt Martha, and Uncle Randolph. The parade featured a large crowd that filled grandstands, windows, sidewalks, and side streets. The Rovers carried small flags to wave as the soldiers passed by during the parade. The parade included various regiments representing every State in the Union and featured numerous brass bands. Ruth could not attend the parade due to her poor eye condition, as advised by her doctor. The event was marked by decorations, including flags and the Arch of Victory.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Jake Tate and Jackson plan to sink a well using their own money. Dick Rover does not oppose their plan but withdraws from the conversation. Andy expresses confidence that there is oil on the land. Dick Rover reacts to an insult from Davenport and admits to losing his temper. Nick Ogilvie suggests that many men would have reacted violently to Davenport's remark. Jack suggests looking into the claim owned by John Franklin. Dick Rover plans to talk to John Franklin and his son Phil about the claim.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Lester Lawrence expressed satisfaction after hearing news from Phil and Dave. Phil informed Lester that he would be a free man and have money coming to him. Lester Lawrence had been living in a cabin rented from the daughter of an old hunter. Lester admitted to dressing as a wild man to scare people away from his cabin. Lester Lawrence sprained his ankle while following someone he believed to be one of the boys. Lester saw Link Merwell earlier that morning and chased him away. Lester believed Link took the trail leading to Carpen Falls after being scared.

The youth spent the day trying to observe warships at sea. On the following night, the cave was filled with a dazzling light. The youth concluded that the light was a searchlight from a ship. On the third day, the youth's provisions ran out. The youth found a pistol and cartridges left by Gilberto. While hunting for food, the youth witnessed a battle between Cubans and Spanish cavalrymen. The youth decided to follow a side path leading eastward towards Guantanamo.

The game featured a significant home run that resulted in four runs for Colby Hall. The crowd reacted with excitement, cheering and throwing caps into the air. Tommy Flanders, the Longley pitcher, refused to be taken out despite calls for a change. Colby Hall scored a total of seven runs by the end of the eighth inning. The new pitcher for Longley managed to retire the side without allowing more runs. Colby Hall won the game with a final score of 7 to 2. The cadets of Colby Hall planned a celebration with bonfires and a collation in the gymnasium.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Walt Baxter made a swing and landed half a foot beyond the mark set by Randy. Andy prepared to make the swing while a crowd gathered to watch the performance. Henry Stowell pushed his way to the front of the crowd to see what was happening. Andy accidentally struck Stowell in the shoulder while attempting to swing, causing both to fall. Stowell complained about his shoulder and expressed a desire to report Andy. Andy successfully completed the swing after the incident with Stowell. Dan Soppinger declared Andy the winner of the swing contest after measurements were made.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dick and Sam traveled in an automobile to Brill. Dick mentioned that business in New York was going well despite some difficulties. Grace welcomed Dick and Tom with a kiss and invited them to a special lunch. Tom took the Rover's automobile to pick up Grace and others for a game. Chester Waltham announced plans to attend the game with Ada Waltham and several young ladies. Sam prepared to change into his baseball uniform before the game. A large automobile truck carrying a drum and fife corps arrived at the field for the game.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Walter encountered a man with a small, dark moustache who ran away after an incident. Walter reported the incident to the police at a station where only a sergeant and several roundsmen were present. The sergeant informed Walter that a similar case had been reported from New York, where pawnshops were searched but nothing was found. Walter identified the man as Deck Mumpers, also known as Foxy Mumpers and Swiller Deck, from a photo album of criminals. Deck Mumpers is described as forty-two years old, five feet seven inches tall, and weighing one hundred and thirty-two pounds. Mumpers has a criminal history, including a two-year sentence in Sing Sing for robbery in 1892. Walter provided his uncle's name and address to the sergeant for further communication regarding the case.

The Rovers telegraphed news of a gala event to friends in New York. The second well produced between four and five thousand barrels per day initially, settling down to fifteen hundred barrels. The first well consistently produced at least twenty-five hundred barrels per day. Phil Franklin expressed disbelief at the financial success of the oil wells. The Rover boys returned to New York City two weeks after the first well came in. Ruth, who wore dark glasses, was recovering from an eye condition. The young folks spent time at Valley Brook Farm with Grandfather Rover and Aunt Martha.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Commodore Schley and Captain Cook were present at a small table in the cabin. Walter Russell was questioned by Captain Cook about his absence from the ship since June. Walter explained that he had fallen overboard and had various adventures since then. Commodore Schley asked Walter about the conditions of the trails and the armament of the Cubans he encountered. Walter reported that food and ammunition were scarce among the Cubans and Spaniards. After the interview, Walter returned to his friends who inquired about the meeting. Walter described the meeting as formal, with no praise or handshakes from the officers.

O'Brian's and Smedley's are two hotels mentioned in the text. Dick Rover was advised to try Smedley Hotel for a better class of people. The station master indicated that Smedley's Hotel is located at the end of the boardwalk. O'Brian's Hotel was reported to be very full. There is no taxicab service available in the area. Smedley's Hotel is a new three-story building with a restaurant on the lower floor. The hotel proprietor offered one big room and one small room for accommodation.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dave spotted a village ahead and thought he saw the white steeple of a church. Dunston Porter expressed a desire to find a hotel and garage in the village. A flash of lightning was followed by a crash of thunder and a large tree fell toward the roadway. Dave attempted to stop the touring-car by pressing both brakes, but the car slid on the slippery road. The car collided with the fallen tree, causing a jar that injured Dunston Porter's elbow and cracked the windshield. Dunston Porter asked if anyone was hurt after the collision. An examination of the car revealed a bent mudguard, a broken headlight, and a cracked windshield.

Sam used Mr. Sanderson's horse and cutter to go to the next farmhouse to use the telephone. Sam contacted the authorities in Ashton to report the robbery and requested a doctor. Songbird was knocked down on the road and robbed, resulting in injuries. The lady of the house treated Songbird's wound with home remedies. Songbird expressed concern about the missing four thousand dollars. Spud suggested they use the horse to pursue the robber. Sam cautioned Songbird to remain still until the doctor arrived.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Codfish decided to inform Slugger and Nappy about the incident involving the goats. Codfish found Slugger and Nappy discussing the previous night's events when he arrived. Codfish revealed that he knew who brought the goats into the school. Slugger and Nappy suspected the Rovers, particularly John Rover and Walter Baxter, were involved. Codfish suggested sending notes to Colonel Colby and Professor Lemm regarding the incident. Codfish wrote the notes in a disguised hand but refused to deliver them. Nappy delivered one note to Professor Lemm while Slugger placed the other on Colonel Colby's desk.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Walter and Gilberto traveled down the opposite side of a mountain in an easterly direction. They reached a series of rocks overlooking the ocean, where Gilberto suggested a cave as a hiding place. Gilberto left Walter with food, including bread and jerked beef, and promised to return. Walter never saw or heard from Gilberto or Carlos again. The American warships began bombarding various locations along the coast from Santiago Bay to Guantanamo Bay on June 6. The bombardment damaged Spanish batteries and led to a landing by American marines at Baiquiri. The American flag was hoisted at Guantanamo after the Spanish forces fled to the mountains.

Mr. and Mrs. Wadsworth led the way along a trail that was wet and slippery. The group approached two bungalows that stood a short distance apart. The servant girls came out to meet the group as they arrived. The Basswood family, along with Shadow and Luke, went to the second bungalow. The tourists changed out of their damp garments into more comfortable clothing. Dave, Roger, and Phil shared two rooms, while the girls occupied rooms on the other side of a hallway. Ben and his friends occupied three little rooms at the second bungalow.

Walter is recovering and is encouraged to eat by Carlos and Josefina. Josefina prepares a meal of rice-cakes and strong coffee for Walter. Carlos informs Walter that they are located behind Estrella, halfway to Aguadores on the Guama River. Carlos mentions the presence of a strong Spanish guard in the area and expresses concern about American soldiers arriving. Josefina has a limited English vocabulary, which makes communication with Walter difficult. Carlos warns Walter that Spanish soldiers are approaching and advises him to hide. Carlos and Walter hide in a hollow tree to avoid detection by the Spanish soldiers.

Lemm promised never to bother Barnard Stevenson in the future. Mr. Brown and Professor Lemm agreed to drop their claim on Snowshoe Island. Slugger and Nappy were released and told to leave. Uncle Barney was happy to have the treasure box restored and to resolve his issues with his relatives. The deeds related to the island were recorded and placed in a bank vault. The zinc ore beds on the island were found to be valuable, making Uncle Barney rich. The Rover boys went hunting and had success, bringing in several animals.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Nat Poole knows one of the individuals involved in a road incident and plans to confront him. Nat Poole is the son of a money-lender. Dave and Ben assist Nat Poole in getting his buggy out of a ditch. Nat Poole informs Dave and Ben that Link Merwell is alive and sent him a recent letter from Boston. Link Merwell was not killed in a landslide and had been recuperating in a mining camp. Nat Poole had previously destroyed a letter from Link Merwell without responding. Nat Poole has the letter from Link Merwell in his pocket.

Jack is the captain of the baseball team. Tommy Flanders claims their school will have the finest baseball team in the area. Pete Stevens expresses confidence that Colby Hall will accept challenges from other schools. Jack declines to bet with Tommy Flanders on the outcome of their first game. The group finishes their ice cream and cake before leaving the parlor. The baseball team is preparing for a match against Hixley High in two weeks. Tommy Flanders is noted to be a good pitcher and batsman.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Andy and Fred engage in a pillow fight after Andy throws a pillow at Fred. Jack warns the others to stop rough-housing to avoid being reported. The three boys accidentally knock over a stand, causing books to fall. Gif Garrison enters the room with important news and a morning newspaper. Gif informs the group that Napoleon Martell and Slogwell Brown, Jr. have been given their freedom from a detention camp. The newspaper item about Martell and Brown is located at the bottom of a column on an inside page. The boys express concern about the implications of Martell and Brown's release.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Andy Royce lived in Denver and Colorado Springs several years ago. Andy Royce knew a man named Blackie Crowden who stuttered and had a whistle. Andy Royce believes he saw Blackie Crowden in Center Haven about a week ago. Sam noted that Blackie Crowden's description matched that of a man seen by Songbird at the bank. Songbird expressed frustration about being treated poorly by Mr. Sanderson. Songbird mentioned that Mr. Sanderson told Minnie not to see him anymore. Sam suggested they seek permission from Dr. Wallington to investigate Blackie Crowden.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The grandstand and bleachers filled rapidly, leaving no available seats. Stanley commented on the large crowd, noting it was the biggest they had ever had. Roxley claimed they had a team that could not be beaten. Bob gave final instructions to his team, emphasizing the importance of starting strong. Brill went to bat first, with the first batter striking out. Roxley did not score in the first inning, with all three batters going out. In the second inning, Sam hit a clean ball but did not score.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Minnie expressed concern that the boy was harmed to steal money from him. Sam and Spud provided details about the incident after removing their overcoats and gloves. Dr. Havens examined the boy and determined that his injuries were not serious. Mr. Sanderson expressed regret for sending the boy on the errand with a large amount of cash. Mr. Sanderson needed the four thousand dollars to pay off a mortgage due the next day. The police have been notified about the theft, and telegrams have been sent. Songbird offered to work to make up for the loss of the money, despite not having significant personal wealth.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Dick and Tom are traveling and have reached a city called Pemberton. Mr. Anderson Rover is in New York and is focused on business. The tourists plan to visit Colorado Springs and then return via Denver. In Topeka, Mr. Anderson Rover sent a telegram stating that the Bruno bonds were sold at a profit, but the Lansing deal was uncertain. A telegram from Mr. Anderson Rover indicated that a new opposition led by Chester Waltham has emerged regarding the Lansing deal. The Haverford deal is mentioned as having complications that may affect their investments. Dick considers returning to New York due to the troubling news about the deals.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Dick Rover expressed his distrust of Nelson Martell and his associates. The characters arrived in Texas, which is the largest state in the United States. They were traveling to a small town formerly known as Steerville, now called Columbina. Dick Rover planned to visit Columbina to check on a claim and retrieve documents from a bank in Wichita Falls. The travelers observed multiple oil wells as they approached the oil fields. The cost of sinking oil wells can range from ten to forty thousand dollars, with some requiring depths of three thousand feet or more. Columbina was described as a boom town with limited attractions and basic infrastructure.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Caleb stated that Dewey could not make the boy a captain of marines. Paul mentioned a story about the 'Boy Hero of Havana' saving General Lee's life. General Lee was not in great danger at the time mentioned in the story. The marines had established themselves at and near Guantanamo. Several warships were bombarding Spanish strongholds along the coast. The attack on the fort at Caimanera began at two o'clock in the afternoon and lasted less than two hours. Admiral Sampson planned another attack on the outer defenses of Santiago Harbor.

Ruth Stevenson and May Powell waved to the crowd of cadets. Fatty Hendry made a comment about the race that elicited laughter from the crowd. Professor Brice warned that the ice was not strong enough as the crowd thickened. An ominous crack was heard in the ice, causing panic among the skaters. Jack Rover was thrown down by Fatty Hendry, who contributed to the cracks in the ice. May Powell screamed for help as the ice became depressed beneath her and Ruth Stevenson. The Rover boys, including Jack and Randy, skated to assist the girls from Clearwater Hall.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Walter was captured by Captain Coleo after attempting to escape. The Spanish captain informed Walter that all of his comrades were prisoners in Morro Castle. Walter was provided with a tin cup of guarapo by Captain Coleo. A violent tropical storm began as night fell, bringing thunder and lightning. Walter's hands were bound, and he was allowed to sit beside a wounded negro rebel. Carlos, the negro rebel, suggested they escape during the storm. Walter and Carlos attempted to flee as lightning struck and thunder roared.

Dave assisted Jessie and his sister to alight from the automobiles. The group found a cleared space with green grass and large trees to set up for lunch. The lunch was spread out on a cloth placed on the grass and a flat rock. The lunch lasted about half an hour and was enjoyed by everyone. After lunch, the young people took various photographs. Mr. Basswood noted the appearance of black clouds indicating a storm. The group packed up quickly and started off again as rain began to fall.

The _Texas_ was under the command of Captain John W. Philip and Lieutenant-Commander Giles B. Harber. The _Scorpion_ was a despatch boat with a displacement of six hundred tons and a battery of four 5-inch and six 6-pounders. The signal to weigh anchor was hoisted on the flagship at four o'clock in the afternoon. The Flying Squadron and the collier were traveling at a speed of twelve to fifteen knots. The _New Orleans_ was a warship recently purchased from the Brazilian government, formerly known as the _Amazonas_. The _St. Paul_ was formerly a trans-Atlantic steamer and was commanded by Captain Charles E. Sigsbee. The warships passed the capes a little after seven o'clock in the evening.

Walter expresses a desire to engage in battle similar to Dewey's victory. Jim Haskett feels resentment towards Walter and is envious of his popularity. Haskett falsely believes that he can manipulate the situation regarding a gold piece. Haskett finds a gold piece near Si's bag but does not return it. Caleb instructs Walter and Si on how to clean and oil the gun. Si discovers his gold piece hidden under the gun-track while cleaning. Walter and Caleb are present when Si finds the gold piece.

Colonel Colby ordered some hired help to clean up the melted ice and water on the floor. Asa Lemm found a bundle of clothing that belonged to Walt Baxter in a corner. Asa Lemm claimed the clothing was his and threw it into the clothing closet. Two hired help arrived with pails and mops to clean the floor. Colonel Colby decided to postpone any investigation until the next morning. Jack and Walt returned to Colby Hall and shared their success in returning the goats. Asa Lemm discovered his bed was wet due to sheets of ice placed underneath the covers.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Carson Davenport was pulled back to the station platform by Jake Tate and another man. The crowd surrounded Carson Davenport as he protested against being detained. Jackson took a Gladstone bag from Carson Davenport during the confrontation. A man in the crowd accused Carson Davenport of being a swindler and attempting to leave with money from oil wells. Carson Davenport claimed he intended to deposit the money into a bank at Wichita Falls. The contents of the Gladstone bag were examined, revealing twenty-six thousand dollars and documents belonging to Richard Rover. Corporal John Dunning was involved in a physical altercation with Carson Davenport over the documents.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Nappy Martell expressed eagerness to get tickets for a show. May Powell declined to go with Nappy Martell. Ruth Stevenson indicated that they choose their company when going out. Slugger Brown and Nappy Martell approached Ruth and May, insisting they accompany them to the movies. Ruth Stevenson reported that Slugger Brown had caught her by the arm without her consent. Spouter and Jack confronted Slugger Brown and Nappy Martell about their behavior towards the girls. Slugger Brown dismissed Jack's warning and entered the theater with Nappy Martell.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The Rover Company was incorporated this week. Tom is the secretary of The Rover Company. Dick is the treasurer of The Rover Company. The president of The Rover Company is their dad, who will step down when Sam joins. Songbird is in trouble and needs assistance. Belright Fogg is involved in a case related to a mortgage issue. Sam and Tom are traveling to Brill to discuss Songbird's situation.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Dave applied the foot-brake hard while driving a touring-car. Luke Watson warned Dave about an impending collision by waving a handkerchief. The Basswood automobile's rear-light was visible in the darkness. Dave's car came to a stop on a water-break after swerving to avoid an obstacle. Loose stones were used to block the wheels of Dave's car to prevent it from rolling. The Basswood touring-car was stuck between a rock and a tree after an encounter with a cow. Mr. Basswood explained that a cow caused the accident by blocking the road.

The incident involved a blasting mishap that could have resulted in serious injury. Dick expressed concern about the lack of safety precautions taken by the workers. Tony, the Italian worker, admitted to making a mistake regarding the blasting orders. The gang master ordered Tony to leave the site due to his failure to follow instructions. The man in charge of the blasting expressed regret over the incident and offered to cover any damages. Chester Waltham expressed anger over the situation and suggested legal action for damages. The Rovers were informed that the road would be cleared for them to continue their journey.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Jack knocked on a closed door but received no reply. Randy and Fred expressed doubts about anyone living in the house, noting that the windows were boarded up. The Rover boys searched around the building but found no sign of Nappy and Slugger. Jack observed that the front door was padlocked and concluded the building was likely a storehouse. The Rover boys encountered difficulties navigating back to town due to darkness and mud. They reached the outskirts of Columbina and noted the time was almost ten o'clock. A clerk at the hotel informed them that Uncle Dick had arrived a couple of hours earlier.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Walter wrote a letter to his uncle, Job Dowling, informing him of his enlistment in the navy. Walter expressed concern about the loss of valuable family items, including his father's watch and wedding rings. Walter mailed the letter to Job Dowling without delay. Walter met with several members of Walton's party at the depot before their departure. Walter traveled on a train with a seat-mate named Silas Doring, who was from Maine. Silas Doring expressed his eagerness to join the fight against Spain after the explosion of the USS Maine. Walter felt inexperienced about naval ships compared to Silas Doring, who had experience on merchant vessels.

The four Rover boys were caught in a rainstorm while hiking in the woods near the Rick Rack River. Jack suggested finding shelter to avoid getting soaked under the trees. Fred mentioned a hollow under a cliff at Rocky Bend that could provide shelter. Jack warned that the hollow might be filled with water due to recent heavy rains. The boys had left Colby Hall after lessons for an outing, having been indoors for over two weeks. They were dressed in cadet uniforms, shoulder capes, and rubbers for their hike. Jack was recognized as the leader of the group due to his role as captain of the Colby Hall cadets.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Job Dowling felt nervous and was uncertain about how to interact with the others. Job Dowling instructed Mrs. Graham to prepare extra food, including a twenty-cent pie. Walter and Ben expressed enthusiasm about the pie and their appetite. Job Dowling mentioned that the heirlooms were safe but cost him two hundred and twenty-seven dollars and a half. Larry, dressed in a sailor suit, returned from Hong Kong and joined the family gathering. Larry explained that he returned on a government-chartered vessel carrying troops to the Philippines. Ben stated his intention to pursue a commission in the regular army after his regiment is mustered out.

Rover made a date with Grace Laning for a sleighride if the snow remained on the ground. Sam forgot that the day was set for the annual snowballing contest. Stanley insisted that Sam could not spare both of his chums for Mr. Sanderson's matter. Sam arranged with Abner Filbury to obtain a horse and cutter from the Ashton livery stable. Sam and Spud left the college grounds and headed towards Hope Seminary, which was about two miles away. They encountered a sign indicating that the road was closed due to the moving of the old Jackson barn. Sam and Spud decided to take an alternate road after realizing the original road was closed.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The _Colon_ was faster than the _Vizcaya_ and had not been significantly damaged. The _Vizcaya_ was heavily attacked by the _Brooklyn_ and _Oregon_ during the battle. The _Vizcaya_ eventually caught fire and struck rocks, leading to its destruction. The battle lasted approximately an hour and a half, resulting in the destruction of all but one Spanish ship. The crew of the _Colon_ was urged to increase speed to avoid being sunk. Walter obtained permission to take a break and observed the _Colon_ moving ahead. Si Doring fell overboard during the battle but managed to grab a rope ladder.

The Rover boys attempted to hunt wild turkeys on Snowshoe Island. Jack instructed his cousins to keep their guns pointed at the turkeys and to fire if they started to leave. The wild turkeys flew from the bushes when they noticed the boys approaching. The boys successfully shot two hens and one gobbler during the hunt. Uncle Barney mentioned that wild turkeys are challenging to hunt. The boys planned to send the gobbler home and keep the two hens for themselves. They arrived at a cleared spot with two cabins near a boat-landing on the island.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Barney Stevenson was injured by a falling tree. Jack and Bill Hobson assisted in bringing Barney Stevenson into a cabin for care. Bill Hobson examined Barney Stevenson and determined that nothing was broken but that he had severe bruises. Barney Stevenson has lived on Snowshoe Island for twelve years. Snowshoe Island is located in the middle of Lake Monona and was named for the Indians who once lived there and made snowshoes. Barney Stevenson engages in lumbering during the season and enjoys hunting. Jack inquired about Frederic Stevenson, who is related to Ruth.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: The narrator discusses the need to learn about the ship and its operations. A sailor boards the train at Hyde Park and greets Caleb Walton. The sailor's name is Jim Haskett, a former mate of the _Sunflower_ from Penobscot. Walter expresses a desire not to be assigned to a ship with Jim Haskett due to his reputation. Commodore George Dewey achieved a significant victory over Admiral Montojo on May 1, 1898. The destruction of the battleship _Maine_ in Havana led to increased public anger against Spain. The Cuban rebellion against Spanish rule involved various groups and was led by notable generals.

The cadets surrounded the school janitor, referred to as Plunger. Andy and Randy picked up a shawl and a baby cap to dress the janitor. The janitor was placed in a baby carriage and strapped down by the cadets. A procession was formed with cadets carrying torches, a bass drum, and a fife. A firecracker was set off under the baby carriage, causing it to overturn. The Rover boys received news from their mothers that their fathers were expected home in about ten days. Colonel Colby promised to provide motor-boats for the cadets by Fall.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: A bear was spotted near a cabin, causing excitement among the group. The group discussed organizing a hunt for the bear. Phil expressed skepticism about a claim involving Dave Porter. The boys decided to go out hunting for the bear after lunch. They armed themselves with shotguns and rifles and took provisions. The boys searched through the forest behind the cabin for the bear. They did not find the bear by late afternoon and decided to take a rest.

Walter was passed upon as able-bodied for military service. Walter received a slip of paper signed and sealed by Captain Line for his passage to Fortress Monroe. Walter will travel to Fortress Monroe with Walton and others. Upon arrival at Fortress Monroe, Walter is to report to Lieutenant Lee. Walter must return to Boston to pack his belongings before leaving. Walter informed Mrs. Brown that he had enlisted and would be leaving soon. Walter helped at the news-stand before his departure.

Link Merwell attempted to escape while his hands were tied behind him. Dave, Roger, and Phil pursued Link Merwell after his escape attempt. Link Merwell fell and struck his forehead on a tree root, rendering him unconscious. The boys carried the unconscious Link Merwell toward the brook for assistance. They washed Link Merwell's wound and bound his head with handkerchiefs. The boys agreed to take Link Merwell to the bungalows for further help. Laura and Jessie inquired about Link Merwell's condition upon seeing the group.

Dave and Jessie were canoeing on a lake when they spotted an old log cabin. They observed three or four men and several ladies in front of the cabin. One man was dressed as a woodsman and held an ax raised over his head. Della Ford and Aunt Bess were identified as part of the group in front of the cabin. Dave recognized the group as moving-picture actors from a previous incident on a burning steam yacht. Della Ford expressed surprise at seeing Dave and introduced him to her aunt. Della Ford thanked Dave for saving her life, which made Jessie visibly displeased.

Link Merwell moved away from Dave Porter, expressing fear of being caught by the authorities. Dave Porter explained to Professor Potts that Link Merwell is a criminal who participated in a robbery a year ago. Ward Porton was unaware of Link Merwell's criminal background. Ward Porton traveled to Crumville for business and had previously met Link Merwell on a steam yacht. Link Merwell was on the steam yacht that caught fire. Ward Porton indicated that Link Merwell was taken on by their manager, Mr. Appleby, before their trip. Dave Porter was once placed in a poorhouse as a child, a fact that caused confusion for him and Professor Potts.

The book is titled 'The Rover Boys on a Tour' and is authored by Arthur M. Winfield, also known as Edward Stratemeyer. This book is the twentieth volume in 'The Rover Boys Series for Young Americans'. The series began with the publication of 'The Rover Boys at School', 'On the Ocean', and 'In the Jungle'. Dick and Tom, two of the Rover boys, are married and managing their father's business in New York City. Sam, the youngest Rover boy, is still attending Brill College. The story includes winter sports at Brill College and a significant baseball game featuring Sam. The Rover boys embark on a long automobile tour that includes adventures such as being caught in a storm and a flood.

text: Dave and Roger traveled to Carpen Falls in search of letters. The only letter received was an invitation for Ben to subscribe to a local charity. Dave felt downcast due to the lack of news from Crumville. Roger suggested that Dave might find information about Obadiah Jones in Maine. Phil arrived with his uncle, Lester Lawrence, who had recovered from an ankle injury. Lester Lawrence apologized for his previous behavior and expressed a desire for news from his brother. Phil mentioned a scare he had while cleaning dishes at the cabin.

An old farmer was driving a box-sled filled with milk cans. Sam asked the farmer if he had seen a man driving a horse and cutter rapidly. The farmer confirmed he had seen the man, who was headed straight for Dentonville. The train is due to stop in Dentonville in about fifteen minutes. The distance from the farmer to Dentonville is nearly three miles. Sam and Spud attempted to catch the man who stole Mr. Sanderson's horse and cutter. A blue-coated policeman joined Sam and Spud in their pursuit of the thief.

Ken Ward attends Wayne College to study forestry and faces challenges as a freshman. Ken Ward and Hal take a trip into Mexico to explore the Santa Rosa River and collect specimens. The Redheaded Outfield features three players who incorporate boxing and comedy into baseball. The Last of the Plainsmen tells the story of 'Buffalo Jones,' who preferred capturing wild beasts alive. Roping Lions in the Grand Canyon recounts Zane Grey's experiences capturing lions alive in the Grand Canyon.

Jack suggested that the group jump into the water and hold hands for support. The current was swift, and the cadets struggled to keep their footing as the water reached up to their waists. They reached a point where the water was less than a foot deep and stopped to regain their breath. The cadets used their lessons in bridge building to pull a drifting tree toward the shore. The man and boy trapped by logs were unable to free themselves despite their efforts.

Asa Lemm is a real estate dealer who lost most of his fortune and later became a teacher. The Rover boys are familiar with Asa Lemm and Slogwell Brown. Barney Stevenson has additional old deeds related to the island stored safely.

Sam and Grace left for their wedding trip in a decorated automobile. The guests celebrated with dancing, while older attendees observed with satisfaction. Sam and Grace were showered with rice and confetti as they left for their trip.

The warships are approximately three hundred and sixty feet long and can reach speeds of eighteen to nineteen knots per hour. Each warship carries about five hundred men and has a main battery consisting of two 11-inch Hontoria guns and ten 5.5-inch Hontoria guns, along with a secondary battery of eight 6-pounders, ten 1-pounders, several machine guns, and six torpedo tubes. The _Cristobal Colon_ has a main battery of two 10-inch guns and five 6-inch guns, a secondary battery of rapid-firing rifles, and four torpedo tubes. The blockade has lasted five weeks, and the crew is eager for news from the army of invasion and to engage the Spanish fleet. Fred expressed concern about being put in prison. Dick Rover decided to carry a weapon for protection against oil land swindlers. Carson Davenport was found on the Lorimer Spell claim with several men and oil-well machinery. Davenport claimed that Dick Rover's land claim was no good and demanded proof of ownership. Davenport suggested that the army authorities should investigate Dick Rover's situation.

Some girls from Clearwater Hall expressed a desire to shop in Haven Point before the ride. The boys and girls agreed to meet in front of a moving picture theater in Haven Point. Carson Davenport expressed confidence in obtaining documents related to the claim. Jake Tate and Davenport were aware that Lorimer Spell had died and that Dick Rover was his sole heir. Commodore Schley was sent out to ascertain the location of the Spanish squadron.

Six of Carson Davenport's best workers left the Spell claim within a week to join the Franklin farm. Carson Davenport expressed anger upon learning that six of his men had deserted him. Davenport and his associates were concerned about the possibility of drilling a dry well at the Spell claim. Nick Ogilvie hired additional workers in and around Wichita Falls to replace those who left Davenport. Tom Rover and Sam Rover visited from New York to check on the progress of the oil drilling. Gabe Werner attempted to leave a shooting gallery without settling his bill but was stopped by the proprietor.

Fogg expressed surprise at Sam and Songbird's visit. Fogg hesitated when asked about being in Leadenfield and meeting Blackie Crowden. Sam and Songbird wanted to know if Fogg was connected to Blackie Crowden.

Hixley High lost a baseball game to Longley Academy with a score of 3 to 7. Colby Hall won a baseball game against Columbus Academy with a score of 8 to 3. Jack motioned to Ruth to speak privately about a man named Stevenson.

Minnie supports Songbird when her father criticizes him, which pleases Songbird. Sam considers arranging for his father or uncle to take over the mortgage related to the lost money. Sam leaves college the next day to meet with the police about the robbery.

The letter contained a message that upset Dave and was unsigned. Roger advised Dave to be cautious of Link Merwell's potential actions.

Dave and Ben preferred to travel by automobile instead of by train.

The captain of the steam yacht was upset about the fire, attributing it to carelessness. The first mate reported that the captain would be reluctant to take out another moving-picture company on his vessel. Dave and his friends recognized Ward Porton as the young man they had rescued from the water. Ben commented that Ward Porton resembled Dave, which led to a discussion among the group. The _Eaglet_ resumed its journey to Portland after passing the other vessel. Dave and Roger expressed their anticipation of visiting Mirror Lake, expecting it to be as beautiful as Casco Bay.

Walter was struck on the head by a man who then stole his belongings. Walter lost consciousness after being hit and was later found by a wharf watchman. The watchman initially thought Walter was drunk before realizing he had been attacked. Walter reported that the thief had stolen his uncle's watch and other heirlooms. Walter's uncle had come to New York from Buffalo to sell heirlooms left to Walter and his brothers. The heirlooms included a watch and chain, two gold wedding rings, and a diamond. Walter learned that the time was about three o'clock in the morning when he regained consciousness.

Dave is in Boston. Jessie expressed a desire for Dave to stay in Boston. Dave rescued Della Ford from the sea. Dave plans to visit the old farm with Caspar Potts. Caspar Potts wants to retrieve a box of books from the farm. The Wadsworth library contains many hundreds of volumes. Dave reflects on the changes in his life since leaving the old farm.

Nick Ogilvie and two other oil men were present with Jack and his friends. Jack's father advised the boys to stay in town and avoid trouble. The four young Rovers visited a shooting gallery and held a shooting contest. Jack scored seventeen bull's-eyes, Randy scored fifteen, and Andy scored nine. The boys read about recent oil well strikes that produced twelve hundred barrels of oil a day. Wellington Jonkers approached the boys asking for financial help, claiming to have a profitable oil proposition. Jack and his friends recognized Jonkers as a common type of individual seeking to exploit young investors.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dink Wilsey is considered a great pitcher by the characters in the text. Jack Rover is mentioned as a competitor to Dink Wilsey. Ruth Stevenson received an unsigned letter postmarked from New York City. The letter contains a threat directed at Jack Rover. Jack suspects the letter may have been written by Gabe Werner or Slugger Brown. Ruth expresses concern for Jack's safety regarding the threat in the letter. Jack advises Ruth to keep the letter to herself and not to destroy it.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Mary was spotted by a group who then hurried off in the direction of Haven Point. Jack believed the group did not belong near Haven Point and suspected they had a bad purpose. Martha suggested waiting until night to inform the others about the group. The group began a search for rare ferns in the vicinity of rocks and trees. The girls brought a tablecloth to spread on the ground for their lunch. Ruth explained that the ferns they collected would be beneficial for her home fernery. Jack mentioned that Uncle Barney was living with Ruth and was thankful for the Rovers' help.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Ben called out to inquire about the trouble. Dave indicated that there was a deer by the white birch. Roger spotted the deer after it emerged from the bushes. Dave and Roger shot at two deer simultaneously. One deer fell after being shot by Dave, while the other was shot by Roger. The boys decided to tie the deer together and use saplings to carry them. Dave, Luke, Roger, and Shadow each took part in carrying the deer.

Caleb Walton filled a brier-root pipe with tobacco and lit it. Caleb Walton and Walter discussed their mutual friend Phil Newell. Caleb Walton expressed a desire to keep an eye on Walter. Caleb Walton explained that being on the same ship does not guarantee they will see each other frequently. Caleb Walton intends to be in charge of a gun on the _Brooklyn_. Caleb Walton wants to help Walter get assigned to the gun he expects to command. Walter expressed a desire to learn more about warships.

Two men carried an unconscious negro into a hut while others took charge of a horse and conducted Walter inside. The hut was crowded with insurgents seeking shelter from the rain, and the air was filled with smoke and the smell of stew. Carlos was in poor condition and could only be removed with difficulty by morning. Walter learned that the district was rich in minerals, with large quantities shipped from Santiago and Baiquiri. The Cubans were part of Garcia's army, located many miles north, and were trying to communicate with American warships. Walter and Gilberto started off on horseback after Walter's fever was banished by herbal drinks. Gilberto indicated that the Spaniards heavily guarded the coast at Aguadores and Guantanamo Bay.

The area at the end of the lake is called Bear Camp. The old hunter mentioned shooting a bear in the area last winter. The old hunter believes bears come to the area in the fall for certain roots and herbs. Tad Rason stated that bears and deer do not mix well. Mr. Appleby was negotiating for the loan of rustic furniture from the bungalows. Della Ford expressed delight at the cosiness and beautiful surroundings of the place. Dave proposed taking Della and her aunt in a rowboat while the motor-boat tows it.

The group was traveling over a series of hills with farms and patches of woodland. Tom reduced speed due to uneven terrain filled with rocks. An Italian man waved a small red flag and warned the group to back up due to a blast ahead. Tom stalled his engine while trying to heed the warning. Chester Waltham and his sister were present in the vicinity during the incident. A distant explosion occurred, followed by the sound of stones falling, but no stones fell near the vehicles. The Italian confirmed that the blasting was complete.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The little party was moving through a snowstorm with Uncle Barney and the boys. Uncle Barney expressed concern that the snowstorm could be one of the worst they had experienced. The boys were eager to hunt and did not want to be snowed in. Uncle Barney announced they were in sight of the island and would soon reach a shelter. The group encountered a number of trees and bushes covered in snow as they approached Squirrel Point. Upon reaching the hut, they were surprised to find a full-grown wolf inside. The wolf snarled at the group before leaping away and disappearing into the snow.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Jack reported that several men entered their hotel room and assaulted his father, stealing documents related to the Lorimer Spell claim. Corporal John Dunning, who was staying at O'Brian's Hotel, had the stolen documents and would return them upon proof of ownership. Two under-sheriffs arrived to assess the situation, while some individuals wanted to keep the incident quiet. Jack insisted on the arrest of the man who attacked his father, and Dunning supported this decision. Davenport, Tate, and Jackson were involved in the assault and theft, and Davenport later confessed to the authorities. Davenport was sentenced to prison, and Tate and Jackson were caught three months later and also received prison sentences. The management of the new oil company was taken over by Gabe Werner's father, but the wells drilled resulted in financial losses.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Belright Fogg and Henry Grisley engaged in a verbal dispute lasting approximately fifteen minutes. Henry Grisley expressed his intention to handle the case without a lawyer and stated he would only pay ten dollars for the services rendered. Belright Fogg left in anger after the disagreement with Henry Grisley. Henry Grisley lives on the Millbury road, on the other side of Ashton. Tom offered to take Henry Grisley home after the legal matter was settled. A written agreement was created stating that the mortgage would be taken over by the Rovers within thirty days, with back interest paid and a bonus of twenty-five dollars to Henry Grisley. Henry Grisley received a ten-dollar bill from Tom as part of the agreement.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Tom and his brother ran to another hotel to find Dick. Dick was posting a letter to their father when Tom and his brother arrived. The group planned to capture Blackie Crowden. Tom drove the touring car towards Stockbridge. Grace expressed hope that they would catch Crowden and recover Mr. Sanderson's money. The touring car encountered a faded signboard at a crossroad. The car suffered a puncture due to a sharp stone.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The roads in the section were improved compared to previous conditions. In Pottown, the boys hired an automobile to visit oil wells. The boys observed new oil wells in operation during their trip. Jack suggested visiting the Spell farm to check on its progress. Randy noted that the Spell farm was actively installing machinery. A group of at least thirty men were working on the Lorimer Spell tract. Nappy Martell was seen at the Spell farm, smoking a cigarette.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Mr. Fogg agreed to accept six dollars for three consultations with Dr. Slamper. Dr. Wallington expected to send a check for six dollars to Mr. Fogg. Sam expressed concern about not hearing from Hope. Bob announced a call for all baseball candidates at the gym. Spud invited Sam to walk to Ashton to visit the stores. Andy Royce informed Sam about Blackie Crowden's possible whereabouts. Bissette, a Frenchman, mentioned that Crowden used the telephone at his roadhouse.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Dick expressed concern about finding a safe stopping place during a storm. A severe storm with strong winds, lightning, and thunder was occurring. Mrs. Stanhope questioned the safety of staying under trees during the storm. Ada Waltham approached Dick and reported that her brother Chester was lost after an accident involving a river. Chester's automobile fell into the river when a bridge broke during the storm. Dick and his companions decided to assist Ada Waltham in searching for Chester.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Jack had one of the keys to the room but found it would not fit in the lock. The room was dark, and Jack stumbled over something on the floor. Jack discovered Dick Rover lying on the floor with a cut on his left temple. The boys used a first-aid kit to treat Dick Rover's injuries. Dick Rover was attacked while seated at a table with an open bag containing documents. Randy suggested that the attackers were likely associated with oil-well operations. Jack and the others speculated that Nappy and Slugger were involved in the attack.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: A strange vessel was sighted, prompting crew members to gather on the spar deck. The _Brooklyn_ was already cleared for action with its big guns loaded. The flagship signaled the _Scorpion_ to follow the unknown ship to the southward. The _Scorpion_ identified the unknown ship as the British steamer _Elsie_, bound for Norfolk, Virginia, with a cargo of phosphate rock. The _Brooklyn_ changed its course to southwest by south on Saturday. The weather on Saturday was raw and cold, with heavy mist making it feel almost like rain. Walter learned about the operation of the gun and how ammunition was raised during a long exercise.

Dick Rover expressed excitement about going to college. The Rover boys searched for a fortune on Treasure Isle before attending Brill College. Dora Stanhope, Nellie Laning, and Grace Laning were acquaintances of the Rover boys. The Rover boys and their female friends attended Brill College and Hope Seminary, respectively. The Rover boys acquired a biplane and experienced a flying accident involving a railroad. Tom Rover suffered a head injury during a confrontation with brokers and wandered off to Alaska. Dick Rover planned to marry Dora and take over the family office in New York City.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The boys took turns staying awake to guard against any calls for help during the night. In the morning, the boys found tracks of Uncle Barney's snowshoes leading into the woods, followed by two other tracks. Jack suggested they follow the footprints, and the boys agreed to do so. The boys discovered Uncle Barney's snowshoes among the branches of a tree and followed the footprints to a cave. Inside the cave, they found Uncle Barney, who had been attacked and robbed of his tin box containing important valuables. Uncle Barney reported that he was hit in the head with a rock and lost consciousness during the robbery. The boys decided to help Uncle Barney recover his stolen tin box and valuables.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Walter was in the water after a ship sank and felt lost. He reached a sandy beach between Morro Castle and Estrella Cove. Walter encountered a Cuban named Carlos Dunetta who spoke to him in Spanish. Carlos Dunetta identified himself as a spy for General Garcia. Walter expressed that he was feeling sick and suspected he had malarial fever. Carlos offered to carry Walter to his sister Josefina's hut for care. They arrived at a hut where a woman named Josefina and a man named Señor Ramona were present.

Dave's father is leaving the decision about college entirely to him. Dave expresses a desire to travel like Uncle Dunston. Jessie questions the practicality of traveling all the time. Dave believes he will want to settle down someday. Ben interrupts the conversation about mountains while they are in a car. Mr. Aaron Poole is a rich money-lender who has had differences with the Porters. Nat Poole claims that racing automobiles scared his horse and caused him to end up in a ditch.

Tom asked how many miles it was to Larkinburg, and Chester Waltham replied it was sixty miles. The group decided to leave after lunch to attend a festival in Larkinburg. The festival included a concert, outdoor tableaux, and refreshments. Chester Waltham offered Grace to change places with his sister during the trip, but she declined. Mrs. Stanhope and Mrs. Laning chose to rest at the hotel while the younger group attended the festival. The festival took place in a large grove near a stream, with a stage constructed among trees and bushes. Chester Waltham focused his attention on Grace during the concert, while Sam was occupied with his brothers.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Chester Waltham was in a tree and needed assistance to get to safety. The Rovers, including Dick, Tom, and Sam, came to help Chester Waltham. Chester Waltham expressed gratitude for the Rovers' assistance and inquired about his sister Ada. The Rovers identified a second individual in the tree as Blackie Crowden, a man wanted for robbery. Blackie Crowden was scared and initially refused to come down from the tree. Sam identified Blackie Crowden as the man who robbed their college chum, John Powell. Ada Waltham joyfully greeted her brother upon his safe return.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Jack hauled down the flag after a snowball fight. Randy was hit in the left ear during the snowball fight. The Rover boys visited a hill for coasting and used a bobsled purchased with money from Jack's father. Mike O'Toole is an Irish farmer who sells fruit and milk to the boys. Andy suggested hiring goats from O'Toole to pull the bobsled. The Rover boys planned to take the goats to Colby Hall to show Professor Lemm. Jack expressed concern about the potential trouble from taking the goats into the Hall.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Tom expressed gratitude for being at Brill College and wished success to his peers. Tom took a drink of ginger ale after his speech while others applauded. Sam warned the group to keep noise levels down to avoid attracting a monitor's attention. Tom called on Songbird to share poetry, despite Songbird's reluctance. Songbird recited a poem expressing feelings of despair and loss. The party in Number 25 continued until after midnight, with attendees enjoying themselves. Tom offered to speak to Mr. Sanderson on behalf of Songbird regarding a mortgage issue.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Walter Russell discovered that the slip of paper he received at the navy-yard was missing. Walter's order for a railroad ticket from Boston to Fortress Monroe was also missing. Walter reported that he had lost about twenty dollars, his keys, and cash. The police officer suggested contacting the railroad to detain the bearer of the stolen order. The ticket office confirmed that Walter's order had already been filled and presented the previous night. The police officer speculated that the thief, Deck Mumpers, might sell the ticket at a cut-rate ticket office in Boston. Walter felt distressed about losing the ticket and expressed doubts about his ability to join the navy.

The school janitor was deaf and could not hear the commotion caused by the mice. The escape of two mice prompted students to chase them in the hallway. Captain Dale commanded the students to stop making noise over the mice. Captain Dale discovered that a figure in the closet was a stuffed dummy. Job Plunger asked about the whereabouts of the mice during the chaos. The janitor and chauffeur managed to capture two mice and kill two others. Captain Dale announced that the incident was a practical joke and planned to investigate.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dave Porter at Bear Camp is the eleventh volume in the Dave Porter Series. The book was written by Edward Stratemeyer and published in August 1915. The story involves a vacation at a camp on the shore of a lake. Dave Porter encounters one of his old enemies during the camp. The narrative includes a rescue from fire at sea. The book features various chapters detailing the adventures and challenges faced by Dave and his friends.

Sam did not want to go to college but needed to in order to inherit money from his uncle. Grace expressed disbelief that their days of studying were over. Graduation exercises at Hope were scheduled to take place two days before those at Brill. Grace's family and Sam's family planned to attend the graduation ceremonies. Sam received several graduation gifts, including a diamond scarf pin from his father and a ring from his brother Dick. The graduation exercises at Hope featured girls dressed in white receiving diplomas. Sam expressed sadness about leaving college but acknowledged the need to focus on business.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: A search was conducted for Job Haskers and Blugg, but it yielded no results. Merwell obtained money and traveled East to seek a job. Merwell expressed bitterness towards Dave and his friends and intended to seek revenge. Dave and his friends discussed Merwell's character and potential threats he posed. Nat Poole expressed his desire to cut ties with Merwell and not respond to his letters. Dave advised Nat to write a strong letter to Merwell to clarify his stance. The group expressed concern about Merwell's past actions and potential for trouble.

The _Oquendo_ and the _Maria Teresa_ were both heavily damaged during the battle. The _Maria Teresa_ caught fire and attempted to run ashore. Admiral Cervera's flag was lowered during the conflict. The _Brooklyn_ and the _Texas_ continued to fire upon the Spanish ships. George Ellis was killed instantly while taking range measurements. The _Iowa_ was approaching to assist the damaged Spanish ships. The _Texas_ was unable to keep pace with the chase but continued to engage the enemy.

Thousands of soldiers were transported from Spain to Cuba to suppress a rebellion. A bloody warfare lasting between two and three years resulted in the deaths of thousands of rebels, including Antonio Maceo. Millions of dollars' worth of property, including railroads and plantations, were destroyed during the conflict. The Spanish authorities forced women and children into cities held by the Spanish, where they were neglected and many died from starvation. Nearly three hundred thousand reconcentrados died due to neglect and lack of food before the war ended. The United States sent the battleship Maine to Havana for the protection of American citizens, which later exploded, resulting in over two hundred and fifty deaths. Commodore Sampson blockaded Havana and other ports, cutting them off from the outside world.

Jack expressed a desire to show that he and his friends were keeping up with their studies. The boys received permission to invite Gif and Spouter for the week between Christmas and New Year's. Jack's mother invited Spouter to bring his cousin May and her friend Ruth to visit. The Rover boys received their examination results, with Fred and Randy scoring ninety-four percent, Jack scoring ninety-two, and Andy scoring eighty-eight. The boys participated in an entertainment after their examinations before returning home. Upon arriving at Grand Central Terminal, the boys were greeted by Martha, Mary, and Tom Rover. The boys expressed excitement about returning to New York after their time at Colby Hall.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Asa Lemm was angry after a practical joke involving ice-water was played on him. The steam in the building had been turned off, making the apartment cold. Colonel Colby suggested that the discipline at the school was not strict enough. Andy, Randy, Jack, and Fred discussed the practical joke the morning after it occurred. Codfish, a cadet, witnessed Walt Baxter and Jack taking goats from the school. Codfish considered reporting the incident to Asa Lemm or Colonel Colby.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Jack cautioned the group about the dangers of spraining an ankle or breaking a leg. Randy pointed out a movement in the snow, prompting Jack to take aim and fire. The group saw two minks that were badly wounded after multiple shots were fired. Each mink was over a foot in length, had a soft brown shade, a ridge of black on the back, and patches of white below. The boys decided to return to the north end of Snowshoe Island after some discussion. The boys were surprised when Uncle Barney did not meet them upon their return. The boys lit a lantern as a signal for Uncle Barney and searched around but found no sign of him.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Carson Davenport proposed to wait until he was sure about a situation. The Rover boys recognized Gabe Werner, Nappy Martell, and Slugger Brown approaching them. Nappy Martell questioned Jack Rover about his presence. Jack Rover accused Gabe Werner of trying to escape. A physical altercation occurred between Jack Rover and Gabe Werner. Jake Tate and other men from the restaurant came outside to investigate the commotion. Randy stated that they had a right to walk on the street.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: A storm with lightning and thunder caused a cloudburst, leading to a flood. The floodwaters were rising quickly, coming from a point about a mile upstream. Sam suggested they find higher ground as they were already standing in water up to their ankles. Ada Waltham expressed concern for her brother's safety during the flood. The group decided to move to a little hill to avoid the rising floodwaters. The three Rovers returned to their touring cars to navigate through the flood-covered roadway. They encountered a farmer and his son near their automobiles, who advised them to move their cars to his place.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Thomas Appleby expressed regret for not capturing Merwell when he had the chance. Merwell left his outfit behind and ran into the woods behind the camp. Tad Rason informed that there are no roads within a couple of miles of the woods. Roger mentioned the possibility of Merwell getting lost in the woods. Ward Porton arrived at the camp two hours before Merwell. Mr. Appleby believes Porton is interested in Miss Ford, who does not reciprocate. Mr. Appleby persuaded Porton to stay for a week to finish several dramas.

The boys were competing in a swimming race in Mirror Lake. Ben was initially in the lead, followed closely by Roger and Phil. Phil made a sudden spurt to take the lead from Ben. The four boys reached the goal, a large flat rock, at nearly the same time. A snake was spotted on the rock, causing the boys to retreat into the water. Dunston Porter went to get a shotgun after hearing about the snake. The snake retreated to the rocks further back and did not enter the water.

Sam and Dora, as well as Tom and Nellie, planned to go on an auto tour from New York. Grace expressed excitement about the auto tour and suggested inviting Songbird and Minnie. Sam hopes to graduate and aims to perform well for the Rover family. Nellie and Cousin Dora left school to get married, motivating Grace to do her best. Miss Harrow has apologized for suspecting Nellie of taking a diamond ring. Andy Royce, the gardener, has returned to work at the seminary and has changed his behavior. Sam encountered Andy Royce in Knoxbury, where Royce wanted to discuss a robbery incident.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: The captain of the vessel is identified as the captain of the steam yacht. The first mate of the _Eaglet_ confirms the captain's identity. Fireworks on board a moving picture company vessel caused smoke and confusion. The fire was mostly smoke and was contained in a zinc-lined compartment. Della Ford expressed a preference to board a steamer bound for Portland rather than return to the yacht. The stout man rescued from the water mentioned that they were part of the Appleby Film Corporation. Ward Porton thanked the young men for their assistance and acknowledged his earlier decision to jump overboard.

Colby Hall features a gymnasium, boathouses, bathhouses, a stable, a barn, a garage, a vegetable garden, and numerous farm fields. The Rover boys arrived at Colby Hall and found several friends, including Dick Powell and Gifford Garrison. Dick Powell is the son of Songbird Powell, and Gifford Garrison is the son of Fred Garrison. Walter Baxter, the son of Dan Baxter, was also among the Rover boys' friends, despite his father's past enmity with the older Rovers. Jack Rover had a quarrel with Napoleon Martell, a student at the military academy, who, along with Slogwell Brown, caused trouble for the Rovers. Colby Hall is located about half a mile from Haven Point, and Clearwater Hall, a girls' boarding school, is situated on the other side of town. Jack Rover developed an interest in Ruth Stevenson, while Fred Rover often interacted with May Powell.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on Snowshoe Island

text: Ward Porton is the nephew of Obadiah Jones, the son of his youngest sister, Clarice Jones Porton. Obadiah Jones disowned Ward Porton due to his poor behavior, including smoking, drinking, and gambling. Ward Porton was placed in the Lumberville poorhouse after his mother died. Obadiah Jones provided Ward Porton with a good education and attempted to help him succeed. Ward Porton left Obadiah Jones's care to pursue a career in acting and later in the moving-picture business. Dave sought information about Ward Porton's identity and shared his concerns with Obadiah Jones. After discussing the situation, Obadiah Jones agreed to sign a document stating the facts about Ward Porton.

Dr. Wallington granted Sam permission to leave the college. Sam and Songbird traveled to Center Haven in an automobile belonging to the Rovers. The automobile had heavy chains on the wheels to navigate snowy roads. The main building of the hotel in Center Haven was closed, with only a small wing open for transients. The hotel proprietor informed Sam and Songbird that Blackie Crowden had been discharged two weeks prior. The hotelkeeper described Blackie Crowden as lazy and mentioned he had stolen clothing from the hotel. Songbird identified Blackie Crowden as a suspect in a robbery incident involving four thousand dollars.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Walter sustained a deep cut on his left cheek and was placed on a swinging cot. The medical man confirmed that Walter would live but had a narrow escape from serious injury. The fighting on land was fierce, with the army of invasion taking various outposts of Santiago. Walter expressed relief that he and his comrade Si were unharmed after a close encounter with death. On Sunday morning, preparations were made on the flagship _Brooklyn_ to rest after a tiring bombardment. The _Brooklyn_ was located about three miles out from Santiago Bay, near the _Texas_. Commodore Schley was in sole command of the blockading fleet while Admiral Sampson was away.

Fred expressed concern about being late to Captain Dale. Jack believed Captain Dale would excuse their tardiness once he learned the truth. The four cadets took shelter from the storm under overhanging rocks. The heavy rain was causing the mountain torrent to become more violent. The cadets observed a chicken-coop floating down the stream, indicating flooding upstream. The boys heard cries for help coming from up the river. They discovered a man and a boy in danger of drowning amidst wreckage in the stream.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: A festival was held in a grove decorated with lanterns. Grace commented on the chilly weather and mentioned she left her jacket in the automobile. Sam went to retrieve Grace's jacket while Chester Waltham seated himself next to Grace at a table. Sam returned to find all seats filled and was surprised to see Chester Waltham beside Grace. Nellie and Dora discussed Chester Waltham's actions regarding the seating arrangement. After the festival, Sam expressed his fatigue and started to walk away from Grace and the others. Chester Waltham invited Grace to ride with him, and Ada Waltham confirmed that Grace could take her place.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Job Dowling wrote a letter to his nephews, expressing his intention to pay two hundred dollars if their heirlooms are recovered. Walter took a quarter of an hour to decipher Job Dowling's poorly spelled letter. Caleb expressed concern about a close call involving Walter's brother during a battle. Walter noted that everything on the ship _Brooklyn_ operates smoothly under normal conditions. Larry wrote that he was currently in Hong Kong and uncertain about his future deployment. The arrival of General Shafter's army was announced, with over thirty transports and nearly seventeen thousand troops. The transports were escorted by fourteen warships, and the crew celebrated the arrival.

Caleb noted that Haskett made many friends among the crew. Walter was initially afraid that the executive officer would hear about his encounter with the crew. The officers of the Flying Squadron were focused on the potential movements of Spanish ships. Commodore Schley speculated that the Spanish would target Cuba or Porto Rico. Rumors circulated about a Spanish submarine that could threaten shipping along the eastern seacoast. On May 12, a fierce fight occurred in the harbor of Cardenas, resulting in casualties including Ensign Worth Bagley. Dewey gained a foothold in the Philippines while Rear-Admiral Sampson had shifted his focus.

Minnie expresses distress over the situation involving Blackie Crowden and the missing money. Dora and her cousins discuss the news about Blackie Crowden with Minnie. Mr. Sanderson doubts that the money will be recovered from Blackie Crowden. Sam defends Songbird, stating it was not his fault that he was robbed. Dora worries about the impact on Minnie if her father forces her to stop seeing Songbird. Ada Waltham announces a grand festival in Larkinburg that evening. Grace expresses enthusiasm about attending the festival after hearing from friends.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Jack discussed Ruth's condition with Mrs. Crews, expressing concern for her well-being. Doctor Borden treated Ruth and was optimistic about her recovery, advising caution regarding her eyes. Jack's sister, Martha, confirmed that Doctor Borden believed Ruth would recover in a few days. The Rovers successfully passed their examinations at the end of the term. Ruth no longer wore a bandage over her eyes but still needed to avoid strong sunlight and reading. Colby Hall closed several days before the girls' school, allowing the Rover boys to visit their sisters. Jack and Ruth planned to keep in touch despite her eye condition.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Dave expressed interest in possibly participating in a moving-picture production. Jessie inquired about Dave's intentions regarding acting in the movies. Dave wanted to ask Mr. Appleby about Link Merwell, who is a criminal. Jessie expressed her disapproval of Miss Ford, an actress, and her behavior. Jessie suggested returning to the bungalows due to the warm weather. Dave and Jessie were in a canoe on Mirror Lake. Jessie felt that Dave was angry with her regarding Miss Ford.

Sam was recognized as the hero of the snowballing contest for capturing the banners of the freshies and sophs. Tom arrived at the grounds and was greeted by several students. Tom announced that he could only stay until the next noon due to his business commitments. William Philander Tubbs returned from Boston and was mentioned by Spud. Tom expressed excitement about seeing Tubby and recalled past practical jokes played on him. The boys reported to Dr. Wallington, who allowed Tom to stay with them for the night. Sam confirmed that he and Songbird had captured the banners and were guarding them from being taken.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys on a Tour

text: Many tracts believed to have oil have proven to be dry. Men spend between ten to forty thousand dollars to sink a well. Lorimer Spell's land is suspected to have oil based on his papers and letters. Dick Rover intends to investigate oil land in Texas after being mustered out of the service. Martha mentioned a story about poor farm people in Texas who became wealthy due to oil wells. The group expressed a desire to accompany Dick Rover to Texas if he goes. Dick Rover's departure was for Hoboken to arrange private affairs before leaving.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
source.title: The Rover Boys in the Land of Luck

text: Walter struck Haskett on the chin, causing Haskett to stagger against a gun-carriage. A crowd of about fifty sailors gathered to watch the altercation between Walter and Haskett. Haskett accused Walter of being a thief, which Walter denied. Caleb intervened to prevent Haskett from hitting Walter again. Haskett threatened Walter, stating he would remember the incident. Walter sought to find Cal Blinker to discuss the situation regarding a gold piece. Si Doring reassured Walter that he believed in his innocence regarding the gold piece.

The highest officer on a warship is the captain. An admiral is the highest officer in any navy and commands all naval vessels. In the United States Navy, the offices of vice-admiral and admiral have ceased to exist. A commodore commands a squadron of warships, while a captain commands the ship. The executive officer, or lieutenant-commander, is responsible for the crew's conduct and various drills. Salaries for naval officers vary, with a commodore earning five thousand dollars a year and a rear-admiral six thousand when at sea. Warrant officers include positions such as boatswain, gunner, carpenter, and sail-maker.

The boys arrived at the little station at Rockville and were assisted by a porter. The porter accepted a tip from the boys and wished them success on their hunting tour. Uncle Barney Stevenson greeted the boys at the railroad station and insisted they call him 'Uncle Barney.' The boys did not bring provisions with them, planning to buy supplies in town. Uncle Barney offered to help carry their baggage to Crumpers' boathouse. The boys had a list of supplies for their trip, which was approved by Uncle Barney. Uncle Barney warned the boys about an impending snowstorm as they prepared to leave.

source.author: Edward Stratemeyer
