Mr. Tredgold expressed a desire to see the world before aging limits his ability to do so. Captain Bowers warned Mr. Tredgold against searching for a specific island, suggesting he sell his schooner instead. Miss Vickers felt anxious about the purchase of the schooner and sought to discuss it with Mr. Stobell. Mr. Chalk prepared for the voyage by purchasing firearms and practicing shooting in his garden. The travelers met on Binchester platform on August 20th after the alterations on the Fair Emily were completed.

Mr. Chalk was digging in the garden when he noticed a girl's head with a large hat. Mrs. Chalk was standing inside the open French windows of the drawing-room. Mr. Chalk began to whistle a popular air while working in the garden. Mrs. Chalk informed Mr. Chalk that a friend was whistling for him. Mr. Chalk initially thought the whistling was a bird. Mrs. Chalk commanded Mr. Chalk to go down and speak to the whistling figure. Mr. Chalk struggled to maintain a cheerful demeanor during breakfast the next morning.

Mr. Kybird expressed concern about the time it takes to get married. Mr. Smith suggested that Mr. Kybird arrange for young Teddy to be married by special license. Mr. Kybird noted that special licenses cost approximately thirty pounds. Miss Kybird commented on the deceitfulness of the plans being discussed. Nathan Smith reassured that the plans were for Teddy's own sake. Mr. Kybird planned to approach Teddy and keep the marriage a secret. Mr. Kybird intended to find Mr. Silk alone to discuss the matter.

Cap'n Naskett is attempting a record trip from New York to Liverpool in a small boat. Cap'n Naskett accuses another captain of attempting to kidnap him while he was asleep. The other captain claims he had a supernatural warning to pick up Cap'n Naskett. Cap'n Naskett demands to be returned to his boat or he will pursue legal action. The two captains engage in a heated exchange while chasing Cap'n Naskett's boat. Cap'n Naskett expresses his disdain for the crew and makes sarcastic remarks about them. The skipper expresses disappointment after learning that Cap'n Naskett reached Liverpool safely.

Mr. Jenkins expressed that he had suspicions about who committed an unspecified act. Mr. Drill indicated he did not want to be called as a witness. Mr. Gunnill poured a glass of ale for the constable. The old man sat outside the Cauliflower with a jug of beer and a churchwarden pipe. Bob Pretty was described as a sly and artful man who never did an honest day's work. After Squire Brown died, a wealthy gentleman named Rockett took his place and invested in rearing pheasants. Bob Pretty was suspected of poaching, but he was never caught.

Mr. Vickers expresses surprise at Mr. Tasker's lack of knowledge about money given to Selina for new clothes. Mr. Tasker denies giving any money to Selina, stating that it is not his responsibility to buy clothes for her children. Mr. Vickers suggests that Selina did not inform Mr. Tasker about the money. Mr. Vickers requests a glass of water from Mr. Tasker, who fills it from the dresser. Mr. Tasker mentions that the water is not safe to drink except in tea or coffee. Mr. Vickers asks Mr. Tasker to lend him a small amount of money for a short period. Mr. Vickers claims that borrowing two pounds would allow him to make five pounds in a week.

Hezekiah Lewis is the captain and part owner of the schooner Thames. The schooner Thames was bound from London to Aberdeen. Hezekiah Lewis proposed to a young lady five times without success. Mr. Rumbolt is a stout, red-faced man who is troubled by his daughter Kate. Mr. Rumbolt described himself as 'chick-pecked' by his daughter. Mr. Rumbolt's daughter appeared while he was laughing with Hezekiah Lewis. Hezekiah Lewis invited Mr. Rumbolt's daughter to visit the Thames.

Dixon instructs Bob and Charlie to leave while allowing the old man to stay for a month. Dixon counts out money for Bob as old Burge and Mrs. Dixon enter the bar. Mrs. Dixon exhibits a change in demeanor after Dixon asserts his authority. Mr. John Blows is dismissed from his job by the foreman for sleeping on the job. The foreman insults Mr. Blows, suggesting he should bury his face in the backyard. Mr. Blows reflects on his dismissal while walking home and notices the state of his house. Mrs. Blows reacts with distress upon learning of her husband's job loss.

Captain Hardy expresses indifference towards how Captain Nugent came aboard his ship. Captain Hardy suggests that Captain Nugent's presence may be due to a drunken mistake or an attempt to escape trouble. Captain Hardy instructs Mr. Prowle to take Captain Nugent forward after a physical altercation. Captain Nugent is known to have served under Captain Hardy's command in Sunwich. Captain Nugent seeks an interview with Captain Hardy to secure a position on the ship. Captain Hardy refuses to treat Captain Nugent as a passenger and states he is a stowaway. Captain Nugent attempts to regain his composure after his conversation with Captain Hardy.

Mrs. Stobell expressed that her husband, Mr. Stobell, was very attentive and caring towards her. Mrs. Chalk mentioned that Mr. Stobell was unselfish and did not complain when Mrs. Stobell stayed with her mother for six weeks. Mrs. Stobell recalled that Mr. Stobell sent her three telegrams in thirty-five minutes when she visited her mother. Mrs. Chalk noted that Mr. Stobell never caused her any uneasiness and that she could trust him. Captain Bowers became moody and lost hope regarding a treasure that had become a forbidden subject. Mr. Tasker injured himself while chopping wood and had to be taken home. Selina Vickers visited Captain Bowers to help him while Mr. Tasker was away.

Tredgold and Son is a land and estate agency located on High Street in Binchester. Tredgold senior left the office early, while Tredgold junior delegated most of the work to a clerk. Mr. Tredgold observed a girl searching for an address outside his office. The girl, identified as Miss Drewitt, requested the key to a cottage in Dialstone Lane. Mr. Tredgold informed Miss Drewitt that her uncle, Captain Bowers, was expected on the next train. Mr. Tredgold accompanied Miss Drewitt to the cottage, pointing out local features along the way. Miss Drewitt demonstrated the ability to open the cottage lock easily, contrary to Mr. Tredgold's initial concerns.

Miss Vickers visited Mr. Tredgold regarding a matter of land. Miss Vickers is interested in an island. Mr. Tredgold stated that Miss Vickers is not a rich woman. Miss Vickers possesses a map of Bowers's Island. Captain Bowers claimed to have burnt a map of the island. Mr. Tredgold proposed that they fit out a ship to recover the treasure. Captain Bowers is to receive an equal share of the treasure without any expense.

The listening circle took place at the Peal o' Bells. Mr. Carter expressed concern about a potential death-warning. Mr. Carter called for more beer and requested gin to be added. The committee of the Ancient Order of Camels reacted calmly to Mrs. Blows's request for funds. Mr. Blows expressed dissatisfaction with the committee's handling of his money. Mrs. Blows returned in tears after speaking with the committee. Mr. Blows contemplated using the money to open a pub.

Captain Nugent has a son who is indebted to Mr. Kybird for lodging. Mrs. Kybird is a stout, sandy-haired lady who has been observant of her husband for thirty years. Mr. Kybird offers Mr. Nugent a cup of tea upon his arrival. Mr. Kybird has a room available for rent at half a crown a week. Mr. Nugent shares stories of his adventures in Australia with the Kybird family. Mrs. Kybird expresses her opinion that Mr. Nugent is a nice young man. Mr. Kybird speculates about the potential relationship between Mr. Nugent and his daughter, 'Melia.

Ginger Dick and Peter Russet went out for a drink after an incident involving old Isaac. Ginger Dick spent all his money at a pub and expressed frustration about it. Old Isaac was asleep in his bed when Ginger Dick and Peter Russet returned. Ginger Dick searched old Isaac's belongings for money but only found a few trivial items. Ginger Dick threatened old Isaac to get his money back. Old Isaac reluctantly got out of bed to address Ginger Dick and Peter Russet's demands. Old Isaac prepared to fight after being pressured by Ginger Dick and Peter Russet.

Mrs. Kingdom began to count the days until her niece's return from London. Mr. Kybird appeared before the magistrates for the second time regarding the purchase of stolen property. Jack Nugent gave evidence in Mr. Kybird's case, which was reported in the Sunwich Herald. The captain brooded over his wrongs after his daughter's return and walked towards the harbour. The whaler Seabird was high out of the water and beautifully rigged after a collision with a fishing-boat. The captain envisioned his son waving farewell from the deck of the whaler as it left the harbour. The captain visited Mr. Wilks to seek assistance for a plan concerning his son.

Master Hardy stopped attending church. Master Hardy participated in a beach play, portraying David. Mr. Wilks expressed a desire to end Master Hardy's situation. Captain Nugent confined the elderly steward to the house after a meeting. The old servant required Master Hardy's attention due to her poor health. Captain Nugent decided to send Master Hardy to live with his Aunt Mary in London. Captain Nugent sold the house and kept some furniture for himself.

Ginger shared a bed with Peter Russet and kept him awake by talking about his romantic experiences. Peter Russet informed Sam that the girl Ginger was interested in was a barmaid at the Jolly Pilots. Ginger expressed his distress over the girl, stating he could not eat or drink due to his feelings for her. Peter Russet mentioned that the girl had previously been involved with a prize-fighter named Bill Lumm. Sam suggested that Ginger could pretend to be a prize-fighter to impress the girl. Ginger decided to follow Sam's advice and planned to visit the Jolly Pilots with Peter Russet. Ginger ordered port wine at the Jolly Pilots, believing it to be more sophisticated than beer.

A crew member jumped onto the deck and ran below deck. The second mate took control of the wheel and pointed to starboard. A large creature resembling a telegraph pole emerged from the water about two miles away. The skipper suggested firing a gun at the creature, but the mate advised against it. The skipper ordered all hands on deck despite his brutal nature. The creature was estimated to be about a hundred yards long and appeared to be peaceable. The crew fed the creature loaves of bread and a hunk of pork.

Mr. Cutts did not respond to Bob Pretty and left in anger. Keeper Lewis contracted rheumatic fever while watching for Bob Pretty. Mr. Cutts broke his leg while attempting to get over a fence. Keeper Smith was left to manage the situation alone and sought help from the squire. Bob Pretty was in a good mood despite the circumstances and was whistling while walking. Three men, including Mr. Cutts and Keeper Lewis, pursued Bob Pretty as he carried a sack. Bob Pretty threw the sack into Farmer Pinnock's pond before being caught.

Mr. Kybird and Mr. Smith are discussing the upcoming wedding banns, which will be put up next week. Mr. Smith expresses a belief that true love is better than money and suggests he should remain silent about the wedding. Mrs. Kybird enters the room and invites Mr. Smith to sit down. Mr. Smith mentions that he has been at Mr. Swann's house and that Mr. Swann is making his will. Mr. Swann's will is a matter of over ten thousand pounds and has been kept a secret until his passing. Dr. Blaikie was the other witness to Mr. Swann's will, which does not leave anything to Mr. Kybird or his family. Mr. Swann has left his estate to a young man who was jilted in love.

The captain is named Crippen. Pepper is an ex-pilot and a friend of Crippen. Crippen has been a sailor all his life. Pepper wants Crippen to act as Cap’n Budd, who was lost in the Dolphin thirty years ago. Martha is the name of the woman involved in the plan. Pepper believes that if Crippen acts as Cap’n Budd, he will reclaim Martha. Crippen initially hesitates but is persuaded by Pepper to consider the plan.

Mr. Cooper's brother-constable, Police-constable Jenkins, confronted Mr. Gunnill in a room. Police-constable Jenkins accused Mr. Gunnill of damaging his helmet and truncheon. Mr. Gunnill stated that he lent the items to young Sims as a joke. Mr. Drill suggested that Mr. Jenkins could get into trouble for lending the items. Mr. Drill offered to attempt to repair the broken helmet in the kitchen. Miss Gunnill assisted Mr. Drill with the repair process. After the repair, Police-constable Jenkins was astonished to find his helmet restored.

Mr. Stobell requested Mr. Chalk to provide his opinion on cigars. Mr. Tredgold informed Mr. Chalk that they needed to go to the ship immediately. Captain Brisket sent a message for Mr. Chalk to calm the men on board. Mr. Chalk expressed concern about a possible mutiny. Mrs. Chalk waited for Mr. Chalk's return while adjusting her cap and gloves. Mrs. Chalk noticed the Fair Emily hoisting her sails and expressed disbelief that it could be their ship. Mrs. Chalk and the others hurried downstairs to pursue the departing schooner.

Miss Nugent was overjoyed to see her father approaching. Captain Nugent expressed indignation over Master Hardy frightening his daughter. Captain Hardy refused to punish his son for the incident. Captain Nugent threatened to take the law into his own hands if Captain Hardy did not punish his son. Captain Hardy warned Captain Nugent that a physical confrontation could occur if he touched his son. Captain Hardy ordered his servant Jem to show Captain Nugent out.

Mr. Nugent and Miss Kybird engage in a conversation at a shop. Jack Nugent attempts to sell items to Miss Kybird, who refuses to buy them. Mr. Kybird enters the shop after hearing raised voices. Mr. Kybird offers three shillings for the items presented by Jack Nugent. Jack Nugent accepts the offer of three shillings and requests a smile from Mr. Kybird. Jack Nugent reveals he has returned from Australia and expresses nostalgia. Miss Kybird inquires about Jack Nugent's father and his plans to stay in Sunwich.

Stobell and Mr. Chalk left the boat and walked along the beach. The other men took the stores out of the boat and pitched a tent. Mr. Chalk felt lonely as he watched the boat depart. Mr. Chalk expressed a desire for someone to keep watch during the night. Mr. Stobell fell asleep after dinner, while Mr. Chalk remained awake with a revolver. Mr. Chalk heard noises outside the tent and attempted to wake Mr. Stobell. The tent collapsed after a wild yell, prompting the men to flee in fear.

The skipper fled below deck and instructed the crew to hide portions of their breakfast for him. The crew returned with minimal food for the skipper after a hearty meal. The wind was against the ship for two days, resulting in little progress. Mrs. Harbolt spent most of her time on deck, which confined her husband below deck. The skipper experienced despondency and hunger, remaining mostly in his bunk. On the third night, the skipper waited for Mrs. Harbolt to retire before speaking with the mate. The crew expressed dissatisfaction with the skipper's treatment, leading to a tense atmosphere on board.

Mr. Cutts and Bob Pretty are involved in a discussion about a sack that was thrown into a pond. Bob Pretty initially ran because he thought poachers were after him. Keeper Lewis is tasked with retrieving the sack from the pond. Bob Pretty expresses reluctance to enter the pond due to concerns about cold water and efts. Lewis enters the pond but struggles to find the sack. Mr. Cutts and Smith physically restrain Bob Pretty when he attempts to leave. Lewis eventually exits the pond without retrieving the sack.

The captain expressed pride in his children, mentioning one is engaged to marry the daughter of a man in Sunwich. The captain's daughter reassured him that she would not do anything to displease him. Hardy chose to take the sea road to avoid a chance meeting with the Nugent family. Mr. Wilks described his current life as one of being out early and home late, often having dinner away from home. Mr. Wilks mentioned that a woman frequently seeks his advice and has been borrowing his frying-pan. Mr. Wilks planned to visit Captain Nugent that afternoon. Mr. Wilks indicated he knows Captain Nugent well and would look for an opportunity to help.

The characters waited for a week before returning to Dialstone Lane. Edward Tredgold informed the company that he had saved five and ninepence. Miss Drewitt announced that the map had been found that morning. Captain Bowers displayed the map, which was drawn in lead-pencil on aged ruled paper. Mr. Chalk expressed interest in the map and inquired about a specific mark on it. Edward Tredgold counted out coins and expressed disappointment over losing a bet. Miss Drewitt felt uncomfortable during the exchange about the bet and Tredgold's finances.

The late master and owner of the ship is missing. George is acting as the captain of the ship. An intruder arrives and greets George on the deck. George informs the intruder that he was found dead and buried recently. The intruder claims to have been drinking and lost track of time. The intruder's wife has been aboard the ship for the last two trips. George expresses confusion about the situation and the intruder's claims.

The captain and crew were confused about the identity of their ship. The captain initially believed they were on the SMILING JANE. The crew revealed that the ship was actually the MARY ANN. The captain expressed distress over having taken the wrong ship. Church bells in Wapping and Rotherhithe were ringing at mid-day. A captain and mate were astonished to find their ship missing. The MARY ANN had left at half-past one in the morning.

Belinda has home lessons to do and expresses that they will take her all evening. Mrs. Wheeler insists that Belinda should take her books out despite her protests. Mr. Wheeler commands Belinda to obey her mother while expressing a desire for quiet. Mrs. Wheeler suggests that Mr. Wheeler should smoke his pipe outside. Poppy Tyrell is asked by Mrs. Wheeler to discuss her son Bob's relationships. Mrs. Wheeler describes Bob as a good son who has not yet married at the age of twenty-three. Poppy Tyrell firmly states that she will not marry Bob, regardless of Mrs. Wheeler's comments.

The farmer claims that young Pascoe has been pursuing his daughter Celia. The farmer locked young Pascoe in his stable and believes he has the right to do so. Mr. Hogg supports the farmer's decision to keep young Pascoe locked up. Mr. Quince confirms that the farmer has the right to lock his stable and keep individuals out. The shoemaker advises the farmer to lose the key to the stable as a precaution. Mr. Hogg expresses satisfaction with the shoemaker's advice. Several individuals in the group display emotional reactions during the discussion.

The new mate ordered Joe to help scrub paintwork. Joe refused to comply with the mate's order. Captain Barber was waiting on the quay when Fraser arrived. Fraser expressed concern about a recent incident involving the skipper. Joe claimed he was on deck shortly before the skipper fell overboard. The mate admitted to sending Joe below deck before the incident occurred. Captain Barber reflected on the loss of his sister's son, Fred.

The captain handed Mr. Stobell a glass. The captain set light to a map at Cape Silvio. The captain claimed that the flame converted Mount Lonesome into a volcano. Mr. Stobell expressed his disapproval of the captain's laughter. Mr. Stobell left the gathering after expressing concern for orphans and widows. Miss Drewitt was displeased with the antiques in her room. The captain discovered that a map he believed he had burned was actually missing.

The captain and his son discuss the ongoing enmity between the captain and Captain Nugent. The captain expresses indifference towards the quarrel with Nugent. The captain's son believes the enmity has lasted long enough and should end. The captain mentions that Nugent's daughter, Kate Nugent, has grown up to be good-looking. Young Murchison, the new doctor, is rumored to be favored by Kate Nugent. Jem Hardy is determined to prevent Dr. Murchison from marrying Kate Nugent. Mr. Adolphus Swann discovers Hardy's intentions regarding Kate Nugent while searching for a document.

The skipper plans to be away for at least six months on a Norwegian barque bound for China. The mate expresses concern about the skipper's mental state due to his love affairs. The skipper intends to fake his own death and will be locked in his state-room. The mate is instructed to inform others about the skipper's supposed death gently. The skipper has withdrawn £40 for wedding expenses, which he expects to lose. The skipper wants the mate to check on Poppy during his absence. The mate is reluctant to face Poppy and finds the situation morally questionable.

Miss Drewitt and Mr. Tredgold are having a conversation in the garden. Mr. Tredgold expresses his intention to model himself after the captain. Miss Drewitt expresses skepticism about Mr. Tredgold's transformation. Mr. Tredgold claims to have hidden sense that he can reveal. Miss Drewitt decides to go indoors, indicating she is not interested in continuing the conversation. Captain Bowers is surprised by Miss Drewitt's hasty entrance into the sitting room. Mr. Tredgold expresses a desire to talk sense once indoors.

DIALSTONE LANE is a work by W. W. JACOBS published in 1911. The text includes a table of contents with multiple chapters and illustrations. Illustrations in the text depict various scenes and characters, including Mr. Chalk and Captain Brisket. Mr. Tredgold is a character who prepares to draw up an agreement. Mrs. Stobell and Mrs. Chalk are mentioned as characters in the text. The narrative includes references to a treasure and discussions about it. The setting includes locations such as a quay and a garden.

Mr. Tredgold is expected to visit in the afternoon. Miss Drewitt believes that Captain Brisket will find the treasure. The captain expresses doubt about the treasure being found. Mr. Chalk struggles to recall Mr. Stobell's remarks from the previous night. Mrs. Chalk sends a note to Mrs. Stobell and waits for a reply. Mr. and Mrs. Chalk plan to visit Mr. Stobell at five o'clock. Mrs. Stobell is surprised to learn about the yachting trip.

Mr. Chalk expressed concern about Mrs. Chalk not eating. Mrs. Chalk indicated that eating would choke her. Mr. Chalk noted that Mrs. Chalk did not look well. Mrs. Chalk mentioned that age is not an excuse for Mr. Chalk's behavior. Mr. Chalk was curious about a girl who whistled over the fence. Mr. Tredgold invited Mr. Chalk to his house for a meeting that evening. Miss Selina Vickers was revealed to be a new client of Mr. Tredgold during the meeting.

Miss Tyrell attempted to escape from the captain's arm as he entered the room. Flower began recounting his adventures but paused when the captain entered. Flower described his struggle to swim towards a ship after falling overboard. Flower was picked up by a Russian brig bound for Riga and later worked his passage home. Flower shipped on a full-rigged ship named Golden Cloud bound for New Zealand. Flower plans to marry Poppy Tyrell in New Zealand. Flower shipped under the name Robert Orth after buying another man's discharges.

The protagonist stood in the center of the room, experiencing a sudden idea. He opened a window and then left the house deep in thought. The next morning, he boarded a train for London and watched Sunset Bay from the window. He took a Bayswater omnibus to Poplar, where he noticed strange changes in the landscape. Upon arriving at a small house, he inquired for Cap’n Crippen and was welcomed by a big man with light blue eyes. Pepper expressed his troubles with his ill-tempered wife to Cap’n Crippen. Cap’n Crippen suggested that Pepper try being sarcastic to manage his wife's temperament.

Jemmy Machiavelli claims to be ill and dying while in Joe's bunk. The skipper expresses concern for Jemmy's health and suggests he stay in bed. Jemmy refuses breakfast and expresses worry about Mrs. Harbolt coming down. Mrs. Harbolt descends to check on Jemmy despite his protests. Jemmy fabricates a story about a gentleman in the other bunk to prevent Mrs. Harbolt from approaching. Mrs. Harbolt is surprised to learn about the presence of the captain in the bunk. Jemmy escapes to the deck just as the captain reveals himself to Mrs. Harbolt.

Mrs. Tipping and Fraser engage in a game of three-handed cribbage after the cook leaves the cabin. Fraser expresses concern about Mr. Robinson's whereabouts and suggests he may be dead. Mrs. Tipping insists she does not believe Mr. Robinson is dead. Fraser reveals that Mr. Robinson can be found at 17, Beaufort Street, Bow. Mrs. Tipping decides to take some crew members with her to find the captain. A cab is hailed to take Mrs. Tipping and her daughter to Beaufort Street. The cabman expresses surprise at the number of people at the gate and suggests they could sit on each other's laps.

Mr. Chalk expressed admiration for the captain's decision to not pursue half a million dollars. Mr. Tredgold stated that the captain could not access the treasure because he left it behind when rescued. Mr. Tredgold suggested that the captain wanted Mr. Chalk to make an offer for a treasure expedition. Mr. Tredgold proposed combining business with pleasure for a potential treasure hunt. Mr. Stobell expressed suspicion about the idea of combining business with pleasure. Mr. Tredgold indicated that if the captain agreed, they would find the money and divide the treasure equally.

Mr. Duckett and Brisket discuss returning a ship and a map. Brisket expresses a desire to send Captain Bowers to search for treasure. Mr. Duckett suggests it is better for others not to know the island does not exist. Mr. Duckett recounts being overpowered by men who forced them to steer to an island. Brisket and Mr. Duckett took the map and returned to rescue the owners but found them gone. They shipped four white men at Viti Levu and sailed for home. Brisket and Mr. Duckett plan to visit Mr. Chalk at Dialstone Lane.

Hardy thanked Mr. Wilks and took a chair behind the door. Mr. Wilks had not had such an attentive listener in sixty years. Hardy expressed a desire for Mr. Wilks to visit him on Tuesday. Mr. Wilks returned with a jug and glasses after mentioning hospitality. Miss Nugent arrived late and recognized Hardy. Hardy reminded Miss Nugent of a past encounter involving Mr. Wilks. Miss Nugent expressed indifference towards past childhood acquaintances.

Bob Pretty is confronted by Mr. Lewis and Keeper Smith, who find two brace of partridges in his coat pocket. Bob Pretty resists being taken by the keepers but is ultimately forced to accompany them to Cudford. Policeman White warns Bob Pretty that anything he says could be used against him. Bob Pretty claims he has a clear conscience and states that the keepers stole his partridges. Bob Pretty admits to putting the partridges in his pocket and shows a bill from Mr. Keen, the poulterer. Policeman White decides not to lock up Bob Pretty and hands the partridges back to him. Squire Rockett hires a new head-keeper named Cutts, who is reputed to be effective against poachers.

Captain Nibletts transferred his belongings to the schooner during the day. Ben expressed concern that Captain Nibletts would not be the same after his experiences. The crew engaged in various tasks such as tarring the rigging and scraping the masts. The cook attempted to create a dish under Ben's supervision, which did not please the crew. Mr. William Green used chalk to write on a frying pan, causing laughter among the crew. Ben, the mate, became frustrated with the cook over the chalk marks on the frying pan. The mate took on the additional duty of inspecting pots and pans, which annoyed the cook.

Mr. Tredgold used to visit a man and bring him tobacco. The man promised Mr. Tredgold that he would have the tobacco when he was done with it. Mr. Tredgold has not seen the man for some time and mentioned that he gave up smoking. Miss Drewitt stated that the man is dead. Mr. Tredgold mentioned that the carving was intended for the man's room. Captain Bowers entered and invited Mr. Tredgold to stay for tea. Mr. Chalk entered the room leading Mr. Stobell after a brief commotion outside.

Joe expressed his aversion to a certain type of person while placing his mug on the counter. Mr. Green suggested that Tommy wash his face and mentioned soap in Charlie's bunk. Mr. Green responded to the fireman's question by saying he wanted a banjo. The unexpected response from Mr. Green led to a physical altercation in the bar. Fraser intervened to help Mr. Green during the fight and later returned home to play cards with his father. Mr. Green left for London with visible injuries from the fight, while the fireman expressed a desire to have done more. Fraser experienced a change in mood during his time in London, leading him to wander the streets and visit places associated with Flower and Miss Tyrell.

Flower passed through the wood and crossed the fields towards London using his knowledge of the stars. He traveled at night and slept during the day, reaching the city in three days. Flower pawned his watch and chain in Stratford and had nearly eighteen shillings before taking a train to Liverpool Street. He secured cheap accommodations in the Mile End Road and decided not to risk sending another letter until he understood the connection with the Tipping family. The Wheeler family had few secrets, with younger members freely sharing each other's misdeeds. Mrs. Wheeler was anxiously awaiting the return of Miss Tyrell for a private conversation. Mr. Bob Wheeler left for work in a bad mood, which affected his interactions with his family.

Joe experienced fits while at the wheel of the ship. The skipper instructed the crew not to let the sea-sarpint see Joe's face during his fits. The crew arranged to catch the sea-sarpint the following morning. Joe clutched the foghorn during a fit, causing a disturbance on the ship. The sea-sarpint vanished after the commotion caused by Joe's fit. Matilda Bunker stood at the open door of a house attached to a wharf in St. Katharine's. The ground-floor office of the house was deserted except for a housemaid sweeping.

Mr. Gunnill expressed astonishment at an event involving Mr. Sims and Mr. Cooper. Mr. Sims claimed to have thrown Mr. Cooper down from behind. Miss Gunnill invited Mr. Sims to help her draw beer in the kitchen. A loud noise was heard in the living-room, prompting Miss Gunnill and Mr. Sims to investigate. Mr. Gunnill was seen jumping in the air while Mr. Drill encouraged him from an easy-chair. Mr. Sims discovered a damaged policeman's helmet and a truncheon. Mr. Drill indicated that the helmet did not belong to Cooper.

Mr. Chalk placed his foot on Mr. Stobell's toe and bore heavily. Mrs. Chalk insisted that she would not go unless Mrs. Stobell went. Mr. Stobell expressed concern about taking his wife into danger. Mrs. Stobell initially did not want to go but eventually agreed to accompany her husband. Mr. Chalk and Mr. Stobell discussed the purchase of a schooner with Mr. Tredgold. Captain Brisket awaited their arrival at the ferry-boat.

George Vickers, aged six, experienced distress from being washed multiple times. Mr. Vickers attributed his daughter Miss Vickers's condition to love and spoke of it with more indulgence. Miss Vickers's period of abstraction lasted three days before she returned to her usual self. Miss Vickers confronted her father about sending Bill Russell to get beer while he stood outside the Horse and Groom. Mr. Vickers denied sending Bill Russell for beer and claimed he could stand where he liked. Miss Vickers ordered Mr. Russell to drink the beer he had, which he did reluctantly. Miss Vickers decided to take care of the Horse and Groom the following day and watched her father leave.

Mr. George Burton is a naval pensioner living in Seacombe. Mr. Burton was approached by a tall man named Joe Stiles. Joe Stiles did not recognize Mr. Burton at first due to his lack of a beard. Mr. Burton expressed that he deserved his pension. Mr. Stiles mentioned he did not receive a pension. Mr. Burton produced a bottle of whisky and glasses for a toast. Mr. Burton has a friend named Mrs. Dutton who disapproves of public houses.

Mrs. Silk suggested having 'just 'alf a glass' of something, but Mr. Wilks insisted on 'not a drop.' Mr. Edward Silk became upset and left the room after Mr. Wilks thumped the table and Mrs. Silk complied with his request. Mrs. Silk expressed concern that Mr. Edward Silk was jealous of Mr. Wilks. Mrs. Silk mentioned that Mr. Edward Silk was still affected by the loss of Amelia Kybird. Mr. Wilks enjoyed his supper and expressed a desire to sit by the fire all night. Mr. Wilks fell asleep in an easy-chair and was unable to be roused by Mrs. Silk. Hardy felt dismissed by Miss Nugent and faced hostility from Captain Nugent during their encounters.

The ship is involved in the lace and brandy trade. Miss Rumbolt refuses to marry Captain Lewis. The crew expresses concern about Miss Rumbolt's feelings towards Captain Lewis. Miss Rumbolt is given the key to the state-room at eight o'clock. The weather conditions on the ship change from a light breeze to calm seas. Miss Rumbolt releases a bear on the ship, causing chaos among the crew. Hezekiah attempts to protect Miss Rumbolt from the situation on deck.
