Le Fort employed a tailor brought by the Danish embassador from Copenhagen to make two military suits. The tailor completed the first suit in two days, which Le Fort wore to meet the emperor. The Czar was surprised by Le Fort's new uniform and praised its design and Le Fort's efforts. Le Fort later appeared in the uniform of a common soldier, which the emperor also examined and found superior for military use. The emperor expressed a desire to have a company of guards dressed in the new style and requested Le Fort to organize it. Le Fort successfully organized a company of fifty men, clothed in the new uniform and properly drilled, which impressed the emperor.

A mother must understand that obedience in children is not natural but must be taught through education. Children have a natural instinct to seek their mother's presence for comfort and security. A mother's failure to instill obedience in her children is her responsibility, not the children's fault. The process of teaching children to obey requires systematic effort from the mother. Three methods can be employed to encourage obedience in children, each requiring different levels of skill from the mother. The first method requires steadiness, calmness, and perseverance, while the second and third methods require more mental resources and ingenuity.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: William and other boys discussed the implications of eating chestnuts before they had time to grow. The master explained that eating small chestnuts would result in less meat in them. The boys believed that if chestnuts were good, they would pick and eat them while small. The master noted that prickles around small chestnuts serve to protect them from boys and animals. The master described how the hard brown shell of the chestnut keeps it dry and protected. The master compared chestnuts to apples, explaining that apples are sour before they are ripe, which deters animals from eating them. The lesson concluded with the master asking Roger to stay behind for a private discussion.

The master appointed committees with two members each to assist with a task. The boys were instructed to create a written memorandum of their findings. The reports submitted by the boys included the number of nails and the number of scholars. The teacher aimed to engage the pupils in the management of the school. The teacher may eventually have various officers and committees to handle different responsibilities. The school can become organized like a society or legislative assembly. The teacher must ensure that the arrangements do not consume too much time.

The fashions at the Russian court one or two hundred years ago were considered awkward, inconvenient, and ridiculous. Ladies wore dresses with sleeves that were ten or twelve yards long, which were drawn up in a puff on the arm. The customary greeting between ladies and gentlemen involved the lady throwing the end of her long sleeve to the gentleman. Nobles, or boyars, moved about the city in grand processions attended by a long train of servants and retainers. The Czar implemented reforms to change the slow-moving processions of the boyars and set an example by moving quickly through the streets. The Czar limited the number of attendants the boyars could have and sent excess attendants into the army if necessary. The Czar's reforms aimed to enhance his power and efficiency as the sovereign of the country.

Communication should be made through an indifferent person to allow the ambassador to express his real opinion freely. Peter the Great asked the ambassador about Le Fort's language skills, noting that he speaks very good Russian and German. Le Fort had learned German and Russian quickly after arriving in the ambassador's service four months prior. Peter the Great expressed his desire to have Le Fort in his service and formally appointed him as his first interpreter. Le Fort was about thirty-five years old while Peter was not yet twenty, leading to a strong bond of trust between them. Le Fort served Peter the Great until his death, rising to great distinction and playing a significant role in public affairs. Le Fort introduced improvements in the dress and equipment of the troops, changing the old-fashioned Russian uniform.

There is a difference among parents regarding the religious education of children and the role of Divine intervention. Some parents believe that true repentance and desires to conform to God's will require a special act of Divine intervention. The powers and capacities of the human soul are also considered to be the result of God's creative agency. The commencement of divine life in the soul is viewed as a special work of the Divine hand. The moral and religious sentiments in children do not develop early and should not be expected to awaken too soon. Animal instincts develop first in young beings, followed by higher attributes of the soul. The development of instincts in young animals occurs in an order that serves the individual's needs.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Parents should avoid inflicting punishment by violence when influenced by irritation or anger. The memory of punitive actions may cause painful retribution in the future. Parents may find comfort in reflecting on their gentle training methods after the loss of a child. Children's faults may stem from their immature mental or bodily development. Parents should maintain authority over their children but can achieve this through gentle measures. Some mothers feel their children are ungrateful despite their sacrifices and efforts to win their love. Children often seek parental support in times of trouble but may not consider their parents' comfort in return.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Deliberate disobedience to a parent's commands requires different treatment than simple ignorance. The principle of influencing human character by commending right actions is universally applicable. Commending positive behavior can encourage individuals to repeat such actions. Many errors and mistakes in children arise from ignorance rather than willful wrongdoing. Mothers need to discern whether a child's actions stem from ignorance or intentional disobedience. Boasting can stem from childish ignorance, as seen in the example of Johnny and his cousin Jane. Children's reasoning abilities develop slowly and are often not supported by appropriate instruction.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Conservatives prefer to preserve existing institutions and resist change. The Church and clergy opposed Peter's proposed improvements and reforms. The plotters in Moscow communicated with the patriarch and leading ecclesiastics. Priests accompanied the Guards to encourage them and assure them of divine support. General Gordon ordered artillery to fire over the heads of the Guards to intimidate them. The Guards were ultimately defeated in battle, with thousands killed and captured. General Gordon executed every tenth prisoner and tortured officers for information.

Georgie's mother seeks to influence his behavior through commendation and encouragement. She finds appropriate moments to discuss behavior with Georgie when he is calm and attentive. Georgie's mother explains the difference in noise preferences between children and adults. She emphasizes that adults prefer children to enter rooms quietly and politely. Georgie expresses his intention to open and shut doors quietly. His mother proposes a plan to help him form the habit of entering rooms quietly. The plan involves Georgie stepping back and re-entering quietly when he makes noise, without punishment.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Each scholar is responsible for maintaining her own place in proper condition. The jury writes 'guilty' or 'not guilty' on a paper, which is returned for sentencing. Sentences typically involve confinement to the seat or require slight effort for the public good. The court influences both amusement and order but does not handle serious school business. Sessions of the court are held outside of school hours and are not considered a core part of school arrangements. The school emphasizes moral and religious influence over the pupils, aiming to foster Christian principles. The Principal seeks to create an atmosphere of piety and moral principle among the students.

The teacher discussed the issue of tardiness among students. The teacher proposed that all tardy students should lose their recess. The teacher acknowledged that some students may be tardy for valid reasons. The teacher expressed concern about the fairness of punishing all tardy students equally. One student suggested that written excuses could be required for tardiness. The teacher identified several objections to the written excuse plan. The teacher noted that written excuses may not accurately reflect the reasons for tardiness.

The influence of pleasure is more effective than pain in teaching children. Children often make mistakes due to ignorance of the laws of external nature and material properties. A boy may break a knife while trying to bore a hole due to a lack of understanding of the material's strength. A girl may spill milk while carrying a pitcher because she does not understand the laws of momentum and oscillation. Accidents involving children are often not due to evil intent or carelessness, but rather to their immature knowledge. Disobedience may be a fault in children, but the resulting damage is not necessarily a reflection of carelessness. Accidents among children can be compared to similar misfortunes that occur among adults.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Students are encouraged to propose changes to their study plans as needed. Students prepare their lessons at their convenience and are expected to be ready for recitation. Some students mark study and recitation times on their schedules to regulate their school time systematically. Students can choose to join fewer classes in case of ill health, allowing them to focus on preparation. Teachers assess students' claims of insufficient time to ensure they are not overloaded with classes. Students are assigned to a limited number of classes initially and can request to add more after a few days. The focus of recitation is on understanding and digesting material rather than memorization.

Peter the Great expressed admiration for the military skill of the Swedish generals. Peter restored the swords of the Swedish officers and presented his own sword to one of them. Peter had a habit of drinking excessively, which may have influenced his generosity. The Swedish officers were held as prisoners but were treated with relative liberty. Mazeppa escaped with the King of Sweden and was never captured despite a reward offered by Peter. Peter was promoted to major general due to his bravery during the battle of Pultowa. The text introduces Empress Catharine and outlines her life events from 1709 to 1715.

Impenitence and earnest entreaties can harden hearts and confirm habits of sin. Religious instruction can cover a multitude of subjects for pupils at stated times. Children can understand ordinary language if the subject is within their comprehension. Children learn the meaning of words through their connection in sentences rather than definitions. Simplifying language can disgust young persons and prevent their interest in the subject. Children feel mortified when treated as if they cannot understand what is within their reach. Making efforts to simplify language can hinder children's language learning.

A mother may express annoyance at a visitor but then greet them with false pleasure in front of her children. Fathers may also deceive their wives in front of their children under certain circumstances. Such behaviors teach children that deception is justifiable in some cases, undermining trust in others' honesty. Children raised by parents who do not lie may struggle to understand wrongful ways of deception without instruction. Some children develop a strong sense of truthfulness at a young age, while others may not remember their early learning process. The distinction between reality and imagination is often unclear for young children, complicating their understanding of truth. Adults can also confuse memories of real events with vivid mental images, leading to honest but incorrect testimonies.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Peter did not seriously intend to learn shipbuilding but sought to be a nominal workman for personal enjoyment and learning opportunities. Travelers visiting Holland often go to Saardam to see the building that Peter occupied, which is a small wooden structure in poor condition. An outer brick building has been constructed around the original hut to protect it from further decay, featuring large open arches for visibility. The area surrounding the hut has been landscaped as a garden and is enclosed by a wall, which includes a cottage for the custodian. While in the shipyards, Peter was known to the workmen, who were instructed not to gather around him or interfere with his activities. Peter made private visits to friends in Amsterdam, preferring to socialize with individuals known for their knowledge or success in commerce and navigation. Peter's demeanor with friends was blunt and often rough, and while he was admired for his intelligence and energy, he did not form real friendships.

Parents should reserve the decision-making authority on vital matters affecting their children's welfare, such as health and education. Parents should ascertain and consider the feelings and wishes of their children regarding important decisions but should not engage in discussions about the decisions themselves. Parents may explain the principles and reasons behind their decisions, but this should not occur when a practical question is pending. Children should be allowed the largest possible indulgence in non-vital matters to promote their development. Parents should assess children's requests based on real objections rather than personal preferences. Parents often decide first and then hear children's requests, which contrasts with the judicial approach of hearing cases before making decisions.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Children can engage in serious conversations about their play, which enhances their enjoyment. Joining children in their play fosters a closer bond of sympathy between adults and children. Moral lessons can be effectively conveyed through children's play and imagination. Individuals without formal authority, such as uncles, aunts, and older siblings, can influence children positively. Visitors in a family can sometimes gain more influence over children than their parents through gentle and indirect methods. Using imagination is an important means of gaining influence over children. Direct admonitions may cause discomfort in children, while indirect approaches through imagination can be more effective.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Aunt Jane and Mary were walking together when Aunt Jane decided to return home instead of going to the village. Aunt Jane altered her mind about the walk because Mary did not obey her instructions. Mary claimed that the grass was dry where she walked and did not cause any harm. Aunt Jane expressed that she does not feel safe with children who do not obey her. Aunt Jane explained that while no harm was done this time, there could be danger in other situations. Mary promised to obey her aunt in the future and asked to continue the walk to the village. Aunt Jane chose to abandon the walk without scolding Mary and instead engaged her in other activities.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The speaker emphasizes the importance of honesty and sincerity in communication. The boy expresses a commitment to improve his behavior and not trouble the speaker again. The speaker has found direct and frank communication effective in resolving disciplinary issues in most cases. The speaker outlines several necessary conditions for successful communication, including deliberation, indulgence, firmness, and openness. The speaker notes that delicate communication can enhance the sensitivity of pupils' feelings. The speaker advises that if initial communication fails, more vigorous measures may be necessary.

When a bullet strikes a solid wall, its movement is converted into heat. The amount of heat produced is proportional to the mechanical motion that is stopped, depending on the bullet's weight and velocity. The quantity of heat produced is equivalent to the mechanical motion that was extinguished in the bullet. Force cannot be destroyed but can be converted into another form or stored in a latent state. A perfectly elastic spring can be bent and held in that position until released, at which point it exerts the same force used to bend it. Nature stores force on a large scale through vegetation, which receives and stores energy from the sun. Animal life expends the stored force from vegetable productions for its functions.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: A large sheet of paper displayed a series of lessons for writing, starting with straight lines and progressing to letters. Each pupil was provided with a writing book made of three sheets of fool's-cap paper, which they were required to rule themselves. Pupils had to practice each lesson until they could write it well before moving on to the next lesson. The teacher examined the pupils' work and marked it with 'Passed' or 'P' if it met the required standards. Specific requirements included that the page must not be soiled or blotted, no paper could be wasted, and no leaves could be torn out. A set of arbitrary marks was created to indicate various faults in the writing, which were applied using red ink. A catalogue of these marks was made available to all pupils to assist in understanding the criticisms of their writing.

The teacher must ensure that the whole class is prepared through reasonable evidence. Different methods can be employed to assess the class's preparedness efficiently. One method involves each student spelling a word individually, which does not accurately reflect their overall preparedness. Another method requires students to write dictated words on slates and spell them aloud, allowing for a thorough examination of the class. The latter method enables the teacher to assess the entire class effectively and quickly. Training classes to operate with precision can enhance the effectiveness of teaching methods. The text illustrates the importance of collective assessment over individual assessment in educational settings.

A teacher should act as a protector and friend to students who are burdened by depression and discouragement. Teachers should be interested in all their scholars and aim to secure the progress of each student equally. Every student has a mother who loves them and deserves attention in a school established for the common benefit of all. Teachers should not attempt to make all pupils alike, as human minds are meant to differ. The teacher's aim should be to cooperate with Providence and bring out the natural powers of each student. Teachers must avoid trying to create a uniform model of excellence for their pupils, as this can lead to wasted time and effort. Teachers should not allow the faults or needs of any individual student to take up an excessive amount of their time.

Peter established a central office at the capital for the collection of revenues. Collectors were appointed for all provinces of the empire to report directly to the central office. The old governors lost power due to the reforms and complained about the changes. Peter mandated changes in the dress of the people, requiring them to adopt Western European styles. A tax was imposed on beards, requiring gentlemen to pay a hundred rubles annually to keep them. Customs officers were ordered to fine or cut the long dresses of individuals entering towns. Many people preferred to pay fines rather than change their traditional clothing.

The pupil needs to practice both written and oral communication of thoughts. A variety of teaching methods is beneficial for pupil engagement and learning. Daily examination systems should create a sense of responsibility among pupils. Books alone are insufficient for young learners without the guidance of a teacher. As pupils progress, their dependence on teachers decreases. Teachers should assist pupils in becoming independent learners. Teachers can enhance interest in studies by removing obstacles to learning.

Children's faculties of perception and consciousness are immature. Young children often confound different perceptions and sensations. Children's minds are occupied with a blend of sensations, conceptions, fancies, and remembrances. The ability to distinguish between different mental images develops over time through growth and experience. Children must be taught to understand and feel the obligation to speak the truth. Teaching children principles of duty, such as justice and equal rights, is necessary. Children learn through experience, often through the consequences of their actions.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The distinction between faults resulting from evil intentions and those from mental or physical immaturity should be maintained by those in charge of children. Training should be conducted gently regarding all that pertains to the embryo condition of plants, animals, and humans. Children exhibit extraordinary activity when in a state of health. The persistence of force is a fundamental principle stating that no force is ever originated or destroyed, only changed in form. All existing forces are continuations of previous forces and are equivalent in amount. Human mechanisms can only utilize existing forces without increasing or diminishing them. The apparent increase or decrease of force in certain situations is illusive and does not reflect a true change in the amount of force.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The book aims to show how authority can be secured by gentle means. Children must be governed by the authority of their parents. Parents' reason, not children's, should control their actions. Children's immaturity necessitates subjection to parental authority. Parental authority must be established and maintained, even if corporal punishment is required. In some cases, such as among savages or poorly managed schools, physical punishment may be the only means to establish authority. Teaching methods have improved significantly over time, reducing the reliance on violent coercion.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Peter the Great is regarded as the founder of Russian civilization. Peter the Great traveled to Holland to study shipbuilding and worked in a shipyard. The shipyard where Peter studied is located in Saardam, near Amsterdam. The original building of the shipyard is decayed and has been encased in a larger brick structure. The building is a site of annual visits by travelers. Peter the Great's father was Alexis Michaelowitz, who reigned as Emperor of Russia from 1645 to 1676. Alexis Michaelowitz had two marriages and a total of eight children.

A teacher faces multiple excuses from pupils during a recitation. Excuses include missing slates, absence during lesson assignment, erased work, and lack of understanding of the task. The teacher's attention is focused on individual pupils, leading to disorder among the rest of the class. Some pupils engage in disruptive behavior while waiting for their turn with the teacher. In a different classroom management approach, the teacher instructs pupils to wait for their turn to offer excuses. The class is organized into those prepared and unprepared, with commands given to manage the recitation effectively. The teacher can identify errors and ensure correct answers by comparing responses from the majority of the class.

The mother feels dejected because she cannot evoke gratitude and consideration from her child. The child currently exhibits a form of love that is typical for his young age. As the child matures, he will change his behavior towards his mother, becoming less dependent on her. In the future, the child will think of his mother's comfort and happiness and will provide her with attention and gifts. The development of emotional faculties in humans occurs in a sequence that aligns with their needs. Unlike lower animals, humans have a natural desire to repay their parents for the care received during childhood. Lower animals do not exhibit a tendency to return to their parents after reaching maturity.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The preceptor of an academy addressed a conflict between two boys regarding a nail for hanging hats. The teacher suggested postponing the discussion until the next day to allow the boys to calm down. The boys agreed to wait until the next day to resolve their disagreement. The teacher recounted the incident to the school without naming the boys or assigning blame. The teacher emphasized the need to prevent similar conflicts by ensuring each boy has a designated nail for his hat. The teacher proposed forming two committees to assess the number of nails available and the number of students present.

A child studying Geography, History, or Natural Science is learning facts and gaining information. A child learning to write, read, or calculate is acquiring skill, which may help increase knowledge in the future. The three fundamental branches of education are reading, writing, and calculating, which are considered first in importance. The primary objective of common schools in the country is to teach the population to read, write, and calculate. The amount of knowledge acquired at schools is generally considered to be very small. Teachers should assess their pupils' abilities in reading, writing, and calculating at the beginning of the school year. Teachers are encouraged to focus on improving the skills of the entire class in the fundamental branches rather than concentrating on advanced studies with a few students.

The teacher encourages children to engage with literary inquiries to foster interest in the Bible. The teacher aims to promote positive emotions during calm and pleasant school afternoons. The teacher shares a personal story about visiting a sick young woman in a remote area. The young woman is suffering from consumption and is described as calm and happy despite her illness. The young woman expresses her Christian faith and feels the presence of God, which brings her peace and happiness. The teacher reflects on his initial pity for the sick woman, which changes after the visit. The teacher advises against following up impactful stories with exhortations, as children respond better to emotional connections.

It is suggested that showing the consequences of wrongdoing to pupils should be seldom used. Children can be easily led to see the pleasures of doing right. Public punishment of faults may not be necessary if the fault is acknowledged publicly and handled privately afterward. Frequent public reprimands can lead to unpleasant associations with school management and may encourage wrongdoing. Severe reproaches in front of a class can punish the entire class, especially affecting good students more than the one being reprimanded. Disciplinary cases should be approached with caution and only when public opinion is likely to support the teacher. Individual cases can be addressed effectively by seizing specific emergencies that arise during school administration.

The teacher's approach to discipline significantly affects the impression made on pupils. The first duty of a teacher is to avoid making an unfavorable first impression on students. A personal anecdote illustrates the lasting impact of a teacher's initial greeting on students. Teachers should greet their pupils with a genuine smile to foster a positive relationship. Teachers should not focus solely on individual instances of misbehavior but consider the broader context of their pupils' moral development. Addressing a pupil's misconduct should involve a more comprehensive approach than simply punishing the behavior.

Peter was characterized by impatience and a lack of moderation in his actions. Peter oversaw the construction of a new city, which resulted in significant suffering and loss of life. He acted as chief engineer, planning fortifications and laying out streets for the city. A large number of mechanics and artisans built approximately thirty thousand structures in one year. The buildings constructed were often rudimentary and hastily made to provide basic shelter. During Peter's city-building efforts, the King of Sweden was engaged in a war in Poland against Russian and Polish forces. Peter took precautions to protect the city from potential threats posed by the King of Sweden.

A boy takes another boy's place to spoil his work, knowing he is breaking school rules. The boy feels delight in the thought of his schoolmate's disappointment. Another boy in the second desk writes carefully to please God and fulfill his duty. The motive of effort for the second boy is love for God, though he does not constantly think of Him. The speaker emphasizes that character depends on the spirit and motive behind actions. The speaker advises caution in using religious sanctions for school discipline. Religious truths should be presented when students are calm and not during moments of discipline.

Siberia has a cold climate that limits agricultural cultivation due to long winters and short summers. The cold climate of Siberia supports a variety of fur-bearing animals, including sable, mink, ermine, and otter. Inhabitants of Siberia primarily engage in hunting animals for their fur and flesh, as well as mining. Criminals have historically been sent to Siberia for banishment, where they are forced to work in harsh conditions. Peter the Great sought to improve communication and mining operations in Siberia while focusing on European advancements. Holland was a major center for ship-building and maritime commerce during Peter's time. Peter developed an interest in naval power after discussing ship-building with Le Fort, despite Russia's lack of sea-ports and ship-building expertise.

The officers discovered a strong box buried in a vault containing a large sum of money and four hundred vessels of silver. All discovered treasures were confiscated and the proceeds were placed into the imperial treasury. Thekelavitaw, the commander-in-chief of the Guards, was executed by beheading. The subordinate officer in charge of the detachment to Obrogensko was punished severely and sent to Siberia in perpetual banishment. Princess Sophia was ordered to retire to a convent for her protection and to prevent public disgrace. Peter made a grand entry into Moscow with an armed escort of eighteen thousand Guards and was greeted by his brother John. Sophia remained a prisoner for fifteen years, during which attempts to restore her to power were unsuccessful.

The chapter discusses questions children ask about external nature and religious subjects. Children's inquiries about religious and moral subjects often stem from misconceptions about spiritual matters. Errors in teaching and children's cognitive immaturity contribute to their misunderstandings of spiritual concepts. Frequent conversations between a mother and her child can enhance the child's learning and development. A child's early education can benefit from a supportive and engaged mother, leading to better academic performance later. The management of money is important in cultivating sound judgment and practical wisdom in children. A lack of a systematic approach to providing money can hinder a child's understanding of its proper use and the development of financial responsibility.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Individuals seek general information through books, newspapers, periodicals, and conversations. Reading induces care and attention, leading to better discrimination in selecting useful facts. Students in the school engaged in singing during recess and proposed to include it in devotional exercises. The initial attempt at singing in school was met with limited success, but subsequent attempts improved. A systematic plan for regular singing was adopted, including the appointment of a chorister and assistants. The term 'Tabu' signifies something that is consecrated and not to be touched or violated in Sandwich Islander culture. A flower labeled 'Tabu' was used as an example to teach students about handling delicate items.

Joseph displayed embarrassment and confusion when confronted about his club. The other boys responded affirmatively when asked if the club was for self-defense. Joseph was encouraged to throw the club away to avoid punishment and maintain friendship. The act of throwing the club was influenced by a good-natured boy's suggestion. Public ridicule or disgrace can have lasting negative effects on a child's character. Teachers should avoid publicly exposing students who misbehave to protect their reputation. Shame can be an effective remedy for certain juvenile faults in specific cases.

Sounds formed by speech can represent either realities or fancies. The phrase 'I see a bird' can denote a conception in the mind or an outward actuality. The necessity for words to correspond with actual realities arises from social relations. Children do not have an instinct or intuition to perceive the necessity of correspondence between words and realities. A mother tells a story to her son, which amuses him and awakens vivid images in his mind. The boy understands that the story told by his mother is not true and consists only of words meant to give him pleasure. The boy hesitates to share his cake with his sister but ultimately decides to keep it for himself.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The exercises of the school should commence with an act of religious worship every day. There are very few districts where parents would object to this practice. Teachers should not introduce religious practices if they believe it contradicts the wishes of their employers. The practice of daily prayer is expected to have a powerful influence on the moral condition of the school. Devotional services must be honest, heartfelt, and simple to be effective. The teacher has a duty to adopt daily prayer due to the influence they have on shaping children's character. The responsibility of guiding children's moral development is significant for teachers.

The authority of a parent is a duty that requires careful consideration and adaptation of methods. Some parents may initially consider rewarding obedience and punishing disobedience as the only methods to teach submission. Mary, a seventeen-year-old, observed her sister's children, Adolphus and Lucia, were ungoverned. Their mother used coaxing and advising but did not command, leading to the children's disobedience. Mary decided to teach the children obedience by involving them in a task of gathering flowers. Mary provided specific instructions to the children while they gathered flowers and arranged them. Mary aimed to form the habit of obedience in the children through numerous and detailed commands.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: A good text-book should be adapted to scholars rather than teachers. Teachers should evaluate the success of new plans based on their intrinsic superiority rather than novelty. Teachers are advised to maintain established educational practices while exercising creativity within those limits. Keeping a journal of teaching plans and experiments is recommended for teachers. Teachers can share their experiences through periodicals, newspapers, and teacher meetings. Teacher meetings should focus on practical experiences rather than formal speeches. The rights of the Committee, Trustees, or Patrons regarding control of the school should be acknowledged in relation to teachers' new plans.

Teachers should evaluate whether their text-book is superior for general use before publishing. Many authors believe their manuscript text-books are better for general circulation than they actually are. Authors often create text-books based on their unique instructional methods, which may not appeal to a wider audience. A significant number of school-books fail to gain general attention and circulation after publication. The preparation of good school-books is encouraged, but the proliferation of poorly executed works is discouraged. Authors should thoroughly examine existing text-books and ensure their work offers significant improvements before proceeding. The success of a new text-book may depend on the character of the teachers who will use it.

The teacher can foster personal attachment by seeking assistance from pupils and expressing gratitude for their help. Boys and girls enjoy having their abilities recognized and contributing to useful tasks. Cooperation with the teacher can lead to a more positive attitude among students compared to opposition. Teachers should take an interest in students' activities and recognize their skills to build rapport. Maintaining respect is essential for authority, but teachers can still be familiar and approachable. Deliberate wrongdoing may still occur despite efforts to build personal influence. In cases of misconduct, teachers should calmly assess the situation and discuss it directly with the student involved.

A child may develop a habit of leaving the door open. Occasional scolding and temporary confinement may not effectively correct this behavior. An automaton figure could provide consistent reminders to shut the door, leading to quicker behavior modification. A mother can implement similar principles of consistency in her approach to discipline when she is present. Punishments should avoid irritation and anger to prevent the development of an irritable temperament in the child. Parents can encourage cooperation from the child in addressing their faults to make the punishment more effective. An example is given of a child named Egbert, who was incentivized to devise a plan to improve his punctuality in dressing.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The management system discussed tends to foster bad qualities rather than good ones in children. This system encourages children to gain money through sycophancy or persistence rather than through honorable means. The effects of this system can be modified by other influences on the child's mind and character. Teaching children proper money management is important regardless of their future financial situation. A fixed and definite income for children can help them learn responsibility in managing money. Parents may object to a regular allowance system because it may lead children to view it as a debt rather than a gift. The proposed plan does not prevent parents from giving additional gifts of money to their children.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The teacher will obtain a memorandum of the usual order of exercises for the classes. The teacher will set all pupils at work preparing for the lessons of the next day. The teacher will need to pay special attention to individual cases such as new scholars and small children. The teacher will watch for opportunities to combine classes or alter recitation times. The teacher will focus on observing the characters of the boys to identify those likely to be troublesome. The teacher may allow students to have their own way initially to identify idle and mischievous individuals. The teacher should note the names and characters of students who are likely to cause trouble.

In matters of essential importance, a parent is to decide independently and announce their decision without justification. In non-essential matters, parents are to allow children the greatest possible freedom of action. Children are required to obey commands the first time they are given, without question. Parents must maintain a calm, quiet, gentle, and firm approach to parenting. The curiosity of children should not be censured and must be encouraged. Children's questions arise from their natural curiosity about the world around them. Parents and caregivers should utilize children's questions as opportunities for engagement and learning.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Pupils are requested to sit based on the number of times they have whispered. The teacher may ask pupils to rise again to determine when they spoke more during the forenoon. The inquiries aim to help pupils provide honest accounts of their behavior. The teacher encourages a pleasant atmosphere for reporting, framing it as a voluntary experiment. The teacher expresses confidence in the honesty of the majority of reports from the pupils. The teacher acknowledges that some reports may not be entirely honest but emphasizes the value of honesty. The process of reducing whispering in the classroom may take weeks and will not achieve complete elimination.

Children may struggle to distinguish between semblance and reality in complex logical ideas. Many individuals are unable to differentiate between sound arguments and those that are nonsensical. Instruction is necessary for children to correct false reasoning rather than ridicule or punishment. Explaining a child's mistake immediately after it occurs may lead to defensiveness and hinder understanding. A more effective approach is to provide instruction at a later time when the child is more receptive. A story about two boys, Jack and Henry, illustrates the concept of boasting and the importance of honesty in self-assessment. The story reveals that Jack falsely claimed to be a good scholar, while Henry, who was actually the better student, was honest about his position.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: A teacher should conduct a thorough survey of the school to elevate the overall knowledge of students. The teacher must consider the existing state of knowledge and character of the students. It is important for the teacher to understand the future stations and conditions of the students. Teachers should ascertain the educational stage of each individual student without formal examinations. The management of schools should focus on how to effectively teach groups of students rather than just individuals. A teacher can significantly increase their effectiveness by addressing large numbers of students simultaneously. It is possible for a teacher to effectively instruct up to three hundred students at once if they are attentive and eager to learn.

Parents can assist children in learning the truth through appropriate instruction. Mothers should not be overly distressed by their children's early deviations from the truth. Punishment for deviations from truth in young children should not be stern or severe. Instruction is preferred over expressions of anger when addressing children's dishonesty. Encouragement and approval for truthfulness are more effective than punishment for dishonesty. There is a distinction between deceitfulness by actions and falsehood by words. The spoken word is considered more sacred and reprehensible to violate than other forms of deception.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Peter aimed to make his army efficient and independent from the people to maintain control. Peter's measures strengthened his power and established it on a firm basis. The Church and leading ecclesiastics opposed Peter during the late rebellion due to their vested interests. The Patriarch of the Russian Church held significant power and was similar in status to the Pope of Rome. The Patriarch was considered the spiritual sovereign of Russia and received homage from Peter during religious ceremonies. During religious anniversaries, the Patriarch rode on horseback while Peter held the bridle, symbolizing the Patriarch's elevated status. Peter sought to bring the Russian Church under his control, as it had been largely independent prior to his reign.

Zeal can lead to temporary success in various endeavors. New plans of instruction or government may be based on good principles taken to extremes. Significant ingenuity and labor have been wasted on educational attempts that could have improved existing institutions. Advancements in education should be made through the industry and fidelity of those involved, with gradual changes. Young teachers should thoroughly examine the current public and private school systems in New England to understand their strengths. Teachers should assess their own experience and standing before proposing new educational plans. The Fellenberg school at Hofwyl has had successful direct results, but many imitations have failed, wasting resources.

The battle of Pultowa was a significant conflict between the King of Sweden and Czar Peter of Russia. Pultowa is located in the heart of Russian territories, approximately three to four hundred miles north of the Black Sea. The town of Pultowa was an important military station with arsenals containing food and ammunition for Peter's army. The King of Sweden aimed to capture Pultowa to supply his army with provisions. General Menzikoff commanded the largest body of Russian forces near Pultowa and sought to relieve the town during the siege. The King of Sweden was wounded in the heel during the siege and had to give orders from his tent. The King of Sweden faced the threat of being surrounded by Peter's advancing army while he was incapacitated.

Influence can be exerted on other educational institutions by aligning with established organizations. Success in an academy or private school can elevate the standard of academic instruction. Professors Cleaveland and Silliman contributed to education by enhancing existing institutions rather than creating new ones. The introduction of new studies in schools should be carefully considered in relation to the institution's primary objectives. Education is a shared responsibility between teachers and parents, with schools focusing on specific educational goals. The complexity of school curricula should be managed to ensure that essential educational objectives are not compromised. Public schools should prioritize teaching fundamental skills such as reading, writing, and arithmetic.

A portion of the force derived from food is expended in actions of the brain and nervous system. The processes of vegetable and animal life involve the reception and storage of force from the sun. The operations of nature are complex and not fully understood. Parents and teachers can modify their actions by understanding the general principle of children's activity. Children should not be reprimanded for their natural restlessness and activity after eating. Encouraging children's activity should focus on promoting physical development and health. Young animals require changes of action or alternations of action and repose due to their developing organs.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The teacher addressed the boys about the use of profane language in a calm and temperate manner. The teacher asked the boys if they wished to abandon the habit of using profane language. All but one boy rose to acknowledge their use of profane language. Only three boys out of approximately twenty claimed they never used profane language. The teacher emphasized that merely resolving to reform would not be sufficient to overcome the habit. The teacher planned to propose methods to help the boys keep their resolutions the following day. The boys adopted the proposed plans, leading to a significant reduction of profaneness in the school.

A child grasps an object by the middle and pulls against another person until they gain control of it. Teasing in children can be encouraged by allowing them to win a discussion after initial resistance. Preventing teasing can be achieved by listening to children's requests before making a decision. When considering children's requests, a mother should assess if there is any harm or danger involved. If there are no serious risks, a mother should consent to children's requests after hearing their arguments. In a scenario, two boys, William and James, propose to dig a fish-pond, but their mother initially denies the request. The mother eventually consents to the boys' plan after they address her objections.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The method described aims to reduce confusion and perplexity for teachers. The author emphasizes the importance of having a plan to minimize interruptions in the classroom. Mending pens is identified as a source of interruption that should be managed with a specific time assigned for it. Students should learn to write with various types of pens rather than focusing solely on having perfect pens. Teachers are advised to minimize the time spent on pen-related issues to avoid disruptions in class. A suggested solution is for teachers to appoint older students to mend pens, relieving the teacher of this task. Teachers should implement a system for answering student questions to manage time and maintain order.

Hannah put on her bonnet and set off towards the gate. Hannah's mother insisted that she must not go and did not want Sarah to accompany them. Hannah disobeyed her mother and ran off to find Sarah, but returned saying Sarah was not at home. Hannah's mother expressed disapproval of Hannah's running around and warned her about getting tired. Hannah continued to run about and ignored her mother's commands. Hannah approached a tree where her mother warned her about a wasps' nest. Hannah gathered flowers at the foot of the tree despite her mother's warnings.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Peter was eighteen years old at the time of his marriage. Peter's father, Alexis, died when Peter was nine years old. General Menesius, a Scotchman, was appointed to oversee Peter's education. Peter was five years old when he began his education under General Menesius. Peter was favored by those connected to his mother's family but faced jealousy from those related to his father's first wife. After Alexis's death, the division between the two branches of the family intensified. Sophia sought to undermine Peter's potential by attempting to spoil him with indulgence.

The teacher discusses different motives for actions among boys. The first motive mentioned is love of money. The second motive discussed is friendship. The third motive is love of honor. The fourth motive is fear. A fifth motive introduced is benevolence. The sixth motive is emulation.

Promised rewards and threatened punishments should be used cautiously in promoting early piety. Genuine piety must rest on different foundations than hope of future reward or fear of future punishment. True gratitude to God should be based on past kindness rather than the expectation of future benefits. The highest condition of human nature is marked by maintaining right moral and spiritual relations with God and man. Motives of hope and fear should be kept in the background when dealing with children in religious contexts. In cases of illness, warnings about danger may hinder the awakening of positive feelings towards God. Feelings of gratitude, penitence, and trust should be encouraged in children facing death.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Parents should not rely on arguing or reasoning with children as a substitute for authority. It is beneficial for children to make decisions when appropriate, but parents should genuinely allow them to decide. Parents should announce their own decisions when they have already determined a course of action. Children find it easier to obey a parent's decision than to agree with it after considering reasons. In serious cases, such as going to school or taking medicine, parents should make decisions for their children. Parents should avoid giving reasons that may lead children to feel they have a choice when they do not. When a child refuses to take medicine, parents should administer it without delay and without showing displeasure.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The teacher observed a difficulty with a boy named James regarding his behavior during prayer time. The teacher decided to cultivate a personal relationship with James to gain influence over him. The teacher invited James to walk home with him to discuss a fault privately. James acknowledged that he preferred to discuss the issue outside of school. The teacher addressed James's disorderly conduct in a mild and non-reproachful manner. The teacher emphasized that the behavior was a significant issue that needed to be corrected. James admitted that he had not improved his behavior as much as expected since the teacher's previous remarks.

The narrator attended a school for two quarters. The old school-house has been replaced by a large brick house. The narrator expresses a lasting memory of their teacher. The text discusses the influence of prejudice on judgment. Several subjects are suggested for writing exercises in school. The subjects include duties to parents, selfishness, faults of the school, excellences of the school, and the Sabbath. An anonymous writing method for teachers and pupils is proposed.

Mary is described as a child who disobeys her aunt, Jane. The text suggests that immediate action by parents is more effective than scolding or threatening. Punishments should be seen as remedies rather than retribution. The author argues that gentle methods of discipline require more time and care than physical punishment. The effectiveness of punishment lies in its certainty rather than its severity. Children can learn from minor consequences rather than severe ones. The text emphasizes that penalties should aim for safety and happiness in the future.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Louisa expressed a desire to always tell the truth after a conversation with her mother. Louisa's mother reminded her that she did not tell the truth about an apple given to her by Bridget. Louisa promised her mother that she would never tell another wrong story. The text discusses the effectiveness of gentle measures in child-rearing. The establishment of parental authority is emphasized as a crucial duty for mothers. Many mothers do not recognize their duty to establish authority over their children. The text argues that reason and reflection develop slowly in children and cannot be relied upon in early years.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The mingling of real and imaginary worlds in children is observed in various ways. Embryo faculties in children are activated by a vital force in an irregular manner. Mental organs in the brain develop through exercise, similar to muscles. Parents should encourage the exercise of their children's embryo powers. The imagination can enhance the attractiveness and effectiveness of lessons. Mothers can engage children's imagination by holding conversations with representations in pictures. Imaginary conversations with pictures can stimulate children's interest and enjoyment.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The mental faculties of children related to judgment and reasoning are not fully developed in the early years of life. Parents should not impose serious tests or burdens on children's judgment but should rely on their own authority. Parents can promote the healthy development of children's faculties by explaining less obvious relations of various acts and occurrences. Discussions with children should be conducted in a calm and considerate manner, acknowledging their views while presenting additional perspectives. The development of children's thinking and reasoning powers should be gradual and aligned with their maturity level. Parents should encourage children to engage in reasoning tasks without taking over the process themselves. General rules regarding children's wishes and requests align with the principles of judgment and reasoning discussed.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Modern cities have complete fire extinguishing arrangements, leading to a lack of concern among residents during fire alarms. The conspirators planned to release Sophia from imprisonment and proclaim her queen after the death of the Czar. The plot was scheduled for execution on February 2, 1697, but was thwarted by two officers who confessed to the Czar. The Czar arrested the conspirators immediately after receiving the confession and ordered them to be tortured for further information. Most of the conspirators were condemned to death after a brief trial, and the execution was carried out in a brutal manner. The executed criminals' remains were displayed on a column in Moscow until the spring, when they were disposed of in a pit. Peter the Great undertook a tour in 1697, traveling incognito and engaging in diplomatic activities with various cities.

Peter the Great took command of a vessel and assumed the title of captain at the age of twenty-two. Peter declared war against the Turks and Tartars with the objective of capturing the city of Azof. Peter invested the city of Azof by land and took possession of the river leading to it using boats and vessels he built. An artillery officer betrayed the Russian army by sabotaging the guns and informing the Turks, leading to the loss of the battery. The Russian army was forced to raise the siege of Azof due to the betrayal and the subsequent defeat. In the following year, Peter renewed the attempt to capture Azof and achieved his first naval victory by overpowering the Turkish fleet. The treacherous artilleryman was captured and executed in Moscow as a condition of the surrender of Azof.

The government of Amsterdam prepared a grand reception for the Russian embassy and set aside a house for the Czar's use during his stay. Peter the Great chose not to occupy the palace and instead stayed in a quiet lodging near the shipping area. Peter made arrangements to visit the ship-yards of the Dutch East India Company in Saardam to study ship construction. Peter enrolled as a common ship-carpenter under the name Peter Michaelhoff and worked among the company's laborers. He spent several months in the ship-yards, dedicating most of his days to work and sailing in various boats. Peter's interest in ship-building and navigation was driven by personal enjoyment rather than a serious intention to become a ship-carpenter. Historians note that while Peter engaged in ship-building activities, he likely did not perform significant manual labor.

Peter planned to construct a large fortress on the shores of an island to command the channel leading up the bay. The fortress was to be built on a sandbank and was designed to be surrounded by shallow water. Peter laid the foundations of the fortress on the ice using timber boxes filled with stones. The fortress, known as the Castle of Cronstadt, was built to keep European navies at bay during wartime. The King of Sweden ordered an attack on Peter's settlement but found the works too advanced and strong. On July 4, 1704, the Swedish fleet attempted to land troops on the island but was repelled by Russian forces. The Swedish fleet's attempt to attack resulted in many casualties and the capture of five of their boats by the Russians.

Sophia attempted to persuade General Menesius to adopt a system of laxity and indulgence for his pupil, Peter. General Menesius aimed to make Peter a virtuous and accomplished man and opposed Sophia's plans. Sophia maneuvered to have General Menesius dismissed from his position to implement her own management of Peter. After Menesius's dismissal, Sophia established a new household for Peter with fifty boys as playmates and minimal restraint. Sophia's intention was for Peter and the boys to grow up idle and vicious, potentially harming Peter's health. Peter resisted the temptations of idleness and vice, instead using his privileges for self-improvement. He organized the boys into a military school, learned drumming, studied fortification, and worked on practical skills.

A powerful party formed in opposition to the foreign influences introduced by Peter. Princess Sophia was the only potential leader for the opposition party. The Czar John, Peter's brother, was deceased, which limited the opposition's rallying options. The opposition communicated with Princess Sophia, who was closely guarded in a convent. The opposition argued against Peter's policies by highlighting heavy taxes and loss of influence for the nobility. They also appealed to the poor by claiming Peter's actions violated religious customs and laws. The opposition planned to assassinate Peter by setting fire to houses near the royal palace.

Louisa's mother gave her an additional apple despite feeling suspicious. Louisa's mother did not express her suspicions after learning the facts. Louisa's mother engaged with her daughter in a playful manner before bed. Louisa is four years old, while the character Ernest in the story is five. Ernest and his cousin Anna went to their uncle's garden hoping for apples. Ernest and Anna found two apples under the tree and ate them. Ernest chose to tell the truth to their uncle instead of lying about the apples.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The text discusses a plan for the regular division of time in a common school. The proposed plan includes specific time slots for subjects such as Reading, Writing, Arithmetic, Grammar, and Geography. A diagram should be created by older scholars to display the schedule, with class names inserted in the appropriate columns. A bell should be rung five minutes before each half hour ends and again at the end to signal transitions between classes. Recesses are marked by the letter R, and periods for General exercise are marked by G, allowing time for the teacher to address the whole school. The text suggests that children appreciate system and regularity in school arrangements. The author notes that some subjects, like Punctuation and Spelling, can be effectively taught to the whole school at designated times.

Latin was taught to boys in the past through physical punishment. There has been a significant change in teaching methods over time. Teachers now rely on tact, knowledge, and skill rather than physical force. Some teachers may still resort to physical punishment due to a lack of understanding and skill. Neglect and mismanagement by parents can lead to rudeness and insubordination in children. In cases of parental neglect, physical punishment may be seen as a last resort for discipline. Parents who train their children using modern principles can achieve authority without physical punishment.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The dolls are named Bella and Araminta, and their mothers are Lucy and Mary. The young lady engages in an imaginary conversation with the dolls to capture the children's attention. The children are asked to identify their dolls' names and mothers, reinforcing the illusion of the dolls as living beings. The young lady uses the dolls to convey moral lessons about quarrelling, which the children find more engaging than direct admonitions. The teacher's approach associates lessons with amusement, reducing the likelihood of resentment from the children. The teacher emphasizes the importance of setting a good example for children, as they tend to imitate their mothers' behavior. The method of using play to convey lessons is suggested to be more effective in influencing children's behavior.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The embassy consisted of about three hundred men. The principal members of the embassy were well-mounted and equipped. The first significant stop of the embassy was in the city of Riga, which was then part of Sweden. The governor of Riga received the embassy politely but denied them access to the fortifications. Peter was disappointed by the governor's refusal and planned to confront the King of Sweden upon his return. The embassy then traveled to the city of Konigsberg, the capital of the King of Prussia. The reception in Konigsberg included a procession with various displays of pomp and honor.

Teachers have different views on the misconduct of their pupils. Some teachers are surprised and irritated by student misconduct, while others expect it. Teachers who expect misconduct are better prepared to handle it. A teacher's understanding of their students affects their approach to teaching. Teachers often overlook the importance of understanding the nature of their students. Mismanagement of expectations can lead to frustration for teachers. Two teachers can manage their schools in completely different ways.

The parent is responsible for the guidance given to their children. Interference in parental duties is not justified without consent, except when children's safety is at risk. The community has the right to require parents to provide for the instruction of their children. Teachers must operate within the specific duties defined by their employers' consent. In a republican country, teachers may discuss principles of free governments with their students. Teachers must avoid influencing students on religious matters unless there is common ground with their employers. The community generally agrees on the existence of God.

The text discusses the importance of understanding individuals and securing personal attachments in educational settings. It outlines the limits and restrictions of religious influence in schools, emphasizing the need for common consent among employers. The text describes the structure and organization of the Mt. Vernon School, including daily exercises and the roles of officers. It addresses the significance of ingenuity and enterprise in educational planning while cautioning against fruitless schemes. The text includes a chapter on reports of cases, detailing various classroom management issues and their resolutions. It highlights the contrasting opinions on the pleasantness of teaching, noting that some teachers view it as drudgery while others find joy in it.

The relationship between employer and employee involves a division of rights and responsibilities. Teachers often perceive their classrooms as their own domain, resisting employer interference. Employers may hesitate to intervene in school matters due to the sensitivity of teachers. Teachers may feel resentment towards employers when they attempt to assert their rights. Employers retain the ultimate decision-making power regarding the work being done. Teachers are obligated to comply with the wishes of their employers while employed. The obligation of teachers to follow employer directives is based on the employers' rights, not their superior knowledge.

Johnny learns that the sun makes the rainbow. Johnny's mother explains that the sun shines on the cloud to create the rainbow. Johnny observes that the cloud is opposite to the sun and is exposed to its beams. Johnny's mother describes that the sun shines on drops of rain in the cloud, creating colors that form the rainbow. The mother aims to provide short and simple answers to Johnny's questions. The mother believes that answers should communicate minimal information to the child. The mother compares providing information to a child to administering small portions of food.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: There are atmospheric conditions that will likely result in a violent storm within a few hours. The captain's topmasts and upper rigging were carried away by the gale. The owners do not blame the captain for the loss if he lacked sufficient meteorological knowledge before leaving port. Children are often held responsible for knowledge of dangers that adults have acquired through experience. A recent accident involved workmen constructing a tunnel who accidentally caused an explosion due to unforeseen circumstances. The explosion in the tunnel resulted from electric force from a thunder-cloud igniting charges prepared for blasting. Learning to read and spell presents significant challenges for children, which are often not appreciated by adults.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The empress gave birth to a son three years after her marriage to Peter. Peter had one son from his first wife, known as the Czarewitz. The birth of Catharine's son was politically significant due to Peter's difficulties with his eldest son. The birth was celebrated with public rejoicings that lasted for eight days. Two kings, from Denmark and Prussia, acted as godfathers at the baptism of the child named Peter Petrowitz. Catharine had a strong influence over Peter, calming him during his fits of irritation. Catharine used her influence to rescue many from Peter's displeasure and soften his character.

The teacher conducts an arithmetic recitation with the class, focusing on addition. Students are asked to rise after completing an addition example, revealing varying speeds in their responses. The teacher observes and notes the time taken by students to complete the addition task. The teacher identifies that differences in speed are primarily due to the methods used by students rather than skill level. The teacher describes three methods of adding numbers: counting, calculating, and specific techniques within those methods. The counting method includes using fingers, mental counting in sets of two, and adding by threes. The calculating method involves techniques such as doubling numbers, skipping to add easier numbers, and adjusting numbers to simplify addition.

The Emperor of Russia was concealed in a disguise during the procession. The military escort for the embassadors included a band of music, foot-guards in green uniforms armed with silver battle-axes, and a troop of horsemen. The grand state carriage of the embassy followed the military escort, carrying the three embassadors. The procession was attended by a large crowd of citizens who lined the streets to witness the event. The embassadors were conducted to a palace in the city, where a garrison was drawn up at the gates to receive them. Twenty-four soldiers were stationed as sentinels to guard the doors and halls of the embassadors' apartments. The embassadors presented a letter from the Czar and valuable gifts to the king during their public audience.

The death of Alexis's father would allow him to succeed to the throne and change the current situation. Many individuals supported Alexis in opposing his father, Peter, due to their opposition to Peter's reforms. The old Muscovite party opposed Peter's changes and rallied around Alexis as a potential leader. Disaffected parties in a monarchy often seek to find a royal family member to lead their opposition. Rumors suggested that some members of the old Muscovite party were conspiring to depose Peter and elevate Alexis. Peter was aware of the conspiracies against him and felt increased anxiety regarding Alexis's actions. Alexis expressed a desire to enter monastic life, which Peter initially interpreted as a threat rather than a genuine intention.

A mother and her daughter hear a bird singing and discuss giving it crumbs as a gesture of gratitude. The mother suggests that the bird's song may come from joy in seeing them. The child expresses a desire to give crumbs to the bird, which fosters a sentiment of gratitude. The interaction is described as suitable for young children to cultivate feelings of gratitude. For older children, the approach to teaching gratitude must be adapted to their maturity. Robert, a twelve-year-old, reflects on his sister Mary's kindness during his illness. Robert's mother suggests he make a garden for Mary as a way to show gratitude for her care.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Dikes and levees were needed to protect land from river inundations. An immense number of laborers, estimated at three hundred thousand, were assembled for construction work. The supply of implements such as pickaxes and shovels was limited, leading workers to use alternative methods to transport earth. The Swedes had control of the Baltic Sea, complicating the supply of provisions which had to be brought by water. Shortages of food led to distress among the laborers, resulting in sickness and death, with an estimated one hundred thousand men perishing. The emperor sent requisitions for more food, but the number of laborers increased faster than the food supply. The labor supply was maintained despite high mortality rates, as serfs were compelled to work under the orders of nobles and governors.

A person may leave written articles for others to read, nominating the reader on the article itself. The practice of leaving articles can positively influence pupils and contribute to good discipline and character formation in school. Teachers can use this method to present suggestions more effectively than through traditional means. The practice resembles a newspaper, where opinions are evaluated based on their merits rather than the author's authority. The author has experienced significant effects from this practice in their own school, including anonymous communication from pupils. Discussions and criticisms regarding school management and faults have occurred as a result of this practice. The teacher retains editorial powers to comment on, alter, or suppress the written articles.

Monsieur and Madame Croquemitaine are fictional characters that are said to carry off bad children. Mothers sometimes threaten their children with the 'black man' or 'policeman' to manage behavior. Exciting imaginary fears can produce violent effects on a child's brain, leading to agitation and terror. Harsh reproofs and threats can disturb a child's nervous system and lead to anxiety and distress. The effects of stern rebukes may cause a child to seek comfort from their mother during times of distress. Gentle methods of discipline are recommended as a preferable alternative to harsh treatment.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: The comfort and enjoyment of children is promoted by making decisions for them when necessary. Parents should not engage in arguments with children over decisions that are ultimately not in their best interest. Children's reasoning powers can be developed by allowing them to make decisions in safe situations. Parents should provide information to children without interfering with their judgment. As children grow older, they can be entrusted with more responsibilities, such as managing minor arrangements during travel. In important cases involving a child's feelings, parents should rely on their own authority rather than the child's judgment. In unimportant cases, parents should allow children to exercise their judgment and take responsibility.

source.author: Jacob Abbott
source.title: Gentle Measures in the Management and Training of the Young

text: Charles expressed willingness to make peace with Peter on previously proposed terms. A portion of Charles's army remained safe after the battle of Pultowa. Charles had a force of one or two thousand men who escaped from the battle. Peter rejected Charles's peace proposal, stating it was too late. Charles's officers decided it was futile to continue resistance. Charles was transported to the Turkish frontier in a carriage due to his illness. The remaining soldiers faced hardships during their retreat, suffering from lack of food and exhaustion.

The institution should not be fully surrendered to the pupils. Plans for self-government in educational institutions have often been abandoned. Anarchy in a college or academy may be viewed positively by students. Involving students in school administration can lead to benefits for both students and teachers. Teachers must prepare students gradually for responsibilities and power. Teachers can delegate simple tasks to students to foster cooperation and interest. Selecting popular students for responsibilities can enhance the success of delegated tasks.

The school is divided into six sections based on age and general maturity of mind. Each section is assigned to a Superintendent who also serves as a Teacher during school hours. Superintendents are responsible for preparing a list of section members and becoming acquainted with them. Superintendents oversee the preparation of schedules for their section and ensure they are submitted to parents for feedback. Superintendents ensure that all daily needs of their section members are met, including providing necessary supplies. Superintendents monitor the progress and habits of section members and address any issues with their performance. Superintendents are encouraged to discuss moral and religious duties during section meetings.

The text discusses the concept of God's forgiveness and the importance of recognizing wrongdoing, even in small actions. A blank schedule is provided to students upon entering the school, which outlines their daily activities for a week. The school day begins with a bell ringing five minutes before the start time, followed by another bell one minute prior to signal students to take their seats.
